words.def_en: a person who cannot stop doing or using something, especially something bad
words.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 addictus，ad- 指向，dicere 表示说，原指被判为奴隶，现表示对事物成瘾的人。
example: He is a video game addict who plays for hours every day.
他是一个电子游戏成瘾者，每天都要玩上好几个小时。

words.def_en: unable to stop doing or using something, especially something bad for you
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 addicere，ad- 表示向，dicere 是说，原意是分配或奉献，后来演变为对某物上瘾的状态。
example: He became addicted to playing video games all day.
他沉迷于整天玩电子游戏。

words.def_en: A strong need to keep doing something, even when it causes harm.
words.mnemonic: addiction 源自拉丁语 addictionem，最初意为奴役，词根 addicere 表示分配或沉迷，现在广泛用于药物或行为依赖问题。
example: His addiction to video games made him miss school often.
他对电子游戏上瘾，经常逃学。

words.def_en: Something that makes people want to keep using or doing it. Easily getting hooked on things.
words.mnemonic: addictive 来自拉丁语 addictus，原意是被奴役的状态，现在指事物具有使人上瘾的特性，常见于药物或游戏领域。
example: This game is very addictive because it's so fun to play.
这个游戏非常容易上瘾，因为玩起来太有趣了。

words.def_en: to tell someone what to do, especially in a bossy way to control or decide how something happens to say words for someone else to write down a rule or order that must be followed
words.mnemonic: 词根 dict 来自拉丁语 dicere 意思说，后缀 -ate 表示动作，意为口述命令或指示。
example: You cannot dictate how I should live my life.
你不能规定我该如何生活。

words.def_en: speaking words for someone to write down a test where students write what they hear
words.mnemonic: dictation 源于 dictate，拉丁词源 dictare 意为反复口述，因此指听写过程，常用于语言学习或秘书工作中。
example: The boss gave dictation to her assistant to type the letter.
老板向她的助理口述了要打印的信件。

words.def_en: to say what will happen in the future
words.mnemonic: predict 词根 pre- 表示之前，dict- 表示说，源自拉丁语 praedicere，指预测或预先说出未来事件。
example: I predict it will rain tomorrow.
我预测明天会下雨。

kaoyan_ex.text: You want to predict if something needs attention now and point to where it’s useful for employees to go to.

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“预测”

words.def_en: How well you can know or guess something before it happens. Being just as expected to the point of being boring.
words.mnemonic: predictability 来自 predict 和 ability，predict 源于拉丁语 praedicere 意为预先说出，因此指事物可被预测的特性。
example: The predictability of the weather makes planning outdoor activities easier.
天气的可预测性使户外活动规划更容易。

words.def_en: Able to be known or guessed before it happens Always the same and therefore uninteresting
words.mnemonic: predictable 基于 predict，pre- 表示之前，dicere 是说，因此指事物可以被提前预知或推断。
example: The weather in this region is very predictable during summer months.
这个地区夏季的天气非常可预测。

words.def_en: Something that happens as expected or can be easily guessed Something that happens in a way that is not surprising or interesting
words.mnemonic: 由 predict 加后缀 -able 和 -ly 构成，predict 源于拉丁语 praedicere 指预测，整个副词表示可预见的方式。
example: Predictably, it rained on the day of the picnic.
不出所料，野餐那天下了雨。

words.def_en: a guess about what will happen in the future
words.mnemonic: prediction 源于拉丁语 prae 之前和 dicere 说，组合表示提前说出未来事件。
example: The weather prediction says it will rain tomorrow.
天气预报说明天会下雨。

kaoyan_ex.text: They reimagined the 300-yearold score by injecting the latest climate prediction data for each season— provided by Monash…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“预测”；常见搭配 by

words.def_en: Not able to be known in advance because it changes often or depends on many things. A person whose actions or behavior cannot be guessed beforehand.
words.mnemonic: un- 表示否定，predict 来自拉丁语 praedicere 预言，-able 表示能够，描述无法预测的事物，如天气或事件，强调不确定性。
example: The weather is unpredictable, so always carry an umbrella just in case.
天气变幻莫测，所以随身带把伞以防万一。

words.def_en: helpful and useful, not negative
words.mnemonic: constructive 基于拉丁语 constructivus，由前缀 con-（一起）和词根 struere（建造）组成，表示建设性的或有助于进步的。
example: Her constructive feedback helped me improve my project.
她建设性的反馈帮助我改进了项目。

words.def_en: the act of destroying something or the state of being destroyed
words.mnemonic: destruction 源自拉丁语 destruere，de- 表示 '向下'，struere 表示 '建造'，合起来意为拆毁或彻底破坏。
example: The hurricane caused widespread destruction along the coast, leaving many homes in ruins.
飓风给沿海地区造成了广泛的破坏，许多房屋沦为废墟。

words.def_en: causing damage or breaking things harmful or unhelpful
words.mnemonic: destroy（破坏）的形容词形式，后缀 ive 表示具有某种性质，整体指具有破坏力的或造成损害的。
example: The destructive storm ruined many homes.
破坏性的风暴摧毁了许多房屋。

kaoyan_ex.text: …water, and protecting nearby communities from potentially destructive storm surges.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“破坏性的”

words.def_en: the basic systems and services needed for a country or organization to work properly, like roads, buildings, and utilities
words.mnemonic: infrastructure 由 infra- 前缀表示下方，结合 structure 结构组成，源于法语，指支撑社会运行的基础系统如道路和网络。
example: The government is investing in infrastructure to improve roads, bridges, and public transportation.
政府正在投资基础设施，以改善道路、桥梁和公共交通。

kaoyan_ex.text: …compared to those who must endure the relatively poor infrastructure of the Midlands and the North.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“基础设施”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: to tell someone to do something, especially in a formal way to teach someone how to do something, especially a practical skill to give someone information about something to hire someone to represent you in a legal matter, especially a lawyer
words.mnemonic: 单词 instruct 源于拉丁语 instruere，词根 in- 表示进入，struere 意为建造，整体引申为教导或指导知识构建，常用于教育场景。
example: The manager will instruct the team to complete the project by Friday.
经理将指示团队在周五前完成项目。

words.def_en: helping you learn something useful
words.mnemonic: 由 instruct 教导和后缀 -ive 构成，表示具有教育意义的。教育类 App 或书籍常提供 instructive 内容。
example: The documentary was very instructive in showing how to solve problems creatively.
这部纪录片在展示如何创造性地解决问题方面很有启发性。

kaoyan_ex.text: …in mixedage playgroups, researchers said that western “instructive teaching”, where pupils are asked to sit still, may contribute to conditions such…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“有教育意义的”

words.def_en: a person who teaches a skill or sport a college teacher below assistant professor
words.mnemonic: instructor 来自拉丁语 instruere， in 表示进入， struere 表示建造，整体意为指导者帮助构建知识，常用于教育或培训场景。
example: The instructor showed us how to swim safely.
教练向我们展示了如何安全游泳。

words.def_en: to build something again that was broken or gone to figure out how something happened using clues
words.mnemonic: reconstruct 来自 re- 再和 construct 建造，意为重建损坏的事物，比如考古学中复原历史场景。
example: We will reconstruct the old bridge that fell down.
我们将重建那座倒塌的旧桥。

kaoyan_ex.text: The team reconstructed the animals’ evolutionary tree and used computer models to pinpoint the domestication event when…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“重建”；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: The act of changing or improving how something works or looks. Building something again after it was damaged or destroyed. A copy of something that no longer exists. Acting out past events to understand them better, like a crime. The time after the US Civil War when the South rejoined the US and rights were given to African Americans.
words.mnemonic: 前缀 re- 表示再次，词根 construct 来自拉丁语 construere 意为建造，后缀 -ion 表示过程或结果，合起来指战后或破坏后的重建。
example: The reconstruction of the old bridge made it safer and more modern.
旧桥的重建使其更安全、更现代化。

words.def_en: to change how something is organized or arranged
words.mnemonic: re- 前缀表示重新，structure 指结构，组合意为调整组织框架，常用于商业或机构改革。
example: The company will restructure to become more efficient.
公司将进行重组以提高效率。

words.def_en: relating to how something is built or arranged
words.mnemonic: 单词 structural 源于拉丁语 structura 表示结构，加上后缀 -ural 构成形容词，描述事物具有结构特征或与建筑框架相关。
example: The structural design of the building makes it very strong against earthquakes.
该建筑的结构设计使其具有很强的抗震能力。

words.def_en: An extra item that is useful but not needed, or added for decoration. Something you wear or carry that goes with your clothes, like a bag or jewelry. A person who helps in a crime or hides it from the police. Less important compared to others.
words.mnemonic: accessory 来自拉丁语 accessorius，ad- 表示向，cedere 意为去，指附加物品如配件，或在法律中表示从犯。
example: She bought a phone accessory to protect it.
她买了一个手机配件来保护手机。

words.def_en: a family member who lived long ago an animal from long ago that modern animals came from an early version of something that later became better
words.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 antecessor，ante- 表示之前，cedere 意为去，合起来指先行者或祖先。
example: My ancestor came from another country many years ago.
我的祖先多年前从另一个国家来到这里。

kaoyan_ex.text: …with looking for photographs that show our Victorian ancestors smiling (what better way to shatter the image of 19thcentury prudery?).

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“祖先”

words.def_en: too much of something an amount that is more than needed the amount you pay first in an insurance claim doing too much of something, like eating or drinking bad behavior that goes too far extra or more than needed needing extra payment
words.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 excessus，前缀 ex-（超出）和 cedere（行走），意思是超过正常限度的量，如 excess weight 超重。
example: Too much excess stress can harm your health.
过多的压力会损害你的健康。

kaoyan_ex.text: For women, the association may be attributable to changes in immunity that resulted from excess abdominal fat; in men, the…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“过量”；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: too much or more than needed
words.mnemonic: excessive 由前缀 ex- 表示超出和词根 cess 源于拉丁语 cedere 意为走，加上后缀 -ive，整体指过度或超出正常界限的状态。
example: Excessive use of water during a drought is wasteful.
干旱期间过度用水是浪费。

kaoyan_ex.text: Society also suffers from excessive employment protections.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“过度的”

words.def_en: more than necessary or desirable, or beyond a certain degree
words.mnemonic: 由 excess 加后缀 -ive 和 -ly 构成，excess 源于拉丁语 excessus，表示超出正常限度的程度。
example: He excessively watered the plants, causing them to drown.
他过度浇水，导致植物被淹死。

words.def_en: someone who had your job before you an older version of something that was replaced
words.mnemonic: predecessor 源于拉丁语 praedecessor，prae-（前）和 decessor（离开者）结合，指前任或前辈在职位上的继承关系。
example: The new manager changed many rules set by his predecessor.
新经理改变了他的前任制定的许多规则。

kaoyan_ex.text: …with Generation Z seeking to learn from their millennial predecessors, even if parents and teachers tend to be still set in the degree mindset.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“前任”

words.def_en: A line of people or vehicles moving slowly, often in a ceremony. A series of people or things coming one after another.
words.mnemonic: procession 源于 process，其中 pro- 表示向前，cess 来自拉丁语 cedere 意为走，因此描述有序行进的行列或仪式。
example: The wedding procession walked slowly down the street.
婚礼队伍沿着街道缓缓行进。

words.def_en: a machine or person that prepares or changes things the main part of a computer that does calculations and controls everything
words.mnemonic: processor 来自 process（处理），后缀 -or 表示执行者，在计算领域特指中央处理器 CPU，是计算机的核心组件。
example: The food processor helps chop vegetables quickly.
食品加工机有助于快速切碎蔬菜。

words.def_en: A series of people or things that come one after another. The regular pattern of one thing following another. Taking over a position or title; the right to become the next leader.
words.mnemonic: succession 源于拉丁语 successio，拆解为 suc-（下）和 cess-（走），意为连续事件或继承，在生态学中描述群落演替。
example: The team won three games in quick succession.
该队连续快速赢得了三场比赛。

kaoyan_ex.text: In quick succession, the Senate and House passed legislation protecting Yellowstone in early 1872.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“一系列”

words.def_en: Someone or something that follows and replaces another
words.mnemonic: successor 由 suc- 表示在之后，cess- 表示走，-or 表示人，源自拉丁语，意思是继任者或接班人。
example: The company announced a new leader as the successor to the retiring CEO.
公司宣布了一位新领导人，作为即将退休的CEO的继任者。

words.def_en: a separate space inside something used for storing things a separate room or area on a train
words.mnemonic: compartment 由拉丁语 com 和 partire 演变而来，com 表示一起而 partire 意为分开，描述分隔成独立小空间的设计。
example: The glove compartment in the car holds important documents.
汽车的手套箱里放着重要文件。

words.def_en: to leave a place, especially to start a trip to leave your job
words.mnemonic: 前缀 de- 表示离开，词根 part 意思是部分，组合起来指从某处出发或分离。
example: The train will depart from the station at 3 PM.
火车将于下午3点从车站出发。

words.def_en: the act of leaving a place a vehicle leaving at a specific time the area in an airport where flights leave a change from what is normal or expected
words.mnemonic: departure 由 depart 离开加后缀 -ure 形成，意思是离开或出发。旅行场景中 departure time 出发时间很常见。
example: Please arrive at the airport two hours before your departure.
请在出发前两小时到达机场。

kaoyan_ex.text: …century known as the Renaissance, the modern world saw a departure from what it had once known.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“离开”；常见搭配 from

words.def_en: to share information or knowledge with others to give a special quality to something
words.mnemonic: impart 来自拉丁语 impartire，由 im-（向内）和 partire（分享）组成，意指传授知识或分享信息，常用于教育语境。
example: Teachers impart important knowledge to their students.
教师向学生传授重要的知识。

words.def_en: fair and not favoring any side
words.mnemonic: impartial 由 im- 不，和 partial 偏袒的组成，所以是公正的，体现了前缀 im- 对形容词的否定作用。
example: The judge needs to be impartial to make sure everyone is treated fairly.
法官需要保持公正，以确保每个人都受到公平对待。

words.def_en: fair and unbiased
words.mnemonic: impartially 源于前缀 im- 作为 in- 的变体表示不，加上 partial 偏袒的，和副词后缀 -ly，意指公正无私地处理事务。
example: The judge decided the case impartially, considering all the facts.
法官公正地裁决了此案，考虑了所有事实。

kaoyan_ex.text: Assess its strength impartially.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“公正地”

words.def_en: not complete or whole liking something very much unfairly favoring one side
words.mnemonic: partial 来自拉丁语 partialis，由 pars 表示 part 和 alis 作为后缀表示 relating to，所以它描述的是部分而非整体的状态。
example: The partial report gave only some of the information needed.
这份部分报告只提供了所需信息的一部分。

words.def_en: Favoritism or bias toward someone or something. A preference or fondness for something.
words.mnemonic: partial 源于拉丁语 partialis 表示部分的，后缀 -ity 形成抽象名词，指不公平的偏爱或偏见。
example: The judge was accused of partiality because he always ruled in favor of his friend's company.
法官被指控偏袒，因为他总是判他朋友的公司胜诉。

words.def_en: in part; not fully
words.mnemonic: partially 基于词根 part（部分，来自拉丁语 pars），加上后缀 -ially，表示部分地或不完整地，常用于修饰程度。
example: The building was partially damaged in the storm.
这座建筑在暴风雨中部分受损。

kaoyan_ex.text: This means that people should avoid crisping their roast potatoes, reject thin-crust pizzas and only partially toast their bread.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“部分地”

words.def_en: a very small piece of something a word that combines with a verb to change its meaning
words.mnemonic: particle 来自拉丁语 particula，词根 pars 表示部分，后缀 -cle 指小事物，因此指微小的颗粒，如在物理学中研究的基本粒子。
example: A tiny particle of dust floated in the air.
一粒微小的灰尘漂浮在空气中。

words.def_en: A food or product that a place is known for making very well. An area of work or study that someone focuses on and is very good at.
words.mnemonic: 词根 special（特殊的）加后缀 -ity 表示状态，指专长或特色领域，在医学或烹饪中常指专业项目。
example: This restaurant's speciality is homemade pasta.
这家餐厅的特色是自制意大利面。

words.def_en: becoming an expert in one specific area a specific area someone focuses on
words.mnemonic: specialization 的词根是 special，源自 species（种类），加上后缀 -ization 表示过程，合起来指专注于某一领域的专业化。
example: Medical specialization means doctors focus on one type of medicine to become experts.
医学专业化意味着医生专注于某一类医学以成为专家。

words.def_en: to focus on one specific area and become an expert in it
words.mnemonic: specialize 来自 special，拉丁语词根 specialis 意为特定种类，加上 ize 后缀表示使专业化，常用于职业或学术领域。
example: Many doctors choose to specialize in a specific type of medicine.
许多医生选择专攻某一特定医学领域。

words.def_en: Made or trained for a particular job or activity.
words.mnemonic: specialized 词根 special 意为特殊，加上 -ized 表示使...化，指针对特定领域或功能优化的状态，如职业或生物器官。
example: She has specialized knowledge in ancient history.
她在古代史方面有专业知识。

words.def_en: for a specific reason or person more than usual or others
words.mnemonic: specially 由 special（特殊的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，表示以特定方式或专门为目的，强调与众不同之处。
example: I made this cake specially for your birthday.
我特意为你的生日做了这个蛋糕。

words.def_en: A food or product that a place is known for making very well. An area that someone focuses on and knows a lot about.
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 specialis 表示特别的，后缀 -ty 指性质或状态，因此 specialty 指专长或特色领域，在职业中常指专业方向。
example: The restaurant's specialty is fresh seafood caught daily.
这家餐厅的特色是每天捕捞的新鲜海鲜。

words.def_en: a detailed list of requirements for how something should be made or work
words.mnemonic: specification 由 specify 意为指定，后缀 -ation 表示动作或结果，因此指详细说明或技术规格，在工程中很常见。
example: The engineer followed the exact specification when building the machine to ensure it worked properly.
工程师在制造机器时遵循了精确的规格，以确保其正常工作。

words.def_en: to state something clearly and exactly
words.mnemonic: specify 来自拉丁语 specificare，species 指种类，facere 意为做，整体表示具体说明或指定细节，常用于技术文档。
example: Please specify the exact time you want to meet.
请指定您想见面的确切时间。

words.def_en: not showing proper respect or courtesy to treat someone or something without proper respect
words.mnemonic: disrespect 拆解为前缀 dis- 表示否定，加上 respect，respect 来自拉丁语 respectus 意为尊重，整体指不敬或轻蔑的态度。
example: Talking back to your teacher shows disrespect and is not allowed.
跟老师顶嘴是不尊重的表现，是不允许的。

kaoyan_ex.text: A small but vocal group of Hawaiians and environmentalists have long viewed their presence as disrespect for sacred land and a…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“不尊重”；常见搭配 for

words.def_en: to look at something carefully to check if it is good or correct to officially check a place to see if rules are followed and standards are met
words.mnemonic: 来自 in-（进入）和 spect（看），源自拉丁语 inspectare，意为仔细查看或检查细节。
example: You should always inspect the food before you eat it to make sure it is fresh.
你应该在吃之前检查食物，以确保它新鲜。

kaoyan_ex.text: …and transportation, use AI image processing technology to inspect infrastructure and prevent equipment failure or leaks before they happen.

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“仔细检查”

words.def_en: An official visit to check if rules are followed and standards are met. The act of looking at something carefully to make sure it is correct or in good condition.
words.mnemonic: 词根 in- 进入和 spect 看结合，加上后缀 -ion 表示动作，因此 inspection 指进入式查看或检查过程，类似于车辆年检的场景。
example: The school principal conducted an inspection of all classrooms to ensure they were clean and safe.
校长对所有教室进行了检查，以确保它们干净安全。

words.def_en: A police officer who leads a team. A person who checks if rules are followed. A person who checks tickets on buses or trains.
words.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 inspectare，in- 意为进入，spectare 表示看，组合起来指检查员，警察体系中的 inspector 是警督职位
example: The inspector solved the case quickly.

words.mnemonic: exception 源自拉丁语 exceptio，由 ex- (出) 和 capere (拿) 构成，指被排除的特殊情况，演变自法律术语。
example: Most students passed the test, but there was one exception who failed.
大多数学生通过了考试，但有一个例外，他不及格。

kaoyan_ex.text: But they are the exception, not the norm that Ms. Marris implies.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“例外”；后接 that 从句

words.def_en: much better than usual very rare or unusual
words.mnemonic: exceptional 来自名词 exception 例外，加上 -al 后缀，形容非凡或超出常规的特质。
example: She has exceptional skills in mathematics.
她在数学方面有着非凡的才能。

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“卓越的”；常接 to 不定式/介词 to；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: A wrong idea or belief someone has.
words.mnemonic: misconception 由 mis- （错误）和 conception （概念）组合，表示误解或错误观念，常出现在教育中纠正认知偏差的场景。
example: There is a common misconception that sugar causes hyperactivity in children.
有一种常见的误解，认为糖会导致儿童多动。

words.def_en: A person who is not in the military or police. Relating to people not in the military or police.
words.mnemonic: civilian 基于 civil，后者源自拉丁语 civis 指公民；在军事语境中，它特指非武装的普通民众。
example: The civilian helped the injured soldier after the attack.
袭击发生后，平民帮助了受伤的士兵。

words.def_en: Politeness or courteousness, especially in speech or behavior. Polite remarks or expressions, often used as a formality.
words.mnemonic: Civility 源于拉丁语 civilitas，词根 civil 公民的，后缀 -ity 形成名词，指文明礼貌的行为。
example: Staff members are trained to treat customers with civility at all times, ensuring a pleasant experience for everyone.
员工接受培训，始终礼貌对待顾客，确保每个人都能获得愉快的体验。

words.def_en: A very advanced and well-organized human society A society with its own culture and way of life at a certain time or place All people and societies in the world together A place with modern comforts and conveniences
words.mnemonic: civilization 是 civilize 的名词形式，后缀 -ization 表示过程或结果，指一个高度发展的文明社会。
example: The spread of writing and cities marked the beginning of civilization.
文字和城市的传播标志着文明的开始。

kaoyan_ex.text: Yet science has a cultural history, too, with roots going back to the dawn of civilization.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“文明”

words.def_en: to help people or societies become more educated and behave better
words.mnemonic: civilize 由 civil 表示公民的后缀 -ize 构成，意思是使变得文明或开化，常用于描述社会进步。
example: Education helps civilize people by teaching good manners and knowledge.
教育通过传授良好的礼仪和知识，帮助人们变得文明。

words.def_en: having a high level of culture and social development following fair and acceptable laws and customs showing polite and reasonable behavior enjoying a comfortable and pleasant lifestyle
words.mnemonic: 单词 civilized 源自 civil，意思是公民的或文明的，后缀 -ized 表示使成为，因此描述有教养或开化的社会状态。
example: The ancient Greeks were a very civilized society.
古希腊人是一个非常文明的社会。

words.def_en: A place where people go for medical care or advice. A scheduled time when doctors provide medical care. A private hospital or one that treats specific health problems. A building where doctors work together. A teaching session where medical students watch doctors treat patients. A training session where an expert gives advice and instruction.
words.mnemonic: clinic 源于希腊语 kline，意思是床，最初指医疗场所，演变为现代诊所，用于提供基础医疗服务。
example: The local clinic offers free check-ups every Tuesday.
当地诊所每周二提供免费检查。

words.def_en: related to medical care and treating sick people emotionless and detached, showing no feelings very plain and simple, without decoration
words.mnemonic: clinical 源于拉丁语 clinicus，最初指与床相关的医疗实践，因为医生常在床边诊治病人，后来演变为描述客观、专业的医学观察。
example: The doctor took a clinical approach to diagnose the patient's illness.
医生采用临床方法来诊断病人的疾病。

words.def_en: a natural desire to do something a growing trend or new way of doing things a slope or angle a slight downward movement of the head
words.mnemonic: inclination 来自拉丁语 inclinare，词根 in 指向而 clinare 表示倾斜，原意物理倾斜后引申为偏好或倾向，天文学中用于行星轨道角度的描述。
example: She has an inclination to help others in need.
她倾向于帮助有需要的人。

words.def_en: to be likely to think or act a certain way; to make someone feel this way to bend your head forward, often to show yes, hello, or thanks to lean or slope; to make something lean or slope a slope
words.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 inclinare，in 表向，clinare 表弯曲，指物理上的倾斜或心理上的倾向于某事。

他的诚实让我倾向于相信他。

words.def_en: wanting to do something likely to do something thinking something might be true but not sure naturally good at or interested in something sloping or at an angle

example: She is inclined to help others when they need it.
她倾向于在别人需要时提供帮助。

words.def_en: A rule or order given by someone in authority Related to or used for giving orders
words.mnemonic: direct 指导 加上后缀 -ive 形成名词或形容词，表示官方或权威性的指令，用于指导行动。

公司收到指令，要求停止污染河流。

words.def_en: A list of names, addresses, or other information, often in order. A place on a computer to store files. A sign that shows where things are in a building.
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 directorium，意为指导性列表，如电话簿或计算机文件目录，用于组织信息。
example: I looked up the number in the phone directory.
我在电话簿里查了那个号码。

words.def_en: not the main or direct cause or result of something not direct; through someone or something else not saying something in a clear way not straight; going around something
words.mnemonic: 前缀 in-（不）加上 direct（直接的），构成间接的含义，源自拉丁语，表示不直截了当的方式。

失业是新政策的间接影响。

words.def_en: in a way that is not the main or direct cause or result in a way that is not clear or obvious
words.mnemonic: indirectly 是 indirect 的副词，indirect 源自拉丁语，意为不直接的，所以 indirectly 描述以迂回方式行事或表达。
example: The new policy affects everyone indirectly through higher prices.
新政策通过更高的价格间接影响到每个人。

words.def_en: Change the use or purpose of something. Send something to a different location or direction. The act of redirecting something to a different location or address.
words.mnemonic: 前缀 re- 表示重新，加上 direct（引导），来自拉丁语 dirigere，合起来指改变方向或路径。

我们将调整努力方向，以更快地完成项目。

words.mnemonic: division 由 divide 演变而来，divide 源于拉丁语 dividere 意为分开，因此表示分割、部门或数学中的除法。

words.def_en: causing disagreement or division between people
words.mnemonic: divisive 源于拉丁语 dividere，di- 分开和 videre 分离构成，意指导致分裂或争议的，多用于社会或政治话题。

这位政客的争议性言论在社区不同群体之间制造了冲突。

words.def_en: The idea of being unique and doing things your own way. The belief that people should be free to make their own choices, not controlled by the government.

她的个人主义让她在人群中脱颖而出。

words.mnemonic: 由 individual 个体加副词后缀 -ly 构成，individual 源自拉丁语 individuus，意为不可分割的，强调每个独立实体的独特性。

学生们被逐一叫上去领奖。

她全神贯注于手头的任务。

怀疑者质疑了科学家的发现。

她对计划的成功感到怀疑。

words.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“无疑地”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: certain and not questioned
words.mnemonic: undoubted 由前缀 un- 和 doubted 构成，表示毫无疑问或绝对确定的状态。

她毋庸置疑的技能使她成为这份工作的最佳人选。

words.def_en: without any doubt; certainly
words.mnemonic: undoubtedly 由 un-（否定前缀）和 doubt（怀疑）加上后缀 -ly 构成，表示毫无疑问地或绝对肯定地表达观点。

她无疑是队里最好的球员。

words.def_en: To clean something by using a substance that kills germs and bacteria. To use a computer program to remove a computer virus.
words.mnemonic: disinfect 由 dis-（去除）和 infect（感染）构成，源自拉丁语，意指清除病菌的消毒过程。

手术后，护士对病人的伤口进行了消毒以防止感染。

words.mnemonic: imperfect 源于拉丁语 imperfectus，im- 为否定前缀，perfectus 意为完成，表示事物存在缺陷或不完整的状态。

这个花瓶有瑕疵，因为上面有一条小裂缝。

words.def_en: to spread a disease to a person, animal, or plant to make something have harmful germs that can cause disease to spread a computer virus to another computer or program to make someone feel the same way you do
words.mnemonic: 单词 infect 源于拉丁语 in- 表示进入和 facere 表示做，组合意为使某物进入并影响，常用于描述疾病传播的过程

病人可能会把感冒传染给他人。

words.def_en: A disease that can spread easily from person to person. A person or animal that can spread a disease to others.

example: The infectious disease spread quickly through the school.
这种传染病在学校里迅速传播开来。

words.def_en: the highest quality or state of being without flaws the process of making something complete and flawless
words.mnemonic: perfection 由 perfect 完美和后缀 -ion 组成，表示达到完美的状态。
example: The chef cooked the steak to perfection, making it juicy and tender.
厨师把牛排烹饪得恰到好处，多汁又嫩。

words.def_en: to become worse in quality or condition having very low moral standards that most people find unacceptable a person with very low moral standards
words.mnemonic: degenerate 由 de-（向下）和 generate（生成）构成，描述道德、品质或生物特征的退化过程。
example: The peaceful protest began to degenerate into violence as tensions rose.
随着紧张局势升级，和平抗议开始演变为暴力。

words.def_en: A person who has a broad knowledge of many subjects or areas, rather than specializing in one.
words.mnemonic: generalist 由 general 和后缀 -ist 组成，general 源自拉丁语 generalis 表示普遍的，-ist 指从事者，形容拥有广泛知识而非专精的人。
example: As a generalist, she was able to handle a wide range of tasks in the office.
作为一名多面手，她能够处理办公室里的各种任务。

kaoyan_ex.text: In this age of generalists, it pays to have specific knowledge or skills.

words.def_en: to form a broad opinion from specific facts to make a broad statement without details to apply an idea to a wider group
words.mnemonic: generalize 来自拉丁语 generalis（普遍的），加上后缀 -ize，表示使事物变得通用或从具体例子中推导出一般规则。

你不应该仅凭几个案例就一概而论。

words.def_en: able to produce or create something

example: This theory is quite generative in its application.
这个理论在其应用中相当具有生成性。

words.def_en: A machine that makes electricity. A machine that makes a specific thing. Someone or something that creates. A company that makes electricity to sell.
words.mnemonic: generator 源于拉丁语 generare，指产生器，如发电机或信号发生器。
example: The wind generator makes power when the wind blows.
风力发电机在风吹时发电。

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“发电机”

words.def_en: when someone loses self-respect and others' respect the process of something becoming damaged or worse
words.mnemonic: degradation 的词源是拉丁语 degradare，de- 向下加上 gradus 步，含义降级或退化，常用于描述道德或环境衰退。
example: The degradation of being publicly shamed made him feel worthless.
当众羞辱的堕落让他觉得自己毫无价值。

kaoyan_ex.text: That’s because economic growth can be correlated with environmental degradation, while protecting the environment is sometimes…

words.def_en: to treat someone as if they are not important or worthy of respect to make something worse in quality or condition to break down into simpler parts, especially in chemistry
words.mnemonic: degrade 的前缀 de- 表示向下，词根 gradus 来自拉丁语，意思是步或等级，因此 degrade 指降级或使品质下降。
example: It is wrong to degrade people based on their appearance.
以外貌贬低他人是错误的。

words.def_en: A student in a particular school grade. A person who grades or evaluates students' work, like tests or homework.
words.mnemonic: grader 基于 grade 加后缀 -er，grade 源于拉丁语 gradus 指步级或等级，-er 表示执行者或工具，因此可指评分老师或工程用的平地机。
example: The school play is open to all seventh and eighth graders.
学校话剧对所有七年级和八年级学生开放。

words.def_en: happening slowly over time, not all at once not steep or sharp
words.mnemonic: gradual 源于拉丁词 gradus 步，描述事物逐步变化而非突然发生的过程。
example: The gradual change in seasons is beautiful to watch.
季节的逐渐变化看起来很美丽。

words.def_en: to make a machine or system better and more powerful to improve a building or area to make it better to get a better seat or room than what you paid for to give someone a more important job a new, better version of a machine or system improvements made to a building or area a better seat or room than what you paid for
words.mnemonic: upgrade 由 up 向上和 grade 等级组合而成，表示提升等级或改进版本，常用于技术领域如软件升级。

你可以升级手机以获得新功能。

words.mnemonic: coincide 源于拉丁语 coincidere，co- 指一起，in- 表示在...上，cadere 意为落下，整体表示事件同时发生或一致。

我们今天穿了同一件衬衫，这不是巧合。

words.def_en: occurring at the same time or in the same place

words.def_en: used to add extra information or change the subject happening by chance while doing something else

example: The team was very cooperative and finished the project quickly.

words.def_en: a worker, especially one who does manual work a person who does secret work for a government or organization working or ready to be used related to a medical operation

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“代表大会”；常见搭配 at

words.def_en: related to the US Congress or its work
words.mnemonic: congressional 与 congress 相关，指涉及国会或立法机构的。
example: The congressional hearing discussed new laws for the country.
国会听证会讨论了国家的新法律。

words.def_en: moving forward step by step a series of things that follow one after another
words.mnemonic: progression 源于拉丁语 progressus，pro- 向前，gress 行走，后缀 -ion 表示过程，指逐步前进或发展的序列。
example: The progression from beginner to expert takes time and practice.
从初学者到专家的进步需要时间和练习。

words.def_en: supporting new ideas and change gradually changing or developing a verb form showing ongoing action tax that increases with income a person who supports new ideas and change
words.mnemonic: progressive 基于 progress，前缀 pro- 向前，词根 gress 走（如 regress），描述逐步前进或改革倾向。
example: The progressive company always adopts new technologies to improve.
这家进步的公司总是采用新技术来改进。

kaoyan_ex.text: Progressives often support diversity mandates as a path to equality and a way to level the playing field.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“进步的”；常见搭配 as

words.def_en: usual or typical for someone or something done often in a way that is hard to stop doing something that has become a habit and is hard to stop
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 habitus，词根 habit 表示习惯，后缀 -ual 构成形容词，形容成为日常惯例的行为。
example: Drinking coffee is her habitual morning routine.
喝咖啡是她习惯性的早晨例行公事。

words.def_en: Doing something regularly or as a usual behavior Doing something often, especially when it is hard to stop or change
words.mnemonic: habitually 来自 habit 习惯，后缀 -ual 和 -ly 表副词，意为习惯性地，描述经常重复的行为模式。
example: He habitually arrives late to work.
他习惯性地上班迟到。

words.def_en: to live in a place
words.mnemonic: inhabit 源自词缀 in- 在内 和 habit 居住，意为居住于某地；词根 habit 来自拉丁语 habere 持有，演变出习惯的含义。
example: Many different animals inhabit this forest.
许多不同的动物栖息在这片森林里。

words.def_en: a person or animal living in a specific place
words.mnemonic: inhabitant 由 inhabit 加后缀 -ant 构成，inhabit 源自拉丁语 inhabitare，意为居住，所以指特定地区的居民，如 urban inhabitant。
example: The city has over one million inhabitants who call it home.
这座城市有超过一百万居民，他们称其为家。

kaoyan_ex.text: They did not always prioritize the protection of Mauna Kea’s fragile ecosystems or its holiness to the island’s inhabitants.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“居民”

words.def_en: loss of respect or reputation; shame to bring shame or disgrace on; to fail to honor an agreement
example: He brought dishonor to his family by his actions.
他的行为给家族带来了耻辱。

words.def_en: When someone does something bad or wrong, they can lose respect from others. This loss of respect is called dishonour. When you do something that causes someone to lose respect from others, you dishonour them. When you don't keep a promise or an agreement, you dishonour it.
words.mnemonic: 前缀 dis- 否定 honour，honour 来自拉丁语 honor 表示荣誉，整体含义是失去尊严或耻辱。
example: His lies brought dishonour to his family.
他的谎言给他的家人带来了耻辱。

words.def_en: deserving great respect having high moral standards protecting someone's good reputation a respectful title for high-ranking officials
words.mnemonic: honorable 源于 honor 荣誉，后缀 -able 表示值得...的，描述可敬或光荣的特质。
example: The honorable judge made fair decisions for everyone.
这位可敬的法官对每个人都做出了公正的裁决。

words.def_en: Doing something in a way that is respected and shows good moral character. Being allowed to leave a job or position without any negative effects on one's reputation.
words.mnemonic: honorably 从 honor（荣誉）派生，后缀 ably 表示方式，意思是有尊严地或光荣地行事。
example: She honourably returned the lost wallet she found to its owner.
她光荣地将捡到的钱包归还给了失主。

words.def_en: to create or use new ideas or methods
words.mnemonic: innovate 由 in- 进入和 novus 新构成，来自拉丁语，表示引入新方法或革新，是创新的核心概念。
example: Companies need to innovate to stay ahead of their competitors.
公司需要创新以保持领先于竞争对手。

words.def_en: Creating new things or ways of doing things A new idea or method that has been created
words.mnemonic: innovation 源于拉丁语 innovare，in- 进入，novare 更新，指创新或革新，在科技领域如 AI 中常见。
example: Innovation helps us find better ways to solve problems.
创新帮助我们找到更好的解决问题的方法。

kaoyan_ex.text: …250,000 jobs, estimates the US Chamber of Commerce’s Global Innovation Policy Center.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“创新”

words.def_en: using new and creative ideas
words.mnemonic: innovative 由前缀 in- 进入、词根 nov- 新和后缀 -ative 组成，强调具有革新性或引入新思想的特点。
example: The company developed an innovative way to solve the problem.
该公司开发了一种创新的方法来解决这个问题。

words.def_en: someone who creates new ideas or methods
words.mnemonic: innovator 拆解自 innovate，in- 表示进入，novare 源于 novus 意为 new，因此创新者是引入全新想法的人。
example: She is known as an innovator in the field of technology.
她被誉为技术领域的创新者。

words.def_en: A law or set of laws made by a government. The process of making and passing laws.
words.mnemonic: legislation 源自 legislate，legis 表示法律，latio 意为提议，合起来指制定法律的过程或法律本身，涉及政府立法活动。
example: The new legislation on taxes will start next month.
新的税收立法将于下个月开始实施。

kaoyan_ex.text: …between Hollywood and Silicon Valley to win passage of legislation in Congress aimed at stopping online piracy.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“法律”；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: related to making laws
words.mnemonic: 词根 legis 意为法律， lative 来自拉丁语 latus 携带，合起来指制定或携带法律的过程。
example: The legislative process involves creating and passing new laws.
立法过程包括制定和通过新法律。

words.def_en: a person who makes laws
words.mnemonic: legislator 源于 legislate 立法，指制定法律的人，词根 lex 法律和 lator 提出者结合
example: The legislator proposed a new law to protect the environment.
立法者提出了一项新法律来保护环境。

kaoyan_ex.text: The emerging consensus around the bill is a sign that legislators are getting frightened about a politically embarrassing…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“立法者”

words.def_en: A group of people who create and change laws for a country or region.
words.mnemonic: legislature 结合 legis（法律）和 lator（携带者），源自拉丁语，原意是法律的制定和颁布机关，演变后专指国家的立法机构如议会或国会。
example: The new law was passed by the state legislature.
新法律由州立法机构通过。

kaoyan_ex.text: The state Legislature recently voted against a bill that would’ve made it illegal for towns to create legislation restricting…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“立法机关”；后接 that 从句；常见搭配 against

words.def_en: not supporting or allowing freedom of thought, speech, or action
words.mnemonic: 前缀 il- 表否定，liberal 指自由的，合起来意思是不自由的、思想狭隘的。
example: The new government's policies were considered illiberal, as they restricted many civil liberties.
新政府的政策被认为是不自由的，因为它们限制了许多公民自由。

words.def_en: open to different ideas and ways of living supporting personal freedom and limited government control favoring social change and fair sharing of wealth relating to the Liberal Party plentiful or generous broad education covering many subjects not strict or exact a person who accepts different ideas and lifestyles a person who supports social change and helping the poor a person who supports personal freedom and free markets a member of the Liberal Party
words.mnemonic: 词根是拉丁语 liberalis，源自 liber 自由，形容适合自由人的品质，如思想开明或慷慨大度。
example: My parents had a liberal attitude about bedtime when we were kids.
我们小时候，父母对就寝时间持开明态度。

words.def_en: the belief in freedom and equal rights for everyone
words.mnemonic: 源于 liberal 自由的，后缀 -ism 表示主义，在政治哲学中强调个人自由和平等权利。
example: People who believe in liberalism argue for free speech and the protection of personal freedoms.
信奉自由主义的人主张言论自由和保护个人自由。

words.def_en: to make rules or systems less strict or more open
words.mnemonic: 词根来自 liberal，源于拉丁语 liberalis 意为自由的，后缀 -ize 表示使...化，整体指放宽限制，如经济 liberalize 政策。
example: The government plans to liberalize trade laws to boost the economy.
政府计划放宽贸易法以促进经济。

words.def_en: done or shared by a group of people together referring to all members of a group as one a group of people who own and run a business or farm together
words.mnemonic: collective 来自 'collect'，拉丁语 'collectus'，col- 表示一起，legere 意为收集，引申为团体或共享的。
example: The team made a collective decision to work on the project together.
团队集体决定一起做这个项目。

kaoyan_ex.text: There’s no change to collective bargaining at the USPS, a major omission considering that personnel accounts for 80 percent of…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“集体的”；常见搭配 at

words.def_en: done by all members of a group together referring to the whole group or society
words.mnemonic: collectively 源自拉丁语 collectus，其中 com- 表示一起和 legere 意为收集，整体指群体共同行动的方式，如团队协作。
example: We all worked together, so we achieved our goal collectively.
我们大家一起努力，所以共同实现了目标。

words.def_en: a person who gathers and keeps things, often as a hobby or job the head of a district in some South Asian countries
words.mnemonic: collect 意为收集，后缀 -or 指人，因此 collector 指收集物品的人，如邮票收藏家。
example: The collector has many rare coins from around the world.
这位收藏家拥有许多来自世界各地的稀有硬币。

words.def_en: to remember something by trying to think about it
words.mnemonic: 词根 re- 表示重新，collect 意为收集，组合起来指在记忆中重新搜集往事，即回忆或回想。
example: I need to recollect where I put my keys this morning.
我需要回想一下今天早上把钥匙放在哪里了。

words.def_en: A person who fixes machines, especially car engines. The science of how things move and forces work. The study of how machines work. The moving parts inside a machine. How something works or is done.
words.mnemonic: mechanic 来自希腊语 mekhanikos 指机械，后缀 -ic 表示相关，整体描述从事机器修理的技师，常见于汽车行业。
example: The mechanic fixed my car's engine quickly.
修理工很快修好了我汽车的发动机。

words.def_en: powered by an engine related to machines done without thinking related to physical movement good with machines
words.mnemonic: 词根 mechan-（机器）加后缀 -ical 形成 mechanical，描述与机械相关的事物，如工程或自动化系统。
example: The mechanical toy moved when wound up.
这个机械玩具上紧发条后就会动。

words.def_en: using machines to do work instead of people
words.mnemonic: 由 mechanic 机械和 -ization 化后缀组成，mechanic 源于希腊语 mekhanikos，指引入机器实现自动化。
example: The mechanization of farming has made food production much faster and easier.
农业机械化使食品生产变得更快、更容易。

words.def_en: to make a process use machines instead of people
words.mnemonic: mechan- 词根来自 machine 意思是机械，-ize 后缀表示使动，mechanize 指机械化，常用于农业或工业领域。
example: The factory decided to mechanize the assembly line to increase production speed.
工厂决定将装配线机械化以提高生产速度。

kaoyan_ex.text: The Industrial Revolution didn’t go so well for Luddites whose jobs were displaced by mechanized looms, but it eventually…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“机械化”；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: To make someone lose enthusiasm or interest in doing something.
words.mnemonic: demotivate 由前缀 de-（表示去除）和 motivate（激励）组成，意思是使失去动力，常用于描述士气低落的情境。
example: Lack of support from his teammates really demotivated him during the game.
比赛中队友缺乏支持真的让他失去了动力。

words.def_en: to be the reason someone does something to make someone want to do something to explain the reasons for something
words.mnemonic: motivate 源于拉丁语 movere（移动），词根 mot-（动）暗示激发行动的内在动力或外部激励。
example: What motivates people to work hard?
是什么激励人们努力工作？

words.def_en: the reason why someone does something the feeling that makes you want to do something a written explanation of reasons for something
words.mnemonic: 拆解自拉丁语 motivus（移动的），来自 movere（移动），加上后缀 -ation，意指驱动行为的内在或外在动力，在心理学中常探讨其来源。
example: Her motivation for studying hard is to get a good job.
她努力学习的动机是找到一份好工作。

words.def_en: the reason why someone does something causing movement or action
words.mnemonic: motive 来自拉丁语 motivus，movere 表示'移动'，后缀 -ive 表示倾向，因此指驱动行为的动机或内在原因。
example: The police are trying to find the motive for the crime.
警方正在试图找出犯罪的动机。

words.def_en: the skill to do something well the legal power to handle something a needed skill for a job or task
words.mnemonic: competence 源于 competent 有能力的，词根是拉丁语 competere，com- 一起，petere 寻求，指具备足够技能的状态。
example: She showed great competence in solving the problem quickly.
她在快速解决问题方面表现出了很强的能力。

words.def_en: able to do something well good enough but not excellent having the legal power to make decisions
words.mnemonic: competent 的词根是拉丁语 competere，本义为竞争或有能力，后来指胜任的或合格的。
example: She is competent at her job and completes tasks efficiently.
她胜任自己的工作，并能高效完成任务。

words.def_en: When someone is not able to do a job or task well because they lack the necessary skills or knowledge.
words.mnemonic: incompetence 由 in-（不）和 competence（能力）组成，意思是不称职或无能，强调缺乏必要技能。
example: Due to his incompetence, he was fired from the company.
由于他的无能，他被公司解雇了。

words.def_en: not having the necessary skills or knowledge to do a job or task properly a person who lacks the necessary skills or knowledge to do a job or task properly
words.mnemonic: incompetent 前缀 in- 表示否定，词根 competent 来自拉丁语 competere，指适合或有能力，合起来意思是不胜任或无能的。
example: The new manager was considered incompetent in handling the crisis.
新经理被认为在处理危机方面无能。

words.def_en: to write music to write something carefully to form or make up something to calm yourself down
words.mnemonic: 由 com- 一起和 pose 放置组成，源于拉丁语 componere，意为组成整体或创作音乐。
example: He learned to compose beautiful songs on the piano.
他学会了在钢琴上创作优美的歌曲。

kaoyan_ex.text: …the 18th century by making his own telescope with mirrors composed of copper and tin.

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“作曲”；常见搭配 of；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: made by combining different parts or materials something made by combining different parts or materials a material made by mixing different substances together a police sketch made by combining different facial features
words.mnemonic: composite 源自拉丁语 componere，意思是组合，指由多种元素合成的整体。
example: The composite material is strong and lightweight.
这种复合材料既坚固又轻便。

words.def_en: what something is made of and how its parts are arranged a short piece of writing done for school a piece of music, art, or writing the act of creating something, especially music how people or things are arranged in a picture
words.mnemonic: composition 源自 compose，com- 表示一起，ponere 意为放置，加上后缀 -ition，指将部分组合成整体的过程，如音乐作品或写作文章。
example: The composition of this soil includes sand, clay, and organic matter.
这种土壤的组成包括沙子、黏土和有机物。

words.def_en: Staying calm and not letting your feelings show.
words.mnemonic: composure 指沉着镇定的状态，源于 compose 组合和名词后缀 ure，意为将情绪整合起来保持冷静。
example: Even though he was nervous, he showed composure during the interview.
尽管他很紧张，但在面试中表现出了镇定。

words.def_en: large in amount or size
words.mnemonic: 基于 consider，拉丁语 considerare 由 con 一起和 siderare 看星星构成，原意是深思，现在指相当大的或显著的。
example: The storm caused considerable damage to the roof.
暴风雨对屋顶造成了相当大的破坏。

kaoyan_ex.text: …such as number of publications or journal impacts, entails considerable savings in time, energy and ambiguity.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“可观的”；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: by a large amount or to a great degree
words.mnemonic: considerably 由 consider（考虑）加后缀 -ably 构成，consider 源于拉丁语 considerare，表示经过思考后达到显著程度。
example: The temperature dropped considerably overnight, making it much colder this morning.
夜间气温大幅下降，今天早上冷多了。

words.def_en: thinking about other people's feelings and needs
words.mnemonic: considerate 来自拉丁语 consideratus，con- 表示共同和 siderare 原指观察星星，引申为体贴周到的行为，体现对他人的关怀。
example: He is very considerate and always helps others.
他非常体贴，总是帮助别人。

words.def_en: to think again about a decision or opinion
words.mnemonic: reconsider 拆解为前缀 re- 重新和 consider 考虑，意为重新评估或改变原有决定。
example: After hearing new facts, I will reconsider my choice.
在得知新的事实后，我会重新考虑我的选择。

words.def_en: to keep doing something even when it is hard or others say to stop to continue to be or last
words.mnemonic: persist 源自拉丁语 persistere，per- 表示通过，sistere 意为站立，指坚持或持续努力，强调面对困难时的韧性。
example: He will persist in trying until he succeeds.
他会坚持尝试直到成功。

words.def_en: continuing to try even when it is hard lasting for a long time
words.mnemonic: persistence 来自拉丁语 persistere，per- 表示彻底，sist 与站立相关，指坚持不懈的状态。
example: Her persistence in practicing every day helped her become a great musician.
她每天坚持练习，这帮助她成为了一位伟大的音乐家。

words.def_en: not giving up easily, even when things are hard lasting for a long time or happening again and again
words.mnemonic: 词根 per- 表示贯穿，sistere 意为站立，整体指坚持不懈或持续存在的。
example: Her persistent efforts helped her achieve her goal.
她坚持不懈的努力帮助她实现了目标。

words.def_en: Continuing to do something even when it is difficult or other people disagree. Happening again and again, especially in a way that is annoying and difficult to stop.
words.mnemonic: persistently 是 persistent 的副词形式，源于 persist 坚持，描述持续不断或锲而不舍的方式。
example: They persistently tried to reach a solution, despite the challenges.
尽管面临挑战，他们仍坚持不懈地试图找到解决方案。

words.def_en: to take the place of someone or something to force people to leave their homes to move something from its normal place to remove someone from a job to push aside liquid when placed in it
words.mnemonic: displace 由 dis-（分开）和 place（位置）组成，意思是取代或移动原物，物理学中用于计算物体位移。
example: Machines displace workers in many factories.
机器在许多工厂中取代了工人。

kaoyan_ex.text: The Industrial Revolution didn’t go so well for Luddites whose jobs were displaced by mechanized looms, but it eventually…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“取代”；常见搭配 by；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: finding someone a job or home a work experience job during studies putting something in a position
words.mnemonic: placement 由 place（放置）和后缀 -ment（动作结果）构成，指安排位置的过程，如 job placement（就业安置）在职业培训中常见。
example: The job placement service helps people find work.
职业介绍所帮助人们找工作。

words.def_en: able to be substituted with another item
words.mnemonic: 由 replace 替换加后缀 able 能够，表示可被替代或更换的，工程中常见概念。
example: If your phone breaks, don't worry, it's replaceable.
如果你的手机坏了，别担心，它是可以更换的。

words.def_en: The act of putting something new in place of something old. A new thing that takes the place of an old one. A person who does a job when the usual person cannot.
words.mnemonic: replacement 是 replace 的名词形式，指用于替代的人或物。
example: The replacement of the old roof with a new one made the house safer.
用新屋顶替换旧屋顶使房子更安全了。

kaoyan_ex.text: These are “tools that help people use data, not a replacement for people,” says Patrick H.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“替换”；常见搭配 for

words.def_en: clear and easy to understand, leaving no doubt said clearly and directly without hiding anything showing or describing something in great detail, often sexual
words.mnemonic: explicit 源于拉丁语 explicitus，其中 ex- 表示向外，plicare 意思是折叠，合起来指内容完全展开而清晰。这个词演变到现代英语中，常用于描述直白或露骨的表达。
example: The instructions were explicit and easy to follow.
说明非常明确，易于遵循。

kaoyan_ex.text: It needs to give the commission explicit authority once and for all to bar broadband providers from meddling in the traffic on…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“明确的”；常见搭配 for

words.def_en: in a way that is clear and leaves no doubt in a very detailed and clear way, especially about adult content
words.mnemonic: explicitly 是 explicit 的副词形式，explicit 源于拉丁语 explicitus (展开的)，意为清晰地表达，避免任何歧义。
example: The instructions were explicitly stated in the manual.
说明书中明确陈述了这些指示。

words.def_en: Not said directly, but understood Part of something without being stated Complete and without doubt
words.mnemonic: implicit 来自拉丁语 implicitus，拆解为前缀 im- 表示在内，和词根 plic 表示折叠，整体意为内含或暗示的，不直接言明。
example: His implicit message was clear without being spoken.

words.def_en: Made to be used once and then thrown away. Easily replaced or ignored, like people or ideas. Ready to be used or spent.
words.mnemonic: disposable 来自 dispose 意思是处理，后缀 -able 表示能够，合起来指可丢弃的，常用于一次性产品。
example: Disposable cups are convenient for parties because you can just throw them away after use.
一次性杯子方便派对使用，因为用完后可以直接扔掉。

words.def_en: Getting rid of something you don't need. Selling property or parts of a business. A machine under the sink that grinds up food waste.
words.mnemonic: 来自 dispose 处理，后缀 -al 表示行为，所以 disposal 指处置或清除。环保话题中， waste disposal 涉及垃圾管理。
example: The city handles garbage disposal for all residents.
该市为所有居民处理垃圾。

words.def_en: to arrange things or people in a certain way to make someone feel or act in a certain way
words.mnemonic: dispose 的词根是拉丁语 disponere，dis- 表示分开，ponere 意思是放置，组合起来指处理或安排，如 dispose of waste。
example: Please dispose the chairs in rows for the meeting.
请把椅子排成行，准备开会。

words.def_en: helping something to happen or making it more likely
words.mnemonic: conducive 源自拉丁语 conducere，前缀 con- 一起，词根 duc- 引导，后缀 -ive 形容词，因此表示有助于或促进特定条件的环境。
example: A quiet room is conducive to good study habits.
安静的房间有利于养成良好的学习习惯。

words.def_en: A person who leads an orchestra or choir. A person in charge of a train who travels with it. A person who collects fares or checks tickets on a bus or train. A material that lets electricity or heat pass through it.
words.mnemonic: 来自 conduct，conduct 表示引导，后缀 -or 表示执行者，所以 conductor 可以是乐队指挥或电的导体，在音乐和物理领域常见。
example: The conductor guided the orchestra through the beautiful music.
指挥引导乐团演奏了优美的音乐。

words.def_en: A material that can conduct electricity under certain conditions, better than insulators but worse than conductors. An electronic device made from semiconductor material.
words.mnemonic: semiconductor 由前缀 semi 一半和 conductor 导体组成，指导电性介于导体和绝缘体之间的材料，广泛用于电子产品如芯片，是半导体产业的核心。
example: Silicon is a common semiconductor used in computer chips.
硅是计算机芯片中常用的半导体。

words.def_en: in the proper way at the right time
words.mnemonic: duly 是 due 的副词形式，due 指应得的或适当的，因此 duly 表示以恰当的方式或及时地完成某事。
example: The form was duly filled out and submitted on time.
表格已按时填写并提交。

words.def_en: not done or paid by the expected time should have happened earlier
words.mnemonic: overdue 由前缀 over- 表示超过，和 due 表示到期，形容逾期未完成的事物。
example: The library book is overdue and needs to be returned.
图书馆的书过期了，需要归还。

words.def_en: more than is proper or needed
words.mnemonic: 由 un- 和 due 组成，un- 表否定，due 指应得的，整体意思是不合理或过度的，如 undue influence 表示不当影响。
example: The teacher avoided giving undue homework over the weekend.
老师避免在周末布置过多的家庭作业。

words.def_en: to let yourself have or do something you enjoy, even if it might not be good for you to let yourself enjoy something you really want to let someone have or do whatever they want to take part in an activity, especially one that is not allowed
words.mnemonic: indulge 来自拉丁语 indulgere，词根 in- 表示向内，dulcere 意为甜，引申为沉溺或放纵自己。
example: Sometimes I indulge in a piece of chocolate cake after dinner.
有时我会在晚餐后放纵自己吃一块巧克力蛋糕。

words.def_en: letting yourself or someone else have or do what they want something nice you give yourself that you don't really need being kind and forgiving when someone makes a mistake
words.mnemonic: 拆解拉丁语 in- 向 dulcis 甜 indulgence 表示放纵或宽容 在天主教历史中指赎罪券的宽恕机制
example: His indulgence means his grandchildren can have anything they ask for.
他的溺爱意味着他的孙辈想要什么就能得到什么。

kaoyan_ex.text: Neuroscientists have been at pains to demonstrate that the pleasure a book provides isn’t indulgence; it’s good for you.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“纵容”；常见搭配 for

words.def_en: allowing someone to have or do whatever they want ignoring someone's or something's weaknesses
words.mnemonic: indulgent 源自拉丁语 indulgere，其中 in- 表示进入，dulgere 意为温柔或纵容，演变到现代英语中描述宽容或溺爱的态度，常用于亲子关系或消费行为。
example: The indulgent mother let her child eat candy for dinner.
那位溺爱孩子的母亲让孩子晚餐吃糖果。

words.def_en: to live in a place
words.mnemonic: dwell 源自古英语 dwellan 原义停留，后演变为居住或深思，体现从物理位置到心理活动的含义扩展。
example: Many people dwell in cities because they like the busy life there.
许多人居住在城市，因为他们喜欢那里忙碌的生活。

words.def_en: a person or animal that lives in a specific place
words.mnemonic: dweller 源于古英语的 dwellan，原意是耽搁或徘徊，后演变为指长期居住在某地的居民，如城市 dweller 表示城市居民。
example: The cave dweller found shelter in the mountains.
洞穴居民在山中找到了栖身之所。

words.def_en: a place where someone lives, such as a house or apartment
words.mnemonic: Dwelling 源于古英语 dwellan 意思是停留或居住 因此指长期居住的场所
example: The new neighborhood has many dwellings for families to live in.
新社区有许多供家庭居住的住宅。

words.def_en: very excited and wanting to do something very much
words.mnemonic: 词源自古法语 aigre，原意尖锐，后演变为形容热切渴望的状态。
example: The children were eager to open their presents on Christmas morning.
孩子们在圣诞节早晨急切地想要打开他们的礼物。

words.def_en: in a very excited and interested way
words.mnemonic: eagerly 的词根可以追溯到拉丁语 acer，意思是尖锐的，后来演变为表示热切或渴望，因此在英语中 eagerly 描述了急切地行动或期待的状态。
example: The children eagerly opened their presents on Christmas morning.
孩子们在圣诞节早晨急切地打开礼物。

words.def_en: a strong feeling of wanting to do or have something
words.mnemonic: 由 eager（渴望的）加上后缀 -ness 表示状态，eagerness 表达了强烈的热情或迫不及待的心情。
example: Her eagerness to learn made her a great student.
她对学习的渴望使她成为一名优秀的学生。

kaoyan_ex.text: In their eagerness to build bigger telescopes, they forgot that science is not the only way of understanding the world.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“渴望”；常接 to 不定式/介词 to

words.def_en: no difficulty feeling relaxed and comfortable to become or make less bad to make easier to move slowly and gently to make or become less tight to become or make lower in price
words.mnemonic: ease 来自古法语 aise，表示舒适，词源与拉丁语 adjacens（邻近）相关，指轻松或缓解的状态。
example: The numbers help with ease of finding information.
数字有助于轻松查找信息。

words.def_en: A feeling of discomfort or anxiety about something.
words.mnemonic: unease 结合了前缀 un- 表示否定和 ease 意为轻松，因此它传达一种不安或不适的情绪，演变自中古英语。
example: The constant noise in the room created a sense of unease among the guests.
房间里持续的噪音让客人们感到不安。

words.def_en: feeling worried or unsure about something not stable or secure making you feel uncomfortable or restless things that don't go well together
words.mnemonic: 单词 uneasy 由前缀 un- 否定和 easy 组成，easy 源于古英语 ese 表示轻松，整体描述不安或焦虑的心理状态。
example: She felt uneasy about leaving the children alone.
她对于把孩子们单独留下感到不安。

words.def_en: giving good value for the money or time spent using only what is needed, without waste careful with money, not spending too much
words.mnemonic: 词根是希腊语 oikonomia，家庭管理，引申为高效节约资源避免浪费。
example: Buying in bulk is economical because it saves money per item.
批量购买很经济，因为每件商品能省钱。

words.def_en: related to the money and trade of a country or society in a way that saves money or resources in a way that uses the least amount of something needed
words.mnemonic: economically 由 economic（经济的）和后缀 -ally 构成，economic 来自希腊语 oikonomikos（家庭管理），oikos 意为家，nomos 意为管理，表示以节约方式运作。
example: The country is growing economically.
该国经济正在增长。

words.def_en: not profitable or costing more than it earns requiring too much time, money, or resources to be profitable
words.mnemonic: 由前缀 un-（表示否定）和 economic（经济的）组成，指不盈利或浪费资源的经济活动。
example: The state subsidizes uneconomic small farms.
国家补贴不经济的小型农场。

words.def_en: to raise someone or something to a higher level or rank to lift something up to a higher position to make something increase in level or amount to make someone feel happier or more positive
words.mnemonic: 从拉丁语 elevare 演变而来，e- 表示向上，levare 意为举起，整体指提升位置或状态，如提升精神或物理高度。
example: She worked hard to elevate her team to the top position.
她努力工作，将她的团队提升到最高位置。

words.def_en: moving up to a higher or more important position how high a place is above sea level a raised area of land a drawing showing one side of a building an increase in the level of something
words.mnemonic: elevation 来自拉丁语 e 出和 levare 升起，指高度提升或海拔增加。
example: His elevation to manager was a big step up in his career.
他被提升为经理是他职业生涯的一大步。

words.def_en: A machine that moves people or things between floors in a building. A tall building used to store and move grain. A part on an airplane's tail that controls up and down movement.
words.mnemonic: 由 elevate 和后缀 -or 构成，elevate 表示提升，-or 表示执行动作的装置，所以是电梯，用于建筑中垂直运输。
example: We took the elevator to the top floor of the hotel.
我们乘电梯到了酒店的顶层。

words.def_en: A person who thinks everyone should be treated the same and have the same chances in life. Something that treats everyone the same and gives everyone the same chances.
words.mnemonic: egalitarian 源于法语 égalitaire，基于 égal（平等），而 égal 又来自拉丁语 aequalis；这个词描述主张人人平等的思想，与社会正义运动密切相关。
example: He said he was an egalitarian because he believed in fairness for all.
他说自己是一个平等主义者，因为他相信对所有人都公平。

words.def_en: the state of being equal in rights, status, or opportunities
words.mnemonic: equality 基于 equal，词根来自拉丁语 aequus（平等），后缀 -ity 构成抽象名词，指权利或机会的均等状态。
example: The organization fights for equality in education for all children.
该组织为所有儿童争取教育平等。

kaoyan_ex.text: Progressives often support diversity mandates as a path to equality and a way to level the playing field.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“平等”

words.def_en: an unfair situation where some people have more money, power, or chances than others
words.mnemonic: inequality 由 in- 否定前缀和 equality 平等构成，equality 源自拉丁语 aequalis，表示社会或数学中的不平等现象。
example: The government is working to reduce inequality in education and healthcare.
政府正在努力减少教育和医疗方面的不平等。

kaoyan_ex.text: …work, reward companies for job creation, and reduce inequality.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“不平等”

words.def_en: moral rules that guide how people act a set of moral rules for behavior the study of moral principles in philosophy
words.mnemonic: 来自希腊语 ethos（习惯或性格），通过拉丁语 ethicus 演变，表示道德规范或行为准则，涉及伦理标准。
example: His strong work ethic helped him succeed in his career.
他强烈的职业道德帮助他在事业上取得了成功。

kaoyan_ex.text: But it did so while holding its nose at the ethics of his conduct , which included accepting gifts such as a Rolex watch and a…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“道德准则”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: relating to what is right and wrong morally right
words.mnemonic: 从 ethic（道德规范）派生，加上后缀 -al 形成形容词，指行为符合伦理标准，词源可追溯至希腊语 ethos。
example: Choosing ethical products supports fair treatment of workers.
选择合乎道德的产品有助于支持公平对待工人。

kaoyan_ex.text: Whenever decisions are based on masses of data, “you quickly get into a lot of ethical questions,” notes Tan Kiat How, chief…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“伦理的”

words.def_en: in a way that follows your own moral beliefs in a way that is considered right and good by most people
words.mnemonic: ethically 来自 ethical，ethic 指道德规范，后缀 ally 构成副词，意为在伦理或道德准则上行事。
example: It is ethically important to treat everyone fairly.
公平对待每个人在道德上很重要。

words.def_en: the gradual development of living things over time as they change to survive in their environment the gradual development or change of something over time
words.mnemonic: evolution 源自拉丁语 evolutio，e-（出） + volvere（滚动），指逐步发展过程，如达尔文的进化论。
example: The theory of evolution explains how animals and plants change slowly over millions of years.
进化论解释了动植物如何在数百万年间缓慢变化。

words.def_en: related to gradual development and change over time
words.mnemonic: evolutionary 由 evolution 和形容词后缀 -ary 组成，表示进化的，源于生物学理论。
example: The evolutionary process explains how species adapt to their environments over many generations.
进化过程解释了物种如何经过许多代适应其环境。

kaoyan_ex.text: …from family and social networks than during most of humans’ evolutionary history, but introducing additional caregivers could reduce stress and…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“进化的”

words.def_en: to change slowly over time into something more complex or better to change over many generations to survive better in the environment
words.mnemonic: evolve 来自拉丁语 evolvere，其中 e 表示 out 而 volvere 表示 to roll，原意是展开或滚动出来，形象地描述了从简单到复杂的发展过程。
example: The small business will evolve into a large company with new products and services.
这家小企业将发展成一家拥有新产品和服务的大公司。

kaoyan_ex.text: Curriculums—from grammar school to college—should evolve to focus less on memorizing facts and more on creativity and complex…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“进化”；常接 to 不定式/介词 to；常见搭配 on

words.def_en: one side or part of something a flat surface on a cut gemstone
words.mnemonic: Facet 源自法语 facette，是 face 的小词形式，表示事物的小面或方面，如在宝石切割中指的每个抛光面，引申为问题的不同维度。
example: We need to look at every facet of this problem before making a decision.
在做决定之前，我们需要审视这个问题的每一个方面。

words.def_en: relating to or on the face a beauty treatment for the face to clean and improve the skin
words.mnemonic: facial 是 face 的形容词形式，指面部的，facial recognition 技术用于生物识别。
example: He has facial hair on his chin and cheeks.
他的下巴和脸颊上长有胡须。

kaoyan_ex.text: AI algorithms can 10 facial features and skin conditions to provide personalized beauty recommendations.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“面部的”

words.def_en: the way a computer program shows information to a user or gets information from a user, especially how the screen and menus look a connection or program that links one device or system to another the point where two things, systems, or areas meet and interact to connect or work with something using an interface
words.mnemonic: 由 inter-（之间）和 face（面）组成，表示两个系统之间的接触面，在计算机科学中特指用户界面，如软件接口。
example: The interface of this app is very easy to use.
这个应用的界面非常容易使用。

words.def_en: to hold someone's interest strongly
words.mnemonic: fascinate 源自拉丁语 fascinum，意为符咒或魅力，演变后表示强烈吸引，反映了人类对神秘事物的天然好奇心。
example: The magic show will fascinate the children with its amazing tricks.
魔术表演将以神奇的戏法让孩子们着迷。

kaoyan_ex.text: Yet humans remain fascinated by the idea of robots that would look, move, and respond like humans, similar to those recently…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“强烈吸引”；后接 that 从句；常见搭配 by；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: very interesting and attractive
words.mnemonic: Fascinating 的词根是拉丁语 fascinare，原意施魔法，现在用来描述极其吸引人或迷人之物。
example: The documentary about deep sea creatures was fascinating to watch.
关于深海生物的纪录片看起来非常吸引人。

kaoyan_ex.text: Plant biology is complex and fascinating, but it differs so greatly from that of animals that socalled evidence of plants’…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“迷人的”；常见搭配 from；以 -ing 形式出现

words.def_en: a strong pull that makes something very interesting the feeling of being very drawn to and interested in someone or something
words.mnemonic: 源于 fascinate（迷住），表示强烈吸引的状态，词源来自拉丁语 fascinare，原意施魔法使人着迷。
example: The fascination of the game comes from trying to guess what your opponent is thinking.
这个游戏的魅力在于试图猜出对手在想什么。

kaoyan_ex.text: …close to home, many more people would be driven by their fascination to travel to wild areas to seek out, disturb and even hunt them down.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“吸引力”；常接 to 不定式/介词 to

words.def_en: making people think well of someone or something showing approval or support agreeing or allowing something good for helping something succeed good and not too costly blowing in the direction you want to go
words.mnemonic: 源自拉丁语 favorabilis，由 favor（喜爱）和 -able（能够的）构成，表示能获得好感或有利的条件，词义从名词 favor 演变为形容词形式。
example: The review gave a favorable opinion of the new movie.
这篇评论对新电影给予了正面评价。

words.def_en: in a way that shows approval or a positive opinion in a way that is beneficial or advantageous
words.mnemonic: favorably 源自 favor（喜爱），通过后缀 -able 和 -ly 构成副词，描述以赞同或支持的方式对待事物。
example: She spoke of him in a way that was favourably impressed.
她以一种留下良好印象的方式谈论他。

words.def_en: not helpful or positive not approving or liking
words.mnemonic: 由前缀 un- 表示否定，加上词根 favor（喜爱）和后缀 -able（能够），构成不利或不赞成的含义。
example: The weather was unfavourable for our picnic.
天气对我们的野餐不利。

words.def_en: how possible something is to do or achieve
words.mnemonic: 可行性源自 feasible，词根 facere 在拉丁语中意思是做，后缀 -ibility 表示可能性，整体指某事可以被实施的特性。
example: We are studying the feasibility of building a new school in this area.
我们正在研究在该地区新建一所学校的可行性。

words.def_en: possible to do or achieve
words.mnemonic: feasible 来自拉丁语 'facere'（做），意为可行的或实际可实现的，如 feasible 计划强调可操作性。
example: Working from home is a feasible option for many jobs today.
如今，在家办公对许多工作来说是一个可行的选择。

words.def_en: impossible to do or carry out
words.mnemonic: unfeasible 拆解为 un- 不 和 feasible 可行，后者源于拉丁语 facere 做，整体指某事不可行。
example: Building a bridge to the moon is unfeasible because of the distance and technology required.
由于距离和技术要求，建造一座通往月球的桥是不可行的。

words.def_en: A person who catches fish, either for work or as a hobby.
words.mnemonic: fisher 由 fish 加后缀 -er 构成，fish 指鱼类，-er 表示从事某活动的人，所以指捕鱼者或渔夫。
example: The fisher spent the whole day by the river, hoping to catch some fish for dinner.
渔夫在河边待了一整天，希望能钓到一些鱼当晚餐。

words.def_en: A place where many fish are caught, usually for selling. A place where fish are raised and bred, usually for selling.
words.mnemonic: fishery 结合 fish（源自古英语 fisc）和 -ery（表示行业或地点），指捕鱼业或渔场，体现从动作到产业的扩展。
example: The local fishery provides a variety of fresh fish to the community.
当地渔场为社区提供各种鲜鱼。

words.def_en: Catching more fish than the water can support, which can make it hard for the fish to come back.
words.mnemonic: 这个词由 over（过度）和 fish（捕鱼）组成，指捕捞超出生态可持续的限度，常用于环境科学中描述渔业资源枯竭问题。
example: To overfish the lake would risk the future of its aquatic ecosystem.
过度捕捞湖泊会危及其中水生生态系统的未来。

words.def_en: a strong feeling of being scared something that makes you feel very scared
words.mnemonic: fright 源自古英语 fyrhto，表示恐惧或惊吓，词根与突然的威胁相关。在娱乐领域，它常出现在恐怖电影情节中。
example: The loud noise gave her a sudden fright.
巨大的噪音吓了她一跳。

words.def_en: to make someone feel scared suddenly
words.mnemonic: 源于 fright（恐惧），加后缀 -en 动词化，意为使人害怕。
example: Loud noises can frighten small children.
巨大的噪音会吓到小孩子。

words.def_en: feeling scared or afraid
words.mnemonic: 源于古英语 fyrhto 表示恐惧，后缀 -en 和 -ed 构成形容词，描述受惊吓后的状态。
example: The loud noise made the child feel frightened.
巨大的噪音让孩子感到害怕。
