如果音量太大，请调整。

kaoyan_ex.text: …structure that denies management the flexibility to adjust its operations to the new reality.

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“调整”；常接 to 不定式/介词 to

words.def_en: A small change to fix or make something better. A change in how someone acts or thinks.
words.mnemonic: adjustment 从动词 adjust（调整）派生，adjust 意为使适应，后缀 -ment 表示行为或结果，涉及微小改变。
example: A small adjustment to the camera lens made the picture much clearer.
对相机镜头进行微调后，画面清晰了许多。

kaoyan_ex.text: …channels like Adwords, Bing and social media and makes adjustments or suggestions about where advertising funds will yield best results.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“调整”

words.def_en: to get used to a new situation to change something slightly
words.mnemonic: readjust 由前缀 re- 表示再次，加上 adjust 调整组成，强调重新适应变化的环境。
example: After moving to a new city, he had to readjust to his new life.
搬到新城市后，他不得不重新适应新生活。

kaoyan_ex.text: If we readjust our view of arguments—from a verbal fight or tennis game to a reasoned exchange through which we all gain…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“重新适应”；常见搭配 from

words.def_en: similar or related to something else
words.mnemonic: akin 表示类似或有血缘关系，词源来自古英语，其中 kin 指亲属，因此 akin 强调相似性或关联性。
example: His quiet nature is akin to that of his father.
他安静的性格与他父亲相似。

kaoyan_ex.text: The residents help to look after the children, an arrangement akin to alloparenting.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“相似的”；常接 to 不定式/介词 to

words.def_en: family members or relatives
words.mnemonic: kin 来自古英语 cynn，直接指家族或亲属关系，生物学中 kin selection 理论解释基于亲缘的利他行为进化。
example: My kin includes my parents, siblings, and cousins.
我的亲属包括我的父母、兄弟姐妹和堂表亲。

words.def_en: the state of being related to each other by blood or marriage a close relationship based on shared characteristics or experiences
words.mnemonic: kinship 来自 kin '亲属' 和 ship '状态后缀'，整体指 '亲属关系'，不仅包括血缘还涵盖情感和社会联系。
example: The family reunion was a celebration of their shared kinship.
家庭团聚是对他们共同血缘关系的庆祝。

words.def_en: A person who is skilled in multiple languages. A person who studies the structure and use of language.
words.mnemonic: linguist 来自拉丁语 lingua（舌头或语言）加上后缀 -ist（专家），表示语言学家，这个词根也出现在 linguistics（语言学）中。
example: She is a linguist who can speak six languages fluently.
她是一位语言学家，能流利地说六种语言。

words.def_en: related to language or the study of language
words.mnemonic: linguistic 与语言相关，词根 lingua 源于拉丁语（舌头或语言），用于指代语言学领域或语言本身的特点。
example: Her linguistic skills help her learn new languages quickly.
她的语言技能帮助她快速学习新语言。

words.def_en: the study of language and how it works
words.mnemonic: linguistics 来自拉丁语 lingua 舌头，引申为语言，加上后缀 -istics 表示学科，研究语言结构，在 AI 领域如自然语言处理中广泛应用。
example: Linguistics helps us understand how people use words to communicate.
语言学帮助我们理解人们如何使用词语进行交流。

words.def_en: to make products in large amounts using machines to create a false story or excuse to produce a natural substance the process of making goods in large amounts products that have been made
words.mnemonic: manufacture 的词根 manu- 来自拉丁语 manus（手），fact 来自 facere（做），后缀 -ure 表示行为，最初指手工制作，现泛指工业制造。
example: This company manufactures the equipment used to make contact lenses.
这家公司制造用于生产隐形眼镜的设备。

words.def_en: a company or person that makes products in large amounts
words.mnemonic: 拆解为 manu- 手和 facture 制作，facture 来自拉丁语 facere 做，原指手工制作，现在指工厂生产者。
example: The manufacturer makes cars in a big factory.
制造商在一家大工厂里生产汽车。

kaoyan_ex.text: …iron and cheaper energy, most of the credit goes to nail manufacturers who simply found more efficient ways to turn steel into nails.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“制造商”

words.def_en: making products in large amounts using machines and factories
words.mnemonic: manufacturing 源自拉丁语 manu factus，manu 意为手， factus 意为制作，最初指手工生产，现代扩展为工业制造过程。
example: The manufacturing of cars requires many parts and workers.
汽车制造需要许多零件和工人。

kaoyan_ex.text: A recent survey of manufacturing and service industries from Tata Consultancy Services found that companies currently use AI…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“制造”；常见搭配 from；以 -ing 形式出现

words.def_en: clearly noticeable or different having a particular characteristic or quality
words.mnemonic: 来自 mark 标记 加上后缀 -ed 形成形容词 表示明显或显著的特征
example: The teacher marked the correct answers in red ink.
老师用红笔标记了正确答案。

kaoyan_ex.text: Last year marked the third year in a row that Indonesia’s bleak rate of deforestation has slowed in pace.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“明显的”；常见搭配 in；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: very noticeably or to a great degree
words.mnemonic: markedly 是副词形式，来自 mark 标记，意为显著地或有明显差异，常用于强调变化或特征。
example: The weather has markedly improved since yesterday.
自昨天以来，天气明显好转。

words.def_en: A tool or sign used to show the position of something. A feature or sign that shows the presence or condition of something. A pen with a thick felt tip used for writing or drawing. A person who checks and grades students' work or exams. A player in a team sport who closely follows and tries to block an opponent.
words.mnemonic: marker 来自 mark，古英语 mearc，意为标记，在生物学中用作基因标识，日常中可指记号笔。
example: She used a marker to highlight the correct path on the map.
她用记号笔在地图上标出了正确的路径。

kaoyan_ex.text: Hugging “is a marker of intimacy and helps generate the feeling that others are there to help in the face of difficulty.” Some…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“标记”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: important and valuable easy to understand and useful showing a message without words
words.mnemonic: meaningful 由 meaning 和形容词后缀 -ful 组成，表示充满意义的，演变自中古英语，常用于描述深刻或有价值的事物。
example: A meaningful conversation can help people understand each other better.
有意义的对话可以帮助人们更好地相互理解。

kaoyan_ex.text: …in ensuring that economic growth is translated into meaningful improvements for its citizens.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“有意义的”；常见搭配 for

words.def_en: in a way that has significance or importance in a way that conveys a message or feeling without using words
words.mnemonic: meaningfully 表示有意义地，源自 meaning 意义，加形容词后缀 -ful 充满，再变副词后缀 -ly，整体强调行为或表达的深度。
example: She wanted to contribute meaningfully to the project.
她想要为这个项目做出有意义的贡献。

words.def_en: Something that has no purpose or value. Something that is not important or valuable. Something that is hard to understand or make sense of.
words.mnemonic: meaningless 由 meaning 意义加后缀 -less 没有构成，直接表示缺乏意义的事物。
example: We fill up our lives with meaningless tasks, which don't really matter in the long run.
我们用无意义的任务填满生活，从长远来看这些任务并不重要。

words.def_en: The quality of being shared by two or more entities. A feature or characteristic that is shared in common.
words.mnemonic: 由 common 加后缀 -ality 构成，common 源自拉丁语 communis，意为共同的，因此 commonality 强调事物之间的共性或相似点。
example: The commonality between the two books is their focus on environmental issues.
这两本书的共同点是它们都关注环境问题。

kaoyan_ex.text: Ferraro suggests the results may transfer to other parts of Asia, due to commonalities such as the importance of growing rice…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“共性”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: the fact of being found or happening often; not unusual the quality of being ordinary, without special features the fact of being shared by two or more people or things
example: The commonness of smartphones has changed how we communicate.
智能手机的普及改变了我们的沟通方式。

words.def_en: not often seen or found more than usual or expected
words.mnemonic: 前缀 un（不）加 common（常见的），描述稀有或不寻常的事物，演变自中古英语的否定形式。
example: It is uncommon to see snow in this warm region.
在这个温暖的地区很少见到雪。

words.def_en: belonging to or shared by all the people in a group relating to or shared by a group of people in a community
words.mnemonic: communal 源于拉丁语 communis，com 表示一起，munis 指服务，词根强调共享或公共的属性，现用于描述集体事物。
example: The communal garden is a great place for neighbors to meet and chat.
社区花园是邻居们见面聊天的好地方。

words.def_en: A system where all property is shared by the community, and everyone works and gets what they need. A government system led by a Communist Party, like in the old Soviet Union.
words.mnemonic: communism 来自法语 communisme，commun 指共同的，-ism 表示主义，描述财产共有和生产资料社会化的政治理念。
example: In communism, all property is owned by everyone together.
在共产主义制度下，所有财产归全体人民共同所有。

words.def_en: relating to communism ruled by a communist party a person who supports communism a member of a communist party
words.mnemonic: 源于 commune，意思是公社，加上后缀 -ist 表示主义者，因此指共产主义者，与马克思的理论相关，在历史和政治语境中常见。
example: The communist party promotes shared ownership.
共产党提倡共有制。

words.def_en: a person who supports democracy a member or supporter of the US Democratic Party
words.mnemonic: democrat 源自 democracy，希腊词根 demos 意为人民，kratos 指统治，整体指民主制度的拥护者。
example: As a democrat, she believes everyone should have a say in decisions.
作为一名民主主义者，她认为每个人都应该在决策中有发言权。

kaoyan_ex.text: Now comes word that everyone involved—Democrats, Republicans, the Postal Service, the unions and the system’s heaviest…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“民主主义者”

words.def_en: relating to a system where people elect their leaders giving everyone equal say in decisions treating all people as equals regardless of wealth or status related to the US Democratic Party
words.mnemonic: 源于希腊语 demos 和 kratos，指人民统治的，常与民主政治制度相联系。
example: Voting is a democratic way to choose leaders.
投票是选择领导人的民主方式。

kaoyan_ex.text: …net neutrality rules the FCC had adopted when it had a Democratic majority in 2015, but rejected the commission’s authority to require broadband…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“民主的”；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: To make something available to everyone, especially by making it free or by giving everyone equal rights.
words.mnemonic: democratize 词根是 democracy 民主，后缀 -ize 表示使...化，意思是将权力或机会普及给更多人。
example: The government decided to democratize the education system by making it free for all citizens.
政府决定通过让所有公民免费接受教育来使教育系统民主化。

words.def_en: The belief in the importance of new ideas and methods over traditional ones. A movement in the early 20th century that favored new styles and techniques in art, architecture, and literature over traditional ones.
words.mnemonic: modernism 拆解为 modern 现代的和 -ism 主义，指20世纪艺术文学运动，强调突破传统和创新表达。
example: The artist embraced modernism, experimenting with new techniques and materials.
这位艺术家拥抱现代主义，尝试新的技术和材料。

words.def_en: the process of updating something to make it modern
words.mnemonic: modernization 来自 modern 现代的 和后缀 -ization 表示过程，指现代化的转型；常涉及社会发展如经济 modernization。
example: The government's modernization of the education system included new technology in every classroom.
政府对教育系统的现代化改造包括在每个教室配备新技术。

kaoyan_ex.text: …Service unable to pay its bills except by deferring vital modernization.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“现代化”

words.def_en: to update something to make it current and useful today to begin using modern tools and ideas
words.mnemonic: modernize 由 modern 现代一词派生，modern 源于拉丁语 modernus，加上动词后缀 -ize，表示使某物更新或适应现代标准。
example: The company is investing $9 million to modernize its factories with new technology.
该公司投资900万美元，用新技术对其工厂进行现代化改造。

words.def_en: a little wet
words.mnemonic: moist 可能源于古法语 moiste，描述物体表面略带水分的潮湿状态，常用于形容天气或土壤。
example: The cake is moist and delicious.
蛋糕湿润可口。

words.def_en: small amounts of water or liquid in something
words.mnemonic: moisture 源于拉丁语 mucidus 表示'潮湿的'，后缀 -ure 指状态，因此描述空气或物体中的湿气状态。
example: Plants need moisture from the soil to grow healthy.
植物需要土壤中的水分才能健康生长。

words.def_en: A product used to keep skin hydrated and healthy by reducing dryness.
words.mnemonic: moisturizer 来自 moisture 词根表示水分和 -izer 后缀表示工具，意思是保湿霜，常用于护肤产品中保持皮肤湿润。
example: After sunbathing, always apply moisturizer to keep your skin hydrated.
晒完太阳后，一定要涂抹保湿霜以保持皮肤水润。

words.def_en: to feel and show sadness when someone dies or something is lost
words.mnemonic: mourn 来自古英语，原义是表达悲伤或哀悼，常与失去亲人或事物相关的情感连接。
example: People mourn when they lose someone they love.
当人们失去所爱之人时，他们会哀悼。

words.def_en: feeling or showing deep sadness
words.mnemonic: mournful 由 mourn（哀悼）加后缀 -ful 构成，描述充满悲伤或哀伤的情感。
example: The room was filled with a mournful silence after hearing the sad news.
听到这个悲伤的消息后，房间里充满了哀悼的沉默。

words.def_en: The sadness felt when someone dies. Special clothes worn to show sadness for a death.
words.mnemonic: mourning 源自古英语 murnan，意为哀悼，描述失去亲人或物的悲伤过程，词根强调情感深度。
example: The family was in mourning after their loss.
这个家庭在失去亲人后沉浸在悲痛中。

words.def_en: similar enough to be compared
words.mnemonic: comparable 来自拉丁语 comparabilis，com- 一起和 parare 准备，意思是可以相互比较的事物。
example: The two products are comparable in quality and price.
这两种产品在质量和价格上相当。

words.def_en: Compared to something else Studying how things are similar or different Showing more in amount, degree, or quality The form of a word that shows more
words.mnemonic: comparative 基于动词 compare，-ative 后缀构成形容词，描述事物之间比较的性质或程度。
example: He lived in comparative comfort compared to his earlier life.
与他早年的生活相比，他过得相对舒适。

words.def_en: when you compare it to something or someone else.
words.mnemonic: comparatively 来自 comparative，词根 compare 源于拉丁语 comparare 指比较，后缀 -ly 构成副词，表示相对地或通过对比。
example: Their house is comparatively bigger than ours.
他们的房子比我们的相对大一些。

words.def_en: A person who studies nature and living things like animals, plants, and birds.
words.mnemonic: naturalist 是自然主义者，natural 源于自然，ist 后缀表示人，指研究动植物和生态的科学家。
example: The naturalist spent his days observing the behavior of the birds in the forest.
这位博物学家整天观察森林中鸟类的行为。

words.def_en: relating to or resembling nature representing nature in a realistic way
words.mnemonic: naturalistic 来自 natural 自然的加上后缀 -istic，表示自然主义风格，强调真实描绘自然世界，词根 nature 源自拉丁语 natura。
example: The artist's naturalistic paintings captured the beauty of the forest.
这位艺术家的自然主义画作捕捉到了森林的美。

words.def_en: not normal or expected not found in nature
words.mnemonic: unnatural 前缀 un- 表示否定，加上 natural 自然的，描述违反自然规律或显得造作的事物，比如人工合成的现象。
example: The sudden silence felt unnatural and made everyone nervous.
突然的寂静显得不自然，让每个人都紧张起来。

words.def_en: important or worth noticing a famous or important person
words.mnemonic: notable 基于 note（注意）加后缀 -able，指值得注意的或著名的，如历史人物或事件。
example: Her notable achievement was winning the science competition.
她的显著成就是赢得了科学竞赛。

words.def_en: used to point out an important example to a large degree
words.mnemonic: notably 是副词，由 note 加上后缀 -ably 构成，note 意为注意，表示显著地或特别突出地。
example: The house had many problems, notably its high price.
这栋房子有很多问题，尤其是它的高价。

words.def_en: to tell someone about something in an official way
words.mnemonic: 词根来自拉丁语 notificare，notus 意为知道， facere 表示做，合起来就是使某人知道或通知信息。
example: The school will notify parents if classes are canceled due to bad weather.
如果因恶劣天气取消课程，学校将通知家长。

words.def_en: to say a word or letter correctly to state something officially or formally
words.mnemonic: pronounce 拆解为 pro- 表示向前和 nounce 源于拉丁语 nuntiare 意为宣布，合起来指发音或正式声明，体现了语言表达的起源。
example: Can you pronounce this word for me?
你能为我读一下这个单词吗？

words.def_en: An official statement or declaration made by someone in authority.
words.mnemonic: pronouncement 词根来自拉丁语 pronuntiare，其中 pro- 表示 forward，nuntiare 意为 announce，组合起来指正式的宣告或声明，常用于官方场合。
example: The president's pronouncement on the new law was widely discussed in the news.
总统关于新法律的声明在新闻中得到了广泛讨论。

words.def_en: how a word or language is said how a person says words
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 pronuntiatio，词根 pronounce 表示发声，后缀 -ation 表示过程，整体指发音的方式或技巧。
example: The correct pronunciation of this word is important for clear communication.
这个词的正确发音对于清晰沟通很重要。

words.def_en: to treat someone cruelly and unfairly, especially by taking away their freedom or rights to make someone feel very sad, worried, or hopeless
words.mnemonic: oppress 来自拉丁语 opprimere，ob- 表示对抗，premere 表示压，合起来指压迫或压制他人自由。
example: The government uses its power to oppress people who disagree with its policies.
政府利用权力压迫那些不同意其政策的人。

words.def_en: cruel and unfair treatment that limits people's freedom and rights
words.mnemonic: oppression 拆解为 op- 向下、press 压和 -ion 名词后缀，意为压迫，词源来自拉丁语 opprimere 压制。
example: The people fought against oppression to gain their freedom.
人民为获得自由而反抗压迫。

words.def_en: unfairly cruel and controlling extremely hot and stuffy causing sadness and worry
words.mnemonic: op- 是 ob- 的变体，表示反对，press 压来自拉丁语 premere，后缀 -ive 表示性质，形容压迫性的统治或气候。
example: The oppressive government did not allow people to speak freely.
这个压迫性的政府不允许人们自由发言。

words.def_en: to organize people or parts so they work well together to make body parts work together smoothly to match or go well together numbers that show a point's position on a map or graph clothing items that match well together
words.mnemonic: coordinate 源于拉丁语 co-（共同）和 ordinare（安排），表示协调一致的行动，如在数学坐标系中定位点。
example: We need to coordinate our efforts to solve this problem.
我们需要协调努力来解决这个问题。

words.def_en: working together in an organized way controlling your body movements well
words.mnemonic: coordination 拆分为 co-（共同）和 ordination（安排），含义是协调多方行动以达到和谐配合。
example: Good coordination between teams helps projects finish on time.
团队之间的良好协调有助于项目按时完成。

words.def_en: having lower rank or authority than someone else less important than something else a person with lower rank or authority to treat as less important than something else
words.mnemonic: 前缀 sub- 意为在下面，ordinate 来自 order 顺序，整体指等级较低的或从属的，常用于职场或军事。
example: In this company, junior employees are subordinate to their managers.
在这家公司，初级员工服从于他们的经理。

words.def_en: feeling sorry for others who are suffering and wanting to help them
words.mnemonic: compassion 来自拉丁语 com- 共同和 pati 受苦，意为同情心，强调感同身受的情感，在心理学中与同理心相关。
example: Her compassion for the sick children made her volunteer at the hospital every weekend.
她对生病孩子的同情使她每个周末都去医院做志愿者。

words.def_en: having very strong feelings about something, like love or anger having strong excitement or belief in something
words.mnemonic: passionate 来自名词 passion（激情），后缀 -ate 表示充满的状态，形容强烈热情的，如 passionate speech。
example: She is passionate about helping others and always volunteers her time.
她热衷于帮助他人，总是自愿贡献自己的时间。

kaoyan_ex.text: Greg Newberry: Emma Marris’s article is an insult and a disservice to the thousands of passionate, dedicated people who work…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“热情”

words.def_en: with very strong feelings, like deep love or strong anger with great enthusiasm or strong belief in something
words.mnemonic: 基于 passion，源于拉丁语 passio 强烈情感，表示充满热情地行动或表达，常与爱情或事业追求相联系。
example: He kissed her passionately, showing his deep love.
他深情地吻了她，表达了他深深的爱意。

words.def_en: A person who gives money to support artists or writers. A famous person who supports a charity or organization. A person who uses a shop, restaurant, or service.
words.mnemonic: patron 源于拉丁语 patronus，意为保护者或赞助人，词根 patr- 与父亲相关，常用于艺术或商业支持者。
example: She was a generous patron who helped many young artists.
她是一位慷慨的赞助人，帮助了许多年轻艺术家。

words.def_en: Support, especially money, given by a person or group to help someone or something. The practice of giving jobs or favors in return for support. The act of being a regular customer at a business.
words.mnemonic: patronage 来自 patron 赞助人，后缀 -age 表示状态，指赞助或光顾行为，在商业中 customer patronage 支持店铺。
example: The museum's patronage comes from local businesses and generous donors.
博物馆的赞助来自当地企业和慷慨的捐赠者。

words.def_en: To act friendly but show you think someone is not smart or experienced. To be a regular customer at a store or business. To support someone or something with money.
words.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 patronus，意为保护者或赞助人，现在可指光顾商店或以居高临下的态度对待他人。
example: Some teachers patronize students by using very simple words.
有些老师用非常简单的词语对学生说话，显得居高临下。

words.def_en: to make up for something bad by doing something good to adjust something to fix a problem or make things equal to pay someone for harm, loss, or injury they suffered
words.mnemonic: compensate 词根来自拉丁语 compensare，com- 前缀表示一起，pensare 意为衡量，所以指通过平衡来弥补损失或不足。
example: No amount of money can compensate for the pain of losing a loved one.
再多的钱也无法弥补失去亲人的痛苦。

kaoyan_ex.text: It is clear that the countries of origin have never been compensated for the stolen artifacts.

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“弥补”；常见搭配 for；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: Money or something given to make up for harm or loss Money paid to someone for their work Something good that makes up for something bad
words.mnemonic: 词根 com- 表示一起， pens 源于拉丁语 pendere 衡量，因此 compensation 意为补偿或赔偿。职场中， employee compensation 包括薪资和福利。
example: She received compensation for the damage to her car.
她因汽车损坏获得了赔偿。

kaoyan_ex.text: …been worst affected by industrial action should receive compensation for the disruption they have suffered.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“赔偿”；常见搭配 for

words.def_en: meant to make up for something lost or damaged balancing or reducing bad effects
words.mnemonic: compensatory 源自 compensate 补偿，后缀 ory 表示性质，指补偿性的，法律或经济中用于损失赔偿。
example: The company gave him compensatory money for his work injury.
公司因他的工伤支付了补偿金。

words.def_en: related to or near the North or South Pole related to the positive and negative ends of a magnet completely opposite to something else
words.mnemonic: polar 与 pole（极点）直接相关，指地球或磁场的极端区域，词根源自拉丁语 polus。
example: Polar bears live in the polar regions near the North Pole.
北极熊生活在北极附近的极地地区。

words.def_en: To cause people to have very different opinions about something. To make light or other waves only move in one direction. To give something a positive or negative charge.
words.mnemonic: polarize 基于 polar 和 -ize，polar 指两极，-ize 表示使...化，因此使群体分裂成对立阵营，常见于社会或物理讨论。
example: The new law has polarized the community into two opposing groups.
新法律将社区分成了两个对立的群体。

words.def_en: a long, thin stick of wood or metal used to hold something up one of the two ends of the Earth where it spins the positive or negative end of a magnet or battery one of two completely different sides or ideas to move a boat by pushing a long stick against the bottom
words.mnemonic: pole 词源来自拉丁语 polus 意为轴或极端 在地理学中指地球的北极或南极 物理中用于磁极概念
example: We used a strong pole to hold up the tent.
我们用一根结实的杆子撑起帐篷。

words.def_en: being liked by many people
words.mnemonic: popularity 源于拉丁语 popularis，由 populus 人民和 ity 后缀表示状态，意思是受欢迎程度，常用于社交媒体或文化现象。
example: The game's popularity grew quickly because many people enjoyed playing it.
这款游戏迅速流行起来，因为很多人都喜欢玩它。

kaoyan_ex.text: “That’s concerning.” Other artists besides Rutkowski have been surprised by the apparent popularity of their work in…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“人气”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: To make something well-known and liked by many people. To make a subject or idea easier for people to understand.
words.mnemonic: popularize 由 popular 和 ize 后缀构成，popular 来自拉丁语 populus 意为人民，ize 表示使...化，意思是使事物在人群中广泛传播或流行。
example: The celebrity helped popularize the new dance move by performing it on stage.
这位名人通过在舞台上表演，帮助推广了这种新舞步。

words.def_en: not liked or enjoyed by many people
words.mnemonic: unpopular 由前缀 un- 不加上 popular 受欢迎组成，popular 来自拉丁语 popularis 意为人民的，整体表达不受欢迎的意思。
example: The new rule was unpopular because it made things harder for everyone.
新规定不受欢迎，因为它让每个人的事情都变得更难。

words.def_en: to give someone the ability to do something by giving them authority or permission to make someone feel more confident and able to control their own life
words.mnemonic: empower 由前缀 em- 表示使动和 power 权力组成，意为赋予能力或授权，常用于描述提升个人或群体的自主性。
example: The new law empowers the police to monitor internet activity.
新法律授权警方监控互联网活动。

words.def_en: When someone is given the ability to control their own life or situation. When someone is given the authority to do something.
words.mnemonic: empowerment 由 empower 演变，em- 前缀表示使能，power 指力量或权力，整体意思是赋权或授权过程，在社会运动中如女性赋权广泛使用。
example: The program focuses on the empowerment of women in the workplace.
该项目侧重于职场女性的赋权。

kaoyan_ex.text: …saw marked changes in their governance arrangements, with empowerment of junior faculty and to some degree of students as well.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“授权”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: Not able to control or change a situation. Not able to do something.
words.mnemonic: 单词 powerless 由 power（力量）和 less（没有）组合而成，表示缺乏能力或无助的状态，源于中古英语对无力感的描述。
example: I felt powerless to help him.
我感到无力帮助他。

words.def_en: not realistic or useful not skilled at making things or managing tasks
words.mnemonic: impractical 由前缀 im-（不）和 practical（实际的）构成，意为不切实际或缺乏可行性。
example: Thinking we can get all this work done by tomorrow is impractical.
认为我们能在明天之前完成所有工作是不切实际的。

words.def_en: how well something works in real life being sensible and realistic the real details of how something works
words.mnemonic: 从 practical 实际的派生而来，后缀 -ity 表示性质，强调实用性和可行性，practical 源于希腊语 praktikos，意为实践。
example: The practicality of this new tool makes it useful for everyday tasks.
这个新工具的实用性使其对日常任务很有用。

words.def_en: almost or very nearly in a realistic or useful way
words.mnemonic: practically 来自 practical 实践的，加上副词后缀 ly，表示实际上或几乎的意思。
example: The room is practically empty, with just one chair left.
这个房间几乎是空的，只剩下一把椅子。

words.def_en: better or more suitable than something else
words.mnemonic: 源自拉丁语 praeferre，拆解为 prae-（前）和 ferre（携带），加上 -able，表示更受偏爱或可取的选择，词义从动词 prefer 演化而来。
example: A quiet evening at home is preferable to a loud party.
安静的夜晚在家胜过喧闹的派对。

words.def_en: in a way that is better or more wanted
words.mnemonic: preferably 来自 'prefer'（更喜欢）和副词后缀 '-ably'，表示更可取或优先的选择方式。
example: Choose a quiet place to study, preferably somewhere with no distractions.
选择一个安静的地方学习，最好是没有干扰的地方。

words.def_en: liking one thing more than another something you like more than others
words.mnemonic: preference 源自拉丁语 praeferre，pre- 表示优先，ferre 意为携带，整体指个人更喜欢的选项或倾向。
example: My preference is for coffee over tea in the morning.
早上我更喜欢咖啡而不是茶。

kaoyan_ex.text: This 11 approach aims to cater to individual preferences and enhance the concept of beauty tailored to each person’s unique…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“偏爱”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: how someone understands or explains something how someone performs music, a play, or other art
words.mnemonic: interpretation 源于拉丁语 interpretari，其中 inter- 表示在...之间， pret 与评估价值相关，整体指在不同语言或观点之间进行解释的过程，帮助传达含义。
example: Her interpretation of the poem was different from mine.
她对这首诗的解读与我的不同。

kaoyan_ex.text: …behind closed doors and does not always lend itself to easy interpretation or explanation.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“解释”

words.def_en: to understand something or someone incorrectly
words.mnemonic: misinterpret 前缀 mis- 表示错误或不当 interpret 来自拉丁语 interpretari 意为解释 整体指误解信息 在交流中容易导致冲突
example: People often misinterpret my silence as anger when I'm just thinking.
人们常常误解我的沉默为愤怒，其实我只是在思考。

words.def_en: understanding something in the wrong way
words.mnemonic: 该词由前缀 mis- 错误和 interpretation 解释组成，interpretation 源于拉丁语 interpretari，因此 misinterpretation 指错误理解或曲解。
example: His words led to a misinterpretation of his true intentions.
他的话导致了他的真实意图被误解。

kaoyan_ex.text: About a third say the problem of fake news lies in “misinterpretation or exaggeration of actual news” via social media.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“误解”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: to do well and become successful, especially by making money
words.mnemonic: prosper 源自拉丁语 prosperare，意思是繁荣或兴盛，常用于描述事业或经济的成功。
example: His business began to prosper after he started using better marketing strategies.
他开始使用更好的营销策略后，生意开始兴旺起来。

kaoyan_ex.text: But the professional companies prospered in their permanent theaters, and university men with literary ambitions were quick to…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“繁荣”；常见搭配 in；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: a state of success and wealth
words.mnemonic: 单词 prosperity 来自拉丁语 prosperitas，意为成功或好运，后缀 -ity 表示状态，现今指经济繁荣或生活富足。
example: Economic growth leads to prosperity for all citizens.
经济增长为所有公民带来繁荣。

kaoyan_ex.text: Stringent job dismissal regulations adversely affect productivity growth and hamper both prosperity and overall well-being.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“繁荣”

words.def_en: doing well and having a lot of money
words.mnemonic: 表示繁荣或兴旺，源于拉丁语 prosperus，前缀 pro- 意为向前，词根 sper- 来自 spes 表示希望，整体指顺利发展。
example: The town became prosperous after the new factory opened, bringing jobs and wealth to the area.
新工厂开业后，这个小镇变得繁荣起来，为当地带来了就业和财富。

words.def_en: only and completely
words.mnemonic: 源自 pure（纯净的），加上副词后缀 -ly，意为完全地或仅仅，强调事物的纯粹性。
example: She helps purely because she wants to, not for any reward.
她帮忙纯粹是因为她想这么做，而不是为了任何回报。

words.def_en: A machine that cleans and makes something pure by taking away bad or unwanted things.
words.mnemonic: purifier 源自拉丁语 purificare，其中 pur 表示纯净，facere 表示制造，因此指制造纯净之物的装置，常用于空气或水净化设备。
example: The water purifier made the water safe to drink.
净水器使水变得安全可饮用。

words.def_en: to clean something by removing dirt or harmful things to make someone spiritually clean by removing bad thoughts or actions to get a pure substance from something that contains it
words.mnemonic: pure 纯净加上后缀 -ify 使成为，purify 指净化或使纯洁的过程，如 purify water 用于水处理技术。
example: This filter can purify water by removing dirt and germs.
这个过滤器可以通过去除污垢和细菌来净化水。

words.def_en: To cause someone to become extremely angry.
words.mnemonic: 前缀 en- 意为使进入某种状态，rage 愤怒，enrage 即使某人极度愤怒，这个词强调情绪的强烈爆发。
example: The rude comment from the stranger enraged her.
陌生人粗鲁的评论激怒了她。

words.def_en: a very strong feeling of shock and anger a very bad act that shocks and angers people to make someone very shocked and angry
words.mnemonic: outrage 来自古法语 outrage，原义为过度或侮辱，现指强烈愤怒或暴行。
example: The unfair decision caused public outrage.
这个不公平的决定引起了公愤。

words.def_en: very strong anger that is hard to control angry and violent behavior caused by a situation to show great anger, often by shouting to continue in a violent or intense way to spread quickly and strongly to go out and have fun
words.mnemonic: rage 源自拉丁语 rabies，原意狂怒或疯狂，这个词根凸显了强烈的情感爆发。
example: He felt a sudden rage when he heard the news.
听到这个消息，他突然感到一阵愤怒。

words.def_en: seeing and accepting things as they really are, not how you wish they were the quality of looking very real or true to life a style in art or writing that shows things as they appear in real life
words.mnemonic: realism 是 real 加上后缀 -ism，指现实主义，在艺术和哲学中强调真实描绘。
example: The leaders showed realism by accepting the difficult facts of the situation.
领导们表现出现实主义，接受了局势的严峻事实。

words.def_en: Land and buildings that are owned or used for business or living purposes.
words.mnemonic: realty 是 real estate 的缩写，源自拉丁语 'res'（事物），特指不动产或房地产领域。
example: The realty market is booming this year, with many new properties being built and sold.
今年房地产市场蓬勃发展，许多新房产正在建设和销售。

words.def_en: so strange it feels like a dream, not real not based on reality or facts used to show you really like or are surprised by something
words.mnemonic: 前缀 un- 表示否定，加上 real，real 来自拉丁语 realis，意为不真实或虚幻。
example: The whole experience felt unreal, like a dream.
整个经历感觉不真实，像一场梦。

words.def_en: to start again after stopping to extend the legal time of something to say something again to stress it to replace old things with new ones
words.mnemonic: renew 由前缀 re-（再次）和 new（新的）构成，意思是使某物恢复新鲜状态或重新开始。
example: We renew our friendship every time we meet.
我们每次见面都重续友谊。

words.def_en: can be replaced naturally and won't run out can be extended or continued for more time
words.mnemonic: renewable 由前缀 re-（再次）、词根 new（新）和后缀 -able（能够）组成，表示可更新或再生的事物，常用于 renewable energy 等环保话题。
example: Wind and solar are renewable energy sources that don't get used up.
风能和太阳能是可再生能源，不会耗尽。

kaoyan_ex.text: Every day, scientists, technologists and engineers are discovering new ways to exploit renewable energy sources and develop…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“可再生的”

words.def_en: when something starts again after stopping extending a contract or agreement for more time making something better or new again
words.mnemonic: 拆解 re- 表示再次，new 表示新的，意思是更新或恢复活力
example: There was a renewal of interest in reading books after the library event.
图书馆活动之后，人们对读书重新产生了兴趣。

words.def_en: to make something better by adding to it to add vitamins or nutrients to food to make it healthier to make someone or something have more money or wealth
words.mnemonic: enrich 由前缀 en-（使成为）和 rich（丰富）组成，意思是使内容或生活更充实。
example: Reading books can enrich your knowledge and understanding of the world.
阅读书籍可以丰富你的知识和对世界的理解。

kaoyan_ex.text: The world of AI is buzzing with an exciting potential to improve and enrich our lives.

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“丰富”

words.def_en: in a way that is full of beauty and costliness with a strong and pleasant color, taste, or smell in a very generous way in a way that is deserved or just with a lot of a particular quality or feature
words.mnemonic: 作为 rich 的副词形式，rich 源自古英语 rice，原意是强大或富饶，后来演变为描述事物在财富或品质上的丰富程度。
example: The walls were richly adorned with tapestries.
墙壁上装饰着华丽的挂毯。

words.def_en: having a lot of something good, like color, minerals, or interesting features
words.mnemonic: richness 来自 rich 富有的和后缀 -ness，表示丰富或多样化的状态。
example: The richness of the soil helps the plants grow strong and healthy.
土壤的肥沃有助于植物茁壮健康地生长。

words.def_en: always doing what is good and fair according to most people's standards believed by many to be morally right
words.mnemonic: 由 right 正确加上形容词后缀 -eous 构成，表示道德上正直或公正的，常用于宗教或伦理语境。
example: They fought for what they believed was a righteous cause.
他们为自认为正义的事业而战。

words.def_en: with good reason correctly or accurately
words.mnemonic: rightly 由 right 正确加后缀 -ly 构成，right 源于古英语 riht，意为公正地或恰当地。
example: He was proud of his beautiful house, and rightly so.
他为自己的漂亮房子感到自豪，这很合理。

kaoyan_ex.text: But Judge Patricia Millett rightly argued in a concurring opinion that “the result is unhinged from the realities of modern…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“有道理地”；后接 that 从句；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: standing straight with your back not bent standing straight up, not lying down honest and good in behavior in a straight up position a tall piece that stands up to hold something a piano that stands up tall
words.mnemonic: upright 结合 up（向上）和 right（正直），最初描述物理上的垂直状态，后引申为道德上的诚实。
example: Sit upright in your chair to feel more alert.
在椅子上坐直，让自己感觉更清醒。

words.def_en: a change to fix an error the act of fixing errors punishment to improve behavior used to correct what you just said
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 corrigere，cor- 一起，regere 引导，意为纠正，词根 rect- 与直相关如 correct。
example: The newspaper printed a correction for the mistake.
报纸刊登了针对错误的更正。

words.def_en: not right or true not following proper rules or manners
words.mnemonic: 由前缀 in- 不结合 correct 正确，直接表达错误或不准确的含义
example: Your answer is incorrect because it does not match the facts.
你的答案不正确，因为它与事实不符。

words.def_en: not in the right or proper way not as it should be done
words.mnemonic: incorrectly 由前缀 in-（不）和 correct（正确）加上副词后缀 -ly 构成，意思是不准确地或错误地。
example: The student was punished for using the calculator incorrectly.
学生因错误使用计算器而受到惩罚。

words.def_en: not enough of something; hard to find only just; barely
words.mnemonic: scarce 源于古法语 escars，意思是稀少的，现在指资源 scarce，如经济稀缺性。
example: Fresh water is scarce in the desert.
沙漠中淡水稀缺。

kaoyan_ex.text: The idea that one might burn down an entire house just to reclaim the nails underlines how scarce, costly and valuable the…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“稀少的”

words.def_en: only just; almost not right after something else happens not at all reasonable or likely
words.mnemonic: scarcely 由 scarce（稀少的）加副词后缀 -ly 构成，意思几乎不，常用于描述稀缺或勉强的情况。
example: I scarcely had enough time to finish my work.
我几乎没有足够的时间完成工作。

words.def_en: not having enough of something that people need
words.mnemonic: 基于 scarce 稀少的，加上后缀 -ity 表示状态，整体指资源短缺或供应不足的情形。
example: During the drought, there was a scarcity of clean water for drinking.
干旱期间，缺乏干净的饮用水。

words.def_en: a person who studies a subject deeply and knows a lot about it a student who gets money to help pay for school a smart and hard-working student
words.mnemonic: scholar 源自拉丁语 schola（学校），源于希腊语 skholē（闲暇学习），指致力于学术研究的人。
example: The scholar spent years researching ancient languages.
这位学者花了多年时间研究古代语言。

kaoyan_ex.text: Board members like her “casually dismiss the career work of scholars and scientists as just another misguided opinion,” says…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“学者”；常见搭配 as

words.def_en: having or showing a lot of knowledge from studying related to academic study or research
words.mnemonic: 由 scholar（学者）加后缀 -ly 构成，学者源自拉丁语 schola 学校。
example: His scholarly approach to research made him an expert in his field.
他严谨的学术研究方法使他成为该领域的专家。

kaoyan_ex.text: The grammar school boy from Stratford-upon-Avon has landed a scholarly punch after groundbreaking research showed that…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“博学的”；后接 that 从句

words.def_en: money given to help pay for someone's education serious study and knowledge of a subject
words.mnemonic: 由 scholar 和 -ship 组合，-ship 表示状态或资格，指奖学金资助或学术研究成就，强调教育支持。

words.mnemonic: bruise 指擦伤，加上 ing 形成形容词，描述导致瘀伤或激烈冲突的过程。

从自行车上摔下来后，她的膝盖有些淤青。

当地官僚让我们为一个小小的请求填写了许多表格。

words.def_en: to be a typical quality of someone or something to describe the qualities of someone or something

words.def_en: not having something you need, such as food, money, or a home

缺乏清洁水导致村民严重贫困。

words.def_en: to take away something important or necessary from someone

许多孩子在没有得到足够关注时会感到被剥夺。

words.def_en: feeling or showing very little hope and being willing to do anything, even dangerous things having very little chance of success; tried as a last hope wanting something very much very serious or dangerous
words.mnemonic: desperate 源于拉丁语 desperatus，de- 表示无，sperare 意为希望，形容极度绝望或迫切需求的状态。

那个绝望的人试图从警察手中逃脱。

kaoyan_ex.text: …both figures seem to rise unstoppably despite increasingly desperate efforts to change them.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“绝望的”；常接 to 不定式/介词 to

words.def_en: a feeling of hopelessness when you are in a very bad situation and see no way out

他的说法的准确性是有争议的，因为没有证据支持它们。

words.def_en: A disagreement or argument between people or groups. To question if something is true or correct. To argue strongly about something. To compete for something.
words.mnemonic: 拉丁语源 disputare，dis 表分开，putare 表思考，意思是争论或辩论，强调观点分歧。

关于谁应该付餐费存在争议。

kaoyan_ex.text: …lesser-known writers, who will be praying for an end to the dispute.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“争议”

words.def_en: A sensation of spinning or lightheadedness that can make it hard to stand or walk straight.

站起来太快，她突然感到一阵头晕，只好又坐了下来。

words.def_en: feeling like you are spinning and might fall making you feel like you are spinning or things are moving too fast silly or not thinking clearly
words.mnemonic: dizzy 来自古英语 dysig，原意是愚蠢的，后来演变为表示头晕或眩晕，常与旋转或高处引起的失衡有关。
example: I feel dizzy when I stand up too fast.
我站起来太快时会感到头晕。

words.def_en: to do something too much or make it seem bigger than it is to use too much of something to cook something for too long

她倾向于过度赞美，使其听起来不那么真诚。

words.mnemonic: undo 由前缀 un- 表示反转动作和 do 做组合而成，简单明了地表达撤销或恢复原状的含义。

请解开这个结，这样我们就能打开盒子了。

words.def_en: within a single country, not involving other countries related to the home or family life

公司的成功很大程度上归功于其在国内的强劲表现。

words.def_en: to give money or things to help others, especially to a charity to give blood or a body part to help someone who is sick
words.mnemonic: donate 源自拉丁语 donare，意思是给予或赠送，现在多指慈善捐赠行为。

许多人捐赠衣物和食物来帮助有需要的人。

words.def_en: Something given to help others, often to a charity. Giving blood or an organ to help someone in need.
words.mnemonic: donation 基于拉丁语 donare，词根 don 表示给，含义指捐赠行为，常见于慈善或器官捐献等场景。

长期的干旱使农民难以种植作物。

请把你的湿衣服放进烘干机里烘干。

请复制这份文件，这样我们俩都有一份。

我们通过保留一个主文件而不是制作多个副本来避免重复。

words.def_en: full of energy and strong character always changing and improving causing movement describing an action, not a state how people or things interact the science of forces in motion a force that causes change changes in volume in music

她是一位充满活力的领导者，激励着每个人。

新经理的活力激励团队更加努力地工作，实现他们的目标。

他郑重承诺要帮助他的朋友。

她帮助他人的热忱确实令人鼓舞。

法院下令对罪犯执行注射死刑。

该罪犯的处决由国家执行。

我们家的电力系统需要升级才能带动所有电器。

电工修好了我们坏掉的灯，并安装了新的插座。

words.mnemonic: elite 来自法语 élite 指精英，后缀 ism 表示主义，指精英主义，关联社会阶层或教育系统中的特权思想。
example: Critics argue that elitism in politics can lead to corruption and a lack of representation for the majority.
批评者认为，政治中的精英主义可能导致腐败和缺乏对多数人的代表性。

words.def_en: the act of sending out light, heat, or gas gas or other substance that is sent out into the air
words.mnemonic: emission 由 emit 排放加后缀 -ion 构成，指排放物。环保议题中 carbon emission 碳排放备受关注。

灯泡发出的光非常明亮。

kaoyan_ex.text: How can we inform decision makers about the best ways to bring down carbon emissions if we can’t track the amount of carbon…

words.mnemonic: emit 的词根是拉丁语 mittere（发送），前缀 e- 表示向外，组合起来指发出光线或信号。

工厂烟囱向空气中排放烟雾。

她有一种令人羡慕的才能，能轻松交到朋友。

看到朋友的新车，她感到嫉妒。

kaoyan_ex.text: By most recent measures, the UK’s GDP has been the envy of the Western world, with record low unemployment and high growth…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“嫉妒”；常见搭配 with

words.mnemonic: 源自希腊语 epokhē ，表示时代或转折点，在地质学和历史学中用于划分特定时期。

互联网的发明开启了人们交流方式的新纪元。

words.def_en: A group of people who share the same culture, language, or traditions.

我的邻居是个杂货商，他在自己的店里卖新鲜水果和蔬菜。

words.def_en: A store that sells food and household items. Food and other items you buy from a store. Related to food and items from a store.
words.mnemonic: 从 gross 演变而来，gross 原指大批量的，后来指批发商品，现在 grocery 表示杂货店，是日常生活中购买食品的地方。
example: I bought milk and bread at the grocery store.
我在杂货店买了牛奶和面包。

words.def_en: A person or company that cultivates and tends to plants, fruits, or vegetables for the purpose of selling them. A plant that grows at a particular rate or under specific conditions.
words.mnemonic: grower 从动词 grow 派生，grow 意为生长，因此 grower 指种植者或促进生长的实体。
example: The grower of these tomatoes uses organic methods to ensure their quality.
这些西红柿的种植者使用有机方法以确保其品质。

words.def_en: become too big for something grow more than someone else no longer be interested in something
words.mnemonic: out 表示超出，grow 指生长，因此 outgrow 描述因身体或心智成长而不再适合原有事物，比如衣服或习惯。
example: The kids have outgrown their clothes.
孩子们长大了，衣服都穿不下了。

words.def_en: a person who protects or looks after something a person legally responsible for someone else, especially a child without parents
words.mnemonic: guardian 由 guard 保护加上后缀 ian 表示人，guard 源自古法语，整体强调守护或监护的角色。
example: Parents are the natural guardians of their children.
父母是子女的当然监护人。

words.def_en: The act of taking care of someone or something, especially when they cannot take care of themselves.
words.mnemonic: 由 guardian 和 ship 组成，guardian 来自古法语 gardien 意为守护者，ship 表示状态或关系，所以整体指代监护或保护的责任。
example: The court granted the uncle guardianship of the child after the parents passed away.
父母去世后，法院授予叔叔对孩子的监护权。

words.def_en: help or advice from someone with more knowledge or experience controlling the direction of something like a rocket using electronic systems
words.mnemonic: guidance 词根 guid 源于古法语 guider 意为引导，后缀 -ance 构成名词，表示提供方向或建议的行为。
example: The teacher gave helpful guidance to students choosing their careers.
老师为选择职业的学生提供了有益的指导。

words.def_en: To give wrong directions or information to someone. To cause someone to believe or do something that is not true or right.
words.mnemonic: misguide 由 mis 表示错误，guide 表示引导，组合起来意为误导，常指错误的信息或方向。
example: The misleading signs misguide people to the wrong destination.
误导性的标志将人们引向错误的目的地。

words.def_en: not even or smooth in shape or pattern not happening at regular times not following the usual rules not formed in the normal way not part of the official army a soldier not in the official army
words.mnemonic: irregular 由 ir- 不和 regular 规则组成，regular 来自拉丁语 regula，因此意思是不规则的或偏离常态。
example: The stone had an irregular surface that was not smooth.
这块石头表面凹凸不平，不光滑。

words.def_en: When something happens over and over again, usually at the same time intervals. When something is arranged in an organized or even pattern. A pattern or something that follows a pattern.
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 regularitas，词根 regular 表示规则，后缀 -ity 构成名词，指事件发生的规律性或一致性。
example: The train arrives with perfect regularity every fifteen minutes.
火车每十五分钟准时到达一班。

words.def_en: a strong feeling of dislike for something that seems wrong or unpleasant to cause someone to feel strong dislike or revulsion
words.mnemonic: disgust 来自古法语 desgouster，前缀 dis- 否定，词根 gust 味道（如 gustatory），原指反感味道，现泛指厌恶感。
example: She felt disgust at the sight of the spoiled food.
她看到变质的食物感到恶心。

words.def_en: very bad or unpleasant causing shock, anger, or strong dislike
words.mnemonic: 词根 dis 表示否定，gust 来自拉丁语 gustare 品尝，加上 ing 形成形容词，意为令人厌恶的
example: The food was disgusting and made me feel sick.
食物令人作呕，让我感到恶心。

words.def_en: to cut or hit roughly to kick roughly to access a computer system without permission to work quickly on computer code to manage or handle a situation to ride a horse for fun to drive a taxi a low-quality writer a person who does boring work an ordinary horse a taxi a rough cut or hit a quick computer code solution a clever way to do something easier
words.mnemonic: hack 源自古英语 haccian 砍，含义演变为计算机黑客行为或快速解决方案。
example: The attacker tried to hack the door with an axe.
袭击者试图用斧头劈开门。

words.def_en: A person who breaks into computer systems without permission. A person who is very skilled at using computers.
words.mnemonic: 源自动词 hack，意为砍或侵入系统，现在常指计算机黑客，这些人精通技术并可能涉及网络安全问题。
example: The hacker stole private information from the company's computers.
黑客从公司的电脑中窃取了私人信息。

words.def_en: an amount that fits in one hand a small number of people or things someone or something hard to control
words.mnemonic: 拆解为 hand（手）和 -ful（满的），表示一手能握住的量，常喻指少量或难控制的事物。
example: She took a handful of nuts from the bowl.
她从碗里抓了一把坚果。

words.def_en: easy to use or do close by or easy to reach good at using hands or tools
words.mnemonic: handy 源于 hand 一词，后缀 -y 赋予其方便的特性，指像在手边一样易于使用。
example: This handy tool makes fixing things simple.
这个方便的工具让修理东西变得简单。

words.def_en: to become or make something firm or solid to become or make something more serious or severe to become or make someone more determined to make someone less kind or sensitive
words.mnemonic: 从形容词 hard 派生，后缀 -en 表示使变化，意为使某物变硬或强化，hard 本身源自古英语 heard，指坚固。
example: The clay will harden when it dries.
黏土干燥后会变硬。

words.def_en: a very hard time when you don't have what you need to live well
words.mnemonic: hardship 源于 hard（困难的）和后缀 -ship（表示状态），指经历艰难或困苦的境遇。
example: Many families face hardship when they lose their jobs and struggle to pay for food and housing.
许多家庭在失业后难以支付食物和住房费用，面临困境。

words.def_en: When things match or work well together. Making things the same or similar, especially rules or systems. Playing music together that sounds good.
words.mnemonic: harmonization 由 harmony 指和谐加 -ization 后缀，harmony 来自希腊语 harmonia，表示使事物协调一致的过程。
example: The harmonization of colors in the painting made it more appealing.
画作中色彩的协调使其更具吸引力。

words.def_en: When things harmonize, they work well together and look or sound good. To make different things the same or similar, especially rules or systems. To sing or play music together in a way that sounds good.
words.mnemonic: harmonize 意为使和谐，源自希腊语 harmonia，常用于音乐或人际关系中协调一致。
example: The colors of the painting harmonize beautifully.
这幅画的色彩和谐地融合在一起。

words.def_en: Air that is hard to see through because it has tiny water drops, often from heat. Air filled with something that blocks sight, like smoke or dust. A confused or unclear state of mind. To become or make something covered in haze. To play mean tricks on someone, like a new member of a group.
words.mnemonic: haze 的词源可能源于古英语 hasu 意为灰色，指薄雾或朦胧的天气现象，与大气污染相关。
example: The morning haze made it hard to see the road.
早晨的薄雾使道路难以看清。

words.def_en: not clear because of smoke or mist not clear in memory or detail unsure or confused
words.mnemonic: hazy 来自 haze，后者可能源于古英语表示薄雾，加上后缀 y 构成，意为模糊不清的，常用于描述天气或记忆。
example: The view was hazy from the morning fog.
晨雾使景色变得朦胧。

words.def_en: unable to help yourself or do things alone unable to control a strong feeling
words.mnemonic: helpless 由 help 加后缀 -less 构成，help 表示援助，-less 表示缺乏，因此 helpless 形容无法自助的状态，强调依赖外部支持。
example: The child felt helpless without anyone to care for him.
这个孩子感到无助，因为没有人照顾他。

words.def_en: in a way that shows you cannot do anything to change a situation in a way that shows you cannot control a strong feeling
words.mnemonic: 由 helpless（无助的）加上副词后缀 -ly 构成，描述一种无力自主行动的方式。
example: They watched helplessly as the flood destroyed their farm.
他们无助地看着洪水摧毁了他们的农场。

kaoyan_ex.text: Have you ever stared helplessly at a ZIP disk, thinking: how do I get the files off this?

words.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“无助地”；常见搭配 at

words.def_en: very brave and admired by many trying very hard to do something difficult about a hero or heroes very large or great
words.mnemonic: heroic 源自希腊语 heros，意思是英雄，描述勇敢或史诗般的行为。在流行文化中，它常出现在英雄故事或游戏角色中。
example: The firefighters made a heroic effort to save everyone from the burning building.
消防员们英勇努力，将所有人从燃烧的大楼中救出。

kaoyan_ex.text: But I believe that well-run zoos, and the heroic animals that suffer their captivity, do serve a higher purpose.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“英勇的”；后接 that 从句

words.def_en: a very strong and illegal drug that is made from morphine and can cause addiction
words.mnemonic: heroin 词源来自希腊语 heros（英雄），最初作为止痛药开发，但现在指一种高度成瘾的非法药物。
example: He became very sick after using heroin for many years.
他吸食海洛因多年后病得很重。

words.def_en: to not allow something by law or rule to make something too difficult or expensive to do
words.mnemonic: prohibit 源于拉丁语 prohibere，pro- 向前，hibēre 持有，指通过规则或法律禁止某种行为发生。
example: The law prohibits smoking in public places.
法律禁止在公共场所吸烟。

words.def_en: the act of stopping something from being done or used, especially by law a law or rule that stops something from being done or used the time in the US from 1920 to 1933 when making and selling alcohol was illegal
words.mnemonic: prohibition 源自拉丁语 prohibere，包含 pro-（反对）和 habere（持有），意为禁止，历史上美国禁酒令是其著名应用。
example: The prohibition of smoking in public places helps keep the air clean.
禁止在公共场所吸烟有助于保持空气清洁。

words.def_en: A device that allows a door, lid, or gate to swing open and closed. To attach something so it can swing open and closed.
words.mnemonic: hinge 来自中古英语，意为铰链，在物理上使物体旋转，比喻为事件的核心依赖点。
example: The door hinge was loose, causing it to squeak when opened.
门铰链松了，开门时会吱吱作响。

words.def_en: To cause someone to lose their mental balance or sanity.
words.mnemonic: unhinge 字面由 un- 去除和 hinge 铰链组成，比喻使精神失去平衡或陷入混乱。
example: The shock of the news was enough to unhinge him, and he started acting erratically.
这个消息的冲击足以使他精神错乱，他开始行为异常。

kaoyan_ex.text: But Judge Patricia Millett rightly argued in a concurring opinion that “the result is unhinged from the realities of modern…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“精神失常”；常见搭配 from；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: a person who owns or has something a container or device that holds something
words.mnemonic: holder 由 hold 加后缀 -er 构成，hold 表示持握，-er 表示物或人，所以指容器或拥有者。
example: The passport holder showed their document at the border.
护照持有人在边境出示了他们的证件。

kaoyan_ex.text: The really successful holders of such titles are those that do a great deal more than fill hotel bedrooms and bring in…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“持有者”；后接 that 从句；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: to support and keep something good or right going to agree that a past decision was correct
words.mnemonic: uphold 由前缀 up-（向上）和 hold（持）构成，描述支持或维护某事物，如法律或价值观，强调坚定性。
example: It is important to uphold the values of honesty and fairness.
坚持诚实和公平的价值观很重要。

words.def_en: the state of being pure and good, like something sacred a respectful title for the Pope and some religious leaders
words.mnemonic: 单词 holiness 源自 holy，表示神圣的状态，后缀 ness 将形容词转化为名词，强调一种神圣的性质。
example: The holiness of the temple made visitors feel peaceful and respectful.
寺庙的神圣让游客感到平和与敬畏。

kaoyan_ex.text: They did not always prioritize the protection of Mauna Kea’s fragile ecosystems or its holiness to the island’s inhabitants.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“神圣”；常接 to 不定式/介词 to

words.def_en: related to God or religion morally and religiously good used to show surprise or shock
words.mnemonic: holy 源于古英语 halig，与 whole 相关表示完整或神圣，宗教语境中 holy sites 如耶路撒冷被视为神圣之地。
example: Mecca is a holy city in Islam.
麦加是伊斯兰教的圣城。

words.def_en: without a home to live in people who have no home
words.mnemonic: 词根 home 表示家，后缀 -less 表示没有，因此 homeless 描述无家可归的状态或人。
example: Many homeless people sleep on the streets because they have no place to live.
许多无家可归的人睡在街上，因为他们没有地方住。

words.def_en: not having a place to live
words.mnemonic: homelessness 由 home 家、后缀 -less 无和 -ness 状态构成，表示无家可归的困境。
example: The city is working to reduce homelessness by providing shelter and support services.
该市正通过提供住所和支持服务来努力减少无家可归现象。

words.def_en: The act of making something the same throughout, often by mixing different parts together. The process where different groups in society become more similar, often by adopting the customs and values of the dominant culture.
words.mnemonic: homogenization 由 homo-（相同）、gen-（产生，来自希腊语）和 -ization（化）构成，指使事物均匀化的过程，如牛奶 homogenization 防止脂肪分离。
example: Homogenization of milk involves breaking up fat globules to make it smooth and uniform.
牛奶的均质化涉及打碎脂肪球，使其变得顺滑均匀。

words.def_en: To make something the same throughout, by mixing different parts together. To process a liquid so it has the same texture throughout, with no separation of parts.
words.mnemonic: 拆解词根，homo- 源于希腊语表示相同，-genize 与产生相关，意思是使事物变得均匀一致
example: The company decided to homogenize the products to create a consistent brand experience.
公司决定统一产品，以创造一致的品牌体验。

words.def_en: the line where the sky meets the land or sea the limits of what you can imagine or achieve
words.mnemonic: horizon 来源于希腊语 'horizein'（划定界限），指地平线或视野边界，常用于比喻人生目标。
example: The sun rose above the horizon in the morning.
早晨太阳升到了地平线以上。

kaoyan_ex.text: The same curiosity to find what lies beyond the horizon that first brought early Polynesians to Hawaii’s shores inspires…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“地平线”；后接 that 从句

words.def_en: flat and level, like the ground having everyone at the same level a flat, level position a flat line or surface
words.mnemonic: horizontal 来自 horizon 地平线一词，描述与地平线平行的方向，词根源于希腊语 horizein 限制边界
example: The horizontal line on the graph shows time passing.
图表上的水平线表示时间的流逝。

words.def_en: not thinking you are better than others saying you are not important, often in a joking way from a simple or poor background simple and ordinary to make someone feel less proud to defeat someone who is stronger to admit you were wrong or ask for help
words.mnemonic: 词根为拉丁语 humilis，humus 表示土地，含义是低矮或接地气的，演变为形容谦逊不自大的态度。
example: A humble person is willing to learn from everyone.
谦逊的人愿意向每个人学习。

words.def_en: in a way that shows you do not think you are better than others from a low social position
words.mnemonic: humbly 从 humble 演变，humble 源于拉丁语 humilis（谦卑的），后缀 -ly 使其成为副词，表示谦逊地行为。
example: He humbly accepted the award, thanking everyone who helped him.
他谦逊地接受了奖项，感谢了所有帮助过他的人。

words.def_en: having a lot of moisture in the air
words.mnemonic: 单词 humid 源自拉丁语 humere，意为湿润的，词根 hum- 与水分相关，常用于描述空气潮湿。
example: The humid air made it feel much hotter than it actually was.
潮湿的空气让人感觉比实际温度热得多。

words.def_en: how much water is in the air when the air is warm and wet
words.mnemonic: humidity 是空气湿度，源自拉丁语 humidus 意为湿润的，hum- 词根与水相关。
example: High humidity makes the air feel wet and heavy.
高湿度使空气感觉潮湿而沉重。

words.def_en: able to be recognized or distinguished
words.mnemonic: 来源于 identify 这个动词，而 identify 又源自 identity，可追溯至拉丁语 identitas，意指相同性，经过演变表示某物能被识别或辨认的特性。
example: The identifiable feature of the bird is its bright red beak.
这只鸟的可识别特征是它鲜红色的喙。

kaoyan_ex.text: Privacy law builds on the concept of damage to an individual from identifiable knowledge about them.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“可识别的”

words.def_en: the act of finding out who or what someone or something is the act of noticing that something exists or is important official papers that prove who you are a strong feeling of understanding or support for someone or something the act of connecting one person or thing with another
words.mnemonic: identification 的词根 identi 表示相同，fic 意为制作，ation 是名词后缀，整体指识别身份或确认相同性的过程。
example: The identification of the missing person was made using dental records.
失踪人员的身份是通过牙科记录确认的。

words.def_en: not working hard not being used without a job having no real purpose or effect free time not spent working to spend time doing nothing important to run slowly when not moving to stop work at a factory temporarily
words.mnemonic: idle 来自古英语 idel（空闲的），描述无所事事的状态，常与忙碌相对。
example: The idle worker spent most of the day on his phone instead of working.
那个懒散的工人一天大部分时间都在玩手机，而不是工作。

words.def_en: A state of being where someone is not working or doing anything productive. A period of time when someone is not working or being used for a particular purpose.
words.mnemonic: idleness 来自古英语 idel 空闲的，后缀 -ness 表示状态，因此是空闲或懒散的状态。
example: His idleness is causing him to fall behind in his studies.
他的懒惰导致他在学业上落后。

words.def_en: not knowing about something
words.mnemonic: 基于 ignore（忽视），添加后缀 -ance，表示缺乏知识或认知的无知状态。
example: His ignorance about other cultures led to misunderstandings.
他对其他文化的无知导致了误解。

words.def_en: lacking knowledge or education not knowing about something specific having bad manners or being rude
words.mnemonic: ignorant 源于 ignore，其中 in- 表示不，gnor 来自拉丁语 gnarus 意为知道，因此指缺乏知识或意识的状态。
example: The teacher was patient with the ignorant student who asked many questions.
老师对那个问了很多问题的无知学生很有耐心。

kaoyan_ex.text: You can call their views stupid, or joke about how ignorant they are.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“无知的”

words.def_en: to copy someone or something to copy how someone speaks or acts to make others laugh
words.mnemonic: imitate 源于拉丁语 imitari，意思是模仿行为，常用于艺术或日常复制。
example: Children often imitate the actions of their parents.
孩子们经常模仿父母的行为。

kaoyan_ex.text: What makes humans humans?” What is being called artificial general intelligence, machines that would imitate the way humans…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“模仿”

words.def_en: a copy of something, especially something expensive the act of copying someone or something copying how someone talks or acts to make people laugh
words.mnemonic: imitation 源于拉丁语 imitari，意为模仿，词根 imit- 表示复制行为，帮助我们理解它描述的是对原物的仿造。
example: This watch is an imitation of a luxury brand.
这块手表是奢侈品牌的仿制品。

kaoyan_ex.text: While hunter-gatherer children learnt from observation and imitation in mixedage playgroups, researchers said that western…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“仿制品”；后接 that 从句；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: to put a plan or decision into action a simple tool used for outdoor work
words.mnemonic: 源自拉丁语 implere，意为填满或完成，后缀 -ment 表示工具或行为，因此 implement 作为名词指器具，作为动词指执行计划。农业中常用 implement 指农具。
example: The school will implement the new safety rules next week.
学校将于下周实施新的安全规则。

words.def_en: the process of putting a plan or system into action
words.mnemonic: 由 implement 实施加后缀 -ation 构成，表示执行计划的过程，implement 源于拉丁语 implementum，意为工具。
example: The implementation of the new software will begin next week.
新软件的实施将于下周开始。

words.def_en: to persuade or influence someone to do something to cause something to happen to start childbirth using medicine
words.mnemonic: 词根是拉丁语 inducere，包含 in-（进入）和 ducere（引导），表示引导某人进入特定状态或引起反应，在科学中用于描述诱发效应。
example: Nothing could induce me to take that job.
没有什么能诱使我接受那份工作。

words.def_en: something offered to persuade someone to do something
words.mnemonic: inducement 来自 induce，induce 源于拉丁语 inducere，in- 进入，ducere 引导，后缀 -ment 表示结果，指诱因或激励因素。
example: The company offered a bonus as an inducement for employees to work overtime.
公司提供奖金作为激励员工加班的诱因。

words.def_en: to decide something is true based on information you have to hint that something is true without saying it directly

example: The tropical climate is perfect for growing bananas and pineapples.
热带气候非常适合种植香蕉和菠萝。

kaoyan_ex.text: Indonesia has the third-largest area of tropical forest in the world and one of the highest deforestation rates.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“热带的”；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: Looking back at past events or thinking about things that have already happened.
words.mnemonic: retrospect 源于拉丁语，由 retro-（向后）和 -spect（看）构成，意思是回顾过去，常用于反思或总结事件。
example: In retrospect, I see that my choice was not the best one.
回想起来，我意识到我的选择不是最好的。

words.def_en: Reflecting on or thinking back over past events or experiences.
words.mnemonic: retrospection 由 retro-（向后）和 inspection（审视）构成，指回顾过去的行为或思考。
example: Her retrospection of childhood memories brought both joy and sorrow.
她对童年记忆的回顾带来了欢乐和悲伤。

words.def_en: A feeling that you believe someone or something is not honest or reliable. To believe that someone or something is not honest or reliable.
words.mnemonic: distrust 由 dis 和 trust 组成，dis 表示否定，trust 源于古诺尔斯语 traust，指信心，整体意为不信任。
example: There was a clear sense of distrust between the two groups.
两组之间明显存在不信任感。

kaoyan_ex.text: Yet as distrust has risen toward all media, people may be starting to beef up their media literacy skills.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“不信任”

words.def_en: to give someone the responsibility to do something or take care of someone
words.mnemonic: 拆解为 en- 使和 trust 信任，意思是将某事托付给他人，强调信任的行为。
example: I will entrust you with looking after my dog while I'm away.
我不在的时候，我会委托你照顾我的狗。

words.def_en: knowing something by feeling, not facts a strong feeling that something is true without proof
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 intuitio，in- 表示进入，tueri 意为看，描述无需推理的直覺洞察。
example: My intuition told me to trust her.
我的直觉告诉我应该信任她。

words.def_en: based on feelings instead of facts able to understand things by feeling easy to use and understand
words.mnemonic: intuitive 来自 intuition，词源是拉丁语 intueri 意为注视或洞察，描述基于本能而非逻辑的理解，如 intuitive design 在用户界面中表示易用性。
example: Her intuitive guess was surprisingly accurate.
她凭直觉的猜测出奇地准确。

words.def_en: to interrupt someone when they are busy, resting, or sleeping to make someone feel worried or upset to move something out of its place to change how something normally works
words.mnemonic: disturb 源自拉丁语 disturbare，dis- 表示分离，turbare 意为扰乱，整体含义是打断平静或引起不安。
example: Please do not disturb me while I am working.
我工作时请不要打扰我。

kaoyan_ex.text: …by their fascination to travel to wild areas to seek out, disturb and even hunt them down.

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“打扰”

words.def_en: something that interrupts or upsets normal activity or peace violent or noisy behavior in public that causes trouble a problem with how the body or mind normally works
words.mnemonic: disturbance 由 disturb 和 -ance 后缀构成，disturb 来自拉丁语 disturbare 意为打乱，整体表示干扰或混乱的状态。
example: The loud noise caused a disturbance that made it hard to concentrate.
巨大的噪音造成了干扰，使人难以集中注意力。

words.def_en: to represent something as a perfect example to be a characteristic feature of something
words.mnemonic: typify 由 type（类型，来自希腊语 typos 模型）和 -ify（使成为）构成，指某事物典型代表一类特征。
example: The red phone box typifies British culture.
红色电话亭是英国文化的典型代表。

words.def_en: a person who types letters and documents in an office a person who uses a keyboard to type
words.mnemonic: typist 来自 type（打字），后缀 ist 表示从事该活动的人，因此指使用打字机或键盘输入文字的职业人员。
example: The office hired a new typist to help with the paperwork.
办公室新雇了一名打字员来协助处理文书工作。

words.def_en: A group of people elected to govern a local area. The organization that provides local services like schools and housing. A group chosen to give advice or make decisions. A formal meeting to discuss important matters.
words.mnemonic: 词根源于拉丁语 concilium 意为会议，所以 council 指一群人组成的决策机构，如政府 council 或社区 council。
example: The city council voted to build a new park.
市议会投票决定建造一个新公园。

kaoyan_ex.text: The Small Business & Entrepreneurship Council advocacy group said in a statement, “Small businesses and internet entrepreneurs…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“议会”；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: a trained person who helps people with personal problems a lawyer who gives legal advice a person who takes care of children at summer camp
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 consulere，con 表示一起，salire 意思是跳跃，引申为咨询，counselor 指提供建议的顾问，如学校 counselor。
example: The counselor helped me talk about my feelings and find ways to feel better.
辅导员帮助我谈论我的感受，并找到感觉更好的方法。

words.def_en: the act of bringing different parts together to form one whole
words.mnemonic: unification 由 uni 表示单一，fic 表示做，加上后缀 ation，指统一的过程或使成为一体。
example: The unification of the two companies created a stronger business.
两家公司的合并创建了一家更强大的企业。

words.def_en: to bring together into one whole
words.mnemonic: uni- 前缀表示单一或统一，-fy 后缀意为使成为，组合指使不同部分成为一体。
example: The new leader wants to unify the country by bringing all regions together.
新领导人希望通过团结所有地区来统一国家。

words.def_en: to give someone a shot to prevent disease
words.mnemonic: 来自 vaccine 疫苗，词源 vacca 在拉丁语中意为牛，因为早期疫苗源自牛痘，用于预防疾病。
example: Doctors vaccinate children to keep them healthy.
医生给儿童接种疫苗以保持他们的健康。

words.def_en: A medicine that helps your body fight off diseases.
words.mnemonic: vaccine 词根源于拉丁语 vacca 牛，因历史上首种疫苗来自牛痘，现在泛指预防疾病的生物制剂。
example: The new vaccine helps protect people from getting sick.
新疫苗有助于保护人们免受疾病侵袭。

words.def_en: to be common or widespread in a place or time to win or be accepted after a fight or argument to defeat someone after a long effort
words.mnemonic: prevail 源于拉丁语 praevalere，其中 prae- 表示在前，valere 表示强壮，整体指在竞争中占据优势或成为主流。
example: Old traditions still prevail in many rural areas.
旧传统在许多农村地区仍然盛行。

words.def_en: the most common or widely accepted the wind that blows most often in a particular area
words.mnemonic: prevailing 来自 prevail 盛行，词根拉丁语 praevalere 意为更强大，加上 -ing 表示占主导的或普遍的。
example: The prevailing opinion is that we should invest in renewable energy.
主流观点认为我们应该投资可再生能源。

words.def_en: using the newest ideas, methods, or technology hard or for people who already know a lot far along in time or development
words.mnemonic: 前缀 ad- 表示向， vance 源于 ante 意思前，后缀 -ed 表示状态，指处于较高发展阶段或复杂的水平。
example: The company uses advanced technology to make better products.
该公司使用先进技术来制造更好的产品。

kaoyan_ex.text: More than half a century ago, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology opened its Center for Advanced Visual Studies (CAVS)…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“先进的”；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: helping something or someone move forward or improve moving up in your job or social position
words.mnemonic: advancement 由前缀 ad-（朝向）和词根 vance（前进）构成，后缀 -ment 表示过程或状态，整体指进步或提升。
example: The advancement of technology makes our lives easier.
技术的进步使我们的生活更加便利。

kaoyan_ex.text: …do bad science, but that our current system of career advancement positively encourages it.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“推动”

words.def_en: helpful or useful in a situation
words.mnemonic: advantageous 基于 advantage，词源是古法语 avantage，其中 avant 指前方，因此表示具有优势或有利的，常用于策略或条件描述。
example: Learning a new language is advantageous for finding better job opportunities.
学习一门新语言有利于找到更好的工作机会。

words.def_en: to put someone in a worse position or make it harder for them to succeed something that makes success more difficult or puts someone in a worse position
words.mnemonic: 前缀 dis- 表示否定或剥夺，advantage 来自法语 avantage 意为优势，因此整体指不利条件或劣势。
example: This new rule could disadvantage people who don't have internet access.
这项新规定可能对没有互联网接入的人不利。

kaoyan_ex.text: The main disadvantage of using AI to respond to customers is that there are concerns about trusting personal interactions to…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“使处于不利地位”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: A person or company that builds or improves buildings and land to make money. A person or company that creates new products. A chemical used to make photos from film.
words.mnemonic: Developer 由 develop 和 -er 组成，develop 来自法语 développer 意思是展开或发展，-er 表示执行者；在科技领域，developer 特指软件开发人员。
example: The developer built new houses on the empty land.
开发商在空地上建了新房子。

kaoyan_ex.text: “I think the question is, shouldn’t a developer who’s really building a hotel, but disguising it as not a hotel, be treated…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“开发商”

words.def_en: not used for farming, building, or other purposes lacking modern industries and having poor living conditions not fully grown or mature
words.mnemonic: undeveloped 由 un-（未）和 developed（发展的）组成，指未开发的地区或资源，如原始森林。
example: The undeveloped land was left natural and wild.
那片未开发的土地保持着自然野生的状态。

words.def_en: to let fresh air move through a room or building to share your thoughts or feelings openly
words.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 ventilare（通风），与 ventus（风）相关，意思是使空气流通，建筑设计中确保室内空气质量。
example: Open the window to ventilate the room and let in fresh air.
打开窗户给房间通风，让新鲜空气进来。

words.def_en: letting fresh air flow into and through a space
words.mnemonic: ventilation 来自拉丁语 ventilare，词根 ventus 意为风，指空气流通系统，用于改善室内环境。
example: Good ventilation helps keep the air clean and fresh in your home.
良好的通风有助于保持家中空气清洁新鲜。

words.def_en: to stop something bad from happening to turn your eyes away from something you don't want to see
words.mnemonic: avert 前缀 a- 表示离开，词根 vertere 来自拉丁语（转动），意为转移视线或避免危险。
example: They worked hard to avert a major accident.
他们努力工作以避免一场重大事故。

words.def_en: straight up and down organized in levels from top to bottom passed from parent to child a straight up and down line a specific business area
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 vertex 顶点，因为顶点常位于垂直方向，现指与地面垂直的线条或结构。
example: The vertical line on the wall shows the exact center.
墙上的垂直线显示了精确的中心点。

words.def_en: Illegal activities involving sex or drugs Bad or immoral behavior; a personal bad habit A tool that holds objects tightly in place for work
words.mnemonic: vice 源于拉丁语 vitium，意为恶习或缺陷；也用于副职，如 vice president（副总统），在道德或职位语境中常见。
example: The police vice unit works to stop illegal activities like gambling and drug use.
警察扫黄队致力于打击赌博和吸毒等非法活动。

kaoyan_ex.text: …researchers could also be artists, writers and poets, and vice versa.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“色毒犯罪”

words.def_en: very violent and cruel likely to attack and hurt others full of hate and anger very bad and hard to stop
words.mnemonic: vicious 源自拉丁语 vitiosus，意为有缺陷的，演变出恶毒或凶猛的含义，与恶习相关。
example: The vicious attack left the victim badly injured.
恶毒的攻击使受害者受了重伤。

words.def_en: to officially decide in court that someone is guilty of a crime a person who has been found guilty of a crime and is in prison
words.mnemonic: convict 前缀 con- 加强意义，vict 源于拉丁语 vincere 意为征服，整体指被定罪的人，含义从战胜演变为司法判决。
example: The court will convict the person if the evidence proves they committed the crime.
如果证据证明此人犯罪，法院将定罪。

words.def_en: a court's decision that someone is guilty of a crime a strong belief or opinion the feeling of being sure about what you say or do
words.mnemonic: conviction 来自拉丁语 convictio，词根 con- 表示强调，vincere 意为征服，既指坚定的信念，也用于法律中的定罪判决。
example: His conviction for theft was based on strong evidence.
他因盗窃被定罪是基于确凿的证据。

kaoyan_ex.text: In a rare unanimous ruling, the US Supreme Court has overturned the corruption conviction of a former Virginia governor,…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“定罪”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: full of energy and strength growing strong and healthy
words.mnemonic: vigorous 源于拉丁语 vigor（活力），后缀 -ous 表示充满的，因此该词形容精力充沛或强有力的状态。
example: She does vigorous exercise every morning to stay healthy.
她每天早上做剧烈运动以保持健康。

words.def_en: with a lot of energy and force
words.mnemonic: vigorously 源于 vigor 表示精力，后缀 -ous 和 -ly 形成副词，形容充满活力地行动。
example: He vigorously defended his ideas in the debate.
他在辩论中激烈地捍卫自己的观点。

words.def_en: using physical force to hurt or kill showing very strong feelings very strong and sudden extremely bright
words.mnemonic: violent 源于拉丁语 violentus，词根 violare 意为侵犯，描述暴力行为，社会应减少 violent incidents。
example: The protest became violent when people started fighting.
当人们开始打架时，抗议演变成了暴力事件。

words.def_en: with strong, forceful movements very strongly or intensely in a way that causes harm or damage
words.mnemonic: 词根 viol- 来自拉丁语 violentus，表示强力或猛烈，与 violate 相关，描述极端激烈行为。
example: He shook the bottle violently to mix the contents.
他猛烈地摇晃瓶子，使内容物混合均匀。

words.def_en: relating to light that is beyond violet in the color spectrum and invisible to human eyes
words.mnemonic: ultraviolet 由前缀 ultra-（超越）和 violet（紫色）组成，指光谱中波长短于可见紫光的部分，与紫外线灯和防晒产品密切相关，用于健康防护。
example: Sunscreen helps protect your skin from harmful ultraviolet radiation.
防晒霜有助于保护皮肤免受有害紫外线的伤害。

words.def_en: a color between blue and purple a small plant with purple or white flowers that smell sweet
words.mnemonic: 词根来自拉丁语 viola，指紫罗兰植物，引申为紫色；在光谱中 violet 代表短波长颜色，与艺术和自然紧密相关。
example: She has beautiful violet eyes that shine in the light.
她有一双美丽的紫罗兰色眼睛，在光线下闪闪发光。

words.def_en: a string instrument played with a bow while held under the chin
words.mnemonic: violin 源自意大利语 violino，指一种弦乐器，中文直接音译为小提琴，常用于古典音乐演奏。
example: She plays the violin beautifully in the orchestra.
她在管弦乐队中优美地演奏小提琴。

words.def_en: someone who plays the violin
words.mnemonic: violinist 由 violin 小提琴和 ist 后缀表示人组成，直接指代演奏小提琴的音乐家。
example: The violinist played a beautiful song at the concert.
小提琴家在音乐会上演奏了一首优美的曲子。

words.def_en: to create or invent something new
words.mnemonic: devise 源于古法语 deviser 意思是计划或发明，现在多用于法律或创新语境中表示设计新方案。
example: The team had to devise a plan to solve the problem quickly.
团队必须迅速制定一个计划来解决问题。

words.def_en: official permission to enter or leave a country, shown as a stamp in your passport
words.mnemonic: visa 源于拉丁语 charta visa，意思是检查过的文件。这个词指官方旅行许可，如旅游 visa，与国际旅行直接关联。
example: You need a visa to visit many foreign countries.
访问许多外国需要签证。

words.def_en: Work that feels right for you Feeling that certain work is right for you Call from God to be a priest or nun
words.mnemonic: vocation 拆解为词根 voc（来自拉丁语 vocare，意为召唤）和后缀 -ation，指职业或天职，强调内在召唤感。
example: Teaching is her vocation because she loves helping children learn.
教学是她的天职，因为她热爱帮助孩子学习。

words.def_en: related to job skills and training for a specific type of work
words.mnemonic: vocational 基于 vocation（职业），vocation 来自拉丁语 vocare（呼唤），指与职业技能培训相关，常用于教育语境。
example: Vocational training helps people learn the skills needed for their chosen career.
职业培训帮助人们学习所选职业所需的技能。

kaoyan_ex.text: Vocational schools should do a better job of fostering problem-solving skills and helping students work alongside robots.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“职业的”

words.def_en: a unit that measures how strong an electric current is
words.mnemonic: volt 以物理学家 Alessandro Volta 的名字命名 作为电压单位 体现了科学史上的重要贡献
example: The electric fence uses 5,000 volts to keep animals safe.
电围栏使用5000伏电压来保护动物安全。

words.def_en: the force that pushes electricity through a wire, measured in volts
words.mnemonic: voltage 以物理学家 Alessandro Volta 命名，后缀 -age 表示相关状态，指电势差单位伏特，用于电力系统测量。
example: The voltage in this power line is too high for household appliances.
这条电力线的电压对于家用电器来说太高了。

words.def_en: To give most of your time or effort to something or someone. To give something like a book or speech to someone to show love or respect.
words.mnemonic: devote 源于拉丁语 devovere，de- 强调完全，vovere 是发誓，引申为全心投入或奉献于某事。
example: She will devote her time to studying for the exam.
她将把时间用于备考。

kaoyan_ex.text: Yet researchers can take some comfort in the fact that there are a multitude of librarians devoted to discovering, organizing,…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“投入”；常接 to 不定式/介词 to；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: a person who votes in an election
words.mnemonic: voter 源于 vote（投票），后缀 -er 表示人，指参与选举过程的个体，在民主制度中扮演核心角色。
example: Every voter should research candidates before voting.
每位选民在投票前都应研究候选人。

words.def_en: being easily hurt or harmed in body or feelings
words.mnemonic: 词根 vulnerable 来自拉丁语 vulnerabilis，vulnus 意为伤口，后缀 -ability 表示性质，所以 vulnerability 指脆弱性；在 cybersecurity 网络安全领域这个词很关键。
example: The child's vulnerability made her parents very protective.
孩子的脆弱让父母非常保护她。

words.def_en: easily harmed or hurt, either physically or emotionally
words.mnemonic: 拆解词根 vulner- 意为伤口，后缀 -able 表示易受的，指易受伤或脆弱的。
example: Children are vulnerable and need protection from danger.
儿童是脆弱的，需要保护免受危险。

kaoyan_ex.text: Certain artifacts are especially vulnerable because some pioneers in plastic art didn’t always know how to mix ingredients…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“脆弱的”；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: Money you get paid for working, usually every week or month. To start and continue a fight or war.
words.mnemonic: wage 源自古英语 wæge，原义为承诺或报酬，后特指工资，也可作为动词表示进行（如战争），与经济劳动领域密切相关。
example: Her wage is enough to pay for her apartment and food.
她的工资足够支付房租和食物。

kaoyan_ex.text: Taxes on low-wage labor need to be cut, and wage subsidies such as the earned income tax credit should be expanded: This would…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“工资”；常接 to 不定式/介词 to

words.def_en: A bet or a bet involving money. To bet money or to risk something. To confidently state that something will happen or is true, as if betting on it.
words.mnemonic: Wager 来自古法语 wagier，最终源于日耳曼语词根，指打赌或下注的行为，常用于赌博或风险决策中。
example: I made a wager with my friend on who would win the game.
我和朋友打了个赌，看谁能赢得比赛。

words.def_en: A legal paper from a judge that lets police take action. A paper that gives you the right to get money, services, or other benefits. A good reason for doing something. To make something necessary or deserved.
words.mnemonic: warrant 源自古英语 warant，意思是保证或授权，演变到法律术语中表示逮捕令或正当理由。
example: The police got a warrant to search the house.
警方获得了搜查房屋的令状。

words.def_en: a promise from a company to fix or replace a product if it breaks within a certain time
words.mnemonic: 源于古法语 warantie，词根 warant 意为保证，指产品或服务的正式担保，常见于消费法律中。
example: The warranty covers repairs for one year after purchase.
