words.def_en: basic or first level of learning most simple or fundamental very easy to understand
words.mnemonic: elementary 来自拉丁语 elementarius，element 指基础元素，表示初级或基本概念，如 elementary school 代表小学教育。
example: The elementary math class covers simple addition and subtraction.
小学数学课涵盖简单的加减法。

words.def_en: the most basic and important quality of something a strong liquid made from plants that keeps their smell and taste
words.mnemonic: essence 源自拉丁语 essentia，词根 esse 指存在，意思是事物的核心本质，在哲学和香水中都用于表示基础特性。
example: The essence of good teaching is making complex ideas simple.
优秀教学的本质在于将复杂的概念简单化。

words.def_en: in the most basic or important way
words.mnemonic: essentially 源自 essential，其中 essence 本质来自拉丁语 essentia，后缀 -ly 使其副词化，表示本质上或根本上。
example: The two plans are essentially the same, with only minor differences.
这两个计划本质上是相同的，只有细微的差别。

words.def_en: in every important way; completely used to introduce an important point about a topic used to say what is most important about someone or something
words.mnemonic: fundamentally 是 fundamental 的副词形式，fundamental 源于拉丁语 fundamentum (基础)，表示本质上或核心层面的含义。
example: Their views are fundamentally different on this issue.
他们在这个问题上的观点根本不同。

kaoyan_ex.text: Fundamentally, the USPS is in a historic squeeze between technological change that has permanently decreased demand for its…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“根本上”；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: being very important or powerful being extremely good and admired by many
words.mnemonic: greatness 从形容词 great 演变而来，意思是伟大的，加上名词后缀 -ness 表示一种卓越的品质或状态。
example: The leader's greatness came from his ability to unite people.
这位领袖的伟大之处在于他能够团结人民。

words.def_en: The tube in your body where food goes after the stomach. The stomach and other organs inside an animal. A person's stomach, especially when it's big. The courage to do something hard or scary. The place where you feel strong emotions or instincts. The most important part of something. Strong string made from animal intestines, used for instruments and medical tools. To destroy the inside of a building or room. To remove the organs from a fish or animal to cook it. Based on feelings instead of thinking.
words.mnemonic: gut 源于古英语 guttas，原指肠子，俚语中扩展为勇气或直觉，在解剖学中强调消化系统功能。
example: Food can take up to 72 hours to move through your gut.
食物可能需要长达72小时才能通过你的肠道。

words.def_en: The big title of a news story in a newspaper or on a website. A short list of the most important news on radio or TV. To give a news story a title. To be the main performer in a show. Very important. The most popular performers at an event.
words.mnemonic: headline 由 head 指头部和 line 指线条合成，最初表示报纸文章顶部的标题行，用于突出新闻要点。
example: The big news story was the main headline for many days.
这个大新闻故事连续多天占据主要头条。

kaoyan_ex.text: Most Americans rely on social media to check daily headlines.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“新闻标题”

words.def_en: A system where people or things are ranked from highest to lowest. The group of people who control a large organization. A ranking of ideas or beliefs by importance.
words.mnemonic: hierarchy 源自希腊词根 hiero- 表示神圣，结合 -archy 表示统治，最初指神圣的等级制度，后来演变为泛指任何分层体系。
example: In the company hierarchy, managers are above regular employees.
在公司层级中，经理高于普通员工。

words.def_en: very important and urgent showing authority giving an order something very important and urgent the form of a verb used for orders
words.mnemonic: imperative 来自拉丁语 imperativus，imper 命令加后缀 -ative，形容必须的，在语法中表示命令式
example: It is imperative to finish this work today.
今天必须完成这项工作。

words.def_en: so important that you cannot do without it
words.mnemonic: 词根 in 表示不，dis 意思是分开，pensare 指权衡，组合起来指不可或缺的，无法被替代的。
example: Her knowledge of local customs made her indispensable to the team during their international project.
她对当地习俗的了解使她在团队的国际项目中不可或缺。

kaoyan_ex.text: But policies to help workers adapt will be indispensable.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“必不可少”

words.def_en: essential to something; a necessary part built-in; included as part of something complete with all necessary parts
words.mnemonic: integral 源自拉丁语 integer，意思是完整或未受损的，后来在数学中表示积分，引申为整体中不可或缺的部分。
example: Teamwork is integral to our success.
团队合作是我们成功不可或缺的一部分。

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“必不可少的”；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: A main word or idea that is important in a particular situation or topic. A word or phrase you type on a computer or phone to find information or give a command.
words.mnemonic: 由 key 和 word 组合而成，key 意为关键，word 是单词，指在信息检索中起核心作用的术语
example: When you're studying a language, the keyword is patience.
学习语言时，关键是耐心。

words.def_en: able to be measured or counted large enough to be noticed or important
words.mnemonic: measure（测量）加后缀 able，表示可以测量的或可量化的，常用于科学或统计语境。
example: Scientists found measurable levels of pollution in the air.
科学家发现空气中存在可测量的污染水平。

words.def_en: something that must happen or be done; the need for something something you must have to live or work a situation that must happen and cannot be changed
words.mnemonic: necessity 源于拉丁语 necessitas，词根 ne- 表示不，cess- 表示屈服，整体指不可避免的事物，常用于描述必需品或必然性。
example: She bought a car out of necessity because the buses stopped running.
她出于需要买了辆车，因为公交车停运了。

words.def_en: The center of an atom that has most of its mass and a positive charge. The center of a cell that holds the genetic material. The central part of something where other parts gather.
words.mnemonic: nucleus 来自拉丁语，意为内核，源自 nux 坚果，在科学中用于原子核或细胞核。
example: The nucleus of an atom contains protons and neutrons.
原子核包含质子和中子。

words.def_en: extremely good or excellent not yet paid, done, or solved very obvious or important
words.mnemonic: outstanding 由 out 和 standing 合成，out 表示超出，standing 意为站立，组合指杰出的或未解决的事物。
example: She did an outstanding job on her project, earning top marks.
她的项目完成得非常出色，获得了最高分。

words.def_en: to be more important or valuable than something else
words.mnemonic: outweigh 由 out（超过）和 weigh（称重）合成，字面意思是在重量上超过，引申为在重要性或价值上占优势，反映了从物理测量到抽象比较的含义演变。
example: The good points of the plan outweigh the bad ones.
该计划的优点多于缺点。

words.def_en: A point or part that something turns around or balances on. The most important person or thing in a group, situation, or system. To turn or move around a point or to make something do this. To change direction or way of doing something.
words.mnemonic: pivot 源自法语，意为支点或轴心，在机械中表示旋转中心，引申为任何决策或事件的关键转折点。
example: The ballerina spun around on her pivot.
芭蕾舞女演员以脚尖为轴旋转。

words.def_en: best or most important a country's leader, like a prime minister the leader of a Canadian province or territory
words.mnemonic: premier 源于拉丁语 primus 表示第一，在政治中常指总理或首要人物
example: The Premier League is the top football competition in England.
英超联赛是英格兰顶级的足球比赛。

words.def_en: most importantly or mostly
words.mnemonic: primarily 源于拉丁语 primus（第一），后缀 -arily 构成副词，意思是最主要地或首先，强调核心重要性。
example: The company primarily focuses on developing new technology.
该公司主要专注于开发新技术。

words.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“主要地”；常接 to 不定式/介词 to；常见搭配 as

words.def_en: happening or existing before something else more important because it came first before something the leader of a small religious house the second leader in a large religious house
words.mnemonic: prior 直接来自拉丁语 prior 意思是更早或优先的 常用于表示时间或重要性上的先后顺序
example: You need prior experience for this job.
这份工作需要你具备相关经验。

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“先前的”

words.def_en: to arrange things by how important they are and do the most important ones first to consider something more important than other things
words.mnemonic: prioritize 由 priority 优先和 -ize 使动后缀组成，意为将任务或事项列为优先处理。
example: To manage your time effectively, you should prioritize your tasks.
为了有效管理时间，你应该优先处理你的任务。

kaoyan_ex.text: They did not always prioritize the protection of Mauna Kea’s fragile ecosystems or its holiness to the island’s inhabitants.

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“优先处理”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: being important, well known, or easy to see
words.mnemonic: prominence 源自拉丁语 prominere（突出），pro- 向前，minere 伸出，指显著地位或突出特征。
example: The mountain's prominence makes it easy to spot from far away.
这座山的突出使其从远处很容易被看到。

words.def_en: important and well-known easy to see or notice sticking out from a surface
words.mnemonic: prominent 源于拉丁语 prominere，pro- 意为向前，minere 突出，形容显著或著名的事物，如 a prominent scientist。
example: The prominent scientist received an award for her research.
这位杰出的科学家因其研究获得了奖项。

words.def_en: no longer needed for work not needed or useful
words.mnemonic: redundant 来自拉丁语 redundare 溢出，其中 re- 表示再， undare 意为流动，现指多余或重复的部分。
example: The company made many workers redundant after the factory closed.
工厂关闭后，公司解雇了许多工人。

words.def_en: most important or noticeable
words.mnemonic: salient 的词根是拉丁语 salire，表示跳跃，引申为突出或显著的特征，就像事物跃然眼前一样。
example: The most salient feature of the plan is its simplicity.
该计划最显著的特点是它的简单性。

words.def_en: the line of bones in your back the main part that holds something together courage and strength sharp points on plants or animals the back edge of a book where pages are attached
words.mnemonic: 词源是拉丁语 spina，最初指刺或荆棘，含义扩展到动物的脊柱或书的脊背，体现了从具体物体到抽象结构的演变。

一股寒意顺着我的脊背往下窜。

words.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“相当大地”

words.def_en: not having much value or meaning
words.mnemonic: unimportant 由前缀 un 表示否定，加上 important，后者来自拉丁语 importare，意为带来重要性，整体表示不重要的。

这支笔的颜色对于这项任务来说不重要。

words.mnemonic: unnecessarily 由前缀 un- 不、词干 necessary 必需和后缀 -ly 构成，necessary 来自拉丁语 necessarius，意思是不必要地，强调多余或浪费。

她为考试不必要地担心，因为她准备得很充分。

words.def_en: needing immediate attention or action showing that something must be done right away
words.mnemonic: urgent 由 urge 表示强烈催促，后缀 -ent 描述状态，因此指需要立即处理的紧急情况。

这是一件需要立即处理的紧急事务。

words.def_en: very important and needed needed to stay alive full of life and energy

kaoyan_ex.text: …“it’s all in here” as evidence that libraries are less vital for researchers today.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“至关重要的”；常见搭配 for

这个计划对我们来说风险太大，不能尝试。

words.def_en: very easy to see or notice

words.def_en: well-known and respected in a specific field outstanding or excellent

她是一位杰出的科学家，做出了重要的发现。

words.def_en: extremely well-known and respected for achievements
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 illustris，前缀 il 在结合 lustrare 照亮，意为著名或显赫的，常形容杰出人物。

这所大学有着悠久的杰出校友历史，其中包括几位诺贝尔奖得主。

words.def_en: a natural quality that you have from birth
words.mnemonic: inborn 由 in-（内在）和 born（出生）组成，描述天生的特质或本能。
example: Some people have an inborn ability to learn languages quickly.
有些人天生就有快速学习语言的能力。

words.def_en: existing from birth, not learned
words.mnemonic: innate 源自拉丁语 innatus，in- 表示内部，natus 指出生，合起来意为天生固有的特质，无需后天学习。
example: Birds have an innate ability to build nests without being taught.
鸟类天生就有筑巢的能力，无需教导。

words.def_en: having an extremely strong desire for something, especially food or success, that can never be satisfied
words.mnemonic: insatiable 基于拉丁语 in- 不加上 satiare 满足，形容欲望或需求永远无法被填满。

他永不满足的好奇心使他学到了许多新东西。

words.mnemonic: 直接借自德语，kinder 意思是儿童，garten 是花园，组合起来指幼儿园，强调儿童早期教育环境。

我女儿每天早上去幼儿园和朋友们一起玩耍学习，她很喜欢。

我急于完成工作，忽略了那个错误。

这家餐厅以其美味的食物而闻名。

这个令人不安的消息让房间里的每个人都感到焦虑。

乌云带来了一种厄运感。

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“厄运”

我们在院子周围建了木栅栏，以确保狗的安全。

用锤子把钉子钉进木头里。

他的身体残疾使行走困难。

恶劣的天气阻碍了我们的旅行计划。

example: He tried to evade the police by hiding in an alley.
他试图躲在巷子里逃避警察。

words.def_en: to hold something tightly to understand something fully to quickly take an opportunity a firm hold on something understanding of something the ability to achieve something
words.mnemonic: grasp 源于古英语 græppian，指用手抓住，也引申为理解或掌握概念
example: He tried to grasp the rope firmly.
他试图紧紧抓住绳子。

words.def_en: holding something tightly control or power over someone or something understanding of something ability to not slip on a surface part made to be held easily hair clip for women camera equipment worker in films large travel bag hold something tightly interest or affect someone strongly have a strong effect on someone or something hold or move without slipping
words.mnemonic: grip 源自古英语 gripan，意为抓住或紧握，词源与德语 greifen 相关，既指物理上的把握，也比喻控制力。
example: Make sure your grip on the handle is firm.
确保你牢牢握住把手。

words.def_en: not based on or using reason or good judgment
words.mnemonic: 前缀 il- 表示否定，加上 logical 源于希腊语 logos（逻辑），意思是不合逻辑的或不合理的，在辩论中常用于指出推理错误。
example: It was illogical to think that we could finish the project in just one day.
认为我们能在一天内完成这个项目是不合逻辑的。

words.def_en: A person who is an expert in logic, which is the study of reasoning and thinking.
words.mnemonic: logician 由 logic 和后缀 -ian 组成，logic 源于希腊语 logos 表示 '理性' 或 '话语'，指专门研究逻辑推理的学者。
example: The logician presented a complex argument, but managed to explain it in a way that was easy to understand.
逻辑学家提出了一个复杂的论点，但设法以一种易于理解的方式解释了它。

kaoyan_ex.text: …attempts by the Church to suppress this new generation of logicians and rationalists, more explanations for how the universe functioned were being…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“逻辑学家”；常见搭配 for

words.def_en: A hard stone that is often white with colored lines, used for buildings and statues. A small glass ball used in children's games. A game played with small glass balls. A way to say someone's mental ability or sanity.
words.mnemonic: marble 起源于希腊语 marmaros，意为闪亮的石头，现在指建筑用大理石或儿童玩的弹珠游戏。
example: The floor was made of shiny marble.
地板是闪亮的大理石做的。

kaoyan_ex.text: Why are people who live within a day’s drive of London entitled to go and see the Elgin Marbles whenever they want, but the…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“大理石”

words.def_en: done without thinking and without any particular reason not requiring any thought or intelligence not thinking about or considering something
words.mnemonic: mindless 来自 mind 意为心智，加上 less 后缀表示缺乏，整体形容无意识或愚蠢的行为，常用于批评盲目跟从。
example: The act of graffiti by mindless vandals.
无脑破坏者的涂鸦行为。

words.def_en: ideas about what is right and wrong in how people act how right or wrong something is based on moral rules a set of moral rules that a group follows
words.mnemonic: Morality 来自 moral 意为道德的，加上 -ity 后缀表示状态，指道德规范或伦理准则。
example: People worry that morality is not as strong as it used to be.
人们担心道德不像过去那样强大了。

words.def_en: hard to understand or explain seeming strange or secret strange and interesting because not well known not telling much when others want to know more
words.mnemonic: mysterious 来自希腊语 mysterion，拆解为 mystery（神秘）和 -ous（性质），表示难以理解或充满谜团。
example: The mysterious illness spread quickly through the village.
这种神秘的疾病迅速在村庄里传播开来。

words.def_en: to go into or through something to enter a group or market successfully to see or show a way through something to understand something difficult to be understood by someone to enter the body during sex
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 penetrare 进入，指穿透或深入某物，常用于描述光线或思想影响。
example: The cold air can penetrate through thick clothing.
冷空气能穿透厚衣服。

words.def_en: a person who studies or writes about big ideas and how we think a person who thinks deeply about life and ideas
words.mnemonic: philosopher 由希腊语 philo（爱）和 sophia（智慧）组合而成，意思是爱智慧的人，如历史上的苏格拉底。
example: The philosopher wrote many books about how to live a good life.
这位哲学家写了许多关于如何过上好生活的书。

words.def_en: to think deeply about something
words.mnemonic: ponder 来自拉丁语 ponderare，意为衡量或深思，常用于表达仔细思考的过程。
example: I need to ponder this decision carefully before choosing.
在做选择之前，我需要仔细考虑这个决定。

kaoyan_ex.text: Have you pondered the life cycle of intangible formats, digital information, given that those who produce these artifacts…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“深思”；常见搭配 of；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: to think something is true without proof to accept something as true until proven false, especially in law to act as if something is true or exists to act too boldly or without proper respect
words.mnemonic: presume 来自拉丁语 praesumere，其中 prae- 表示 '前'，sumere 意为 '拿取'，组合起来是 '预先拿取' 的意思，引申为 '假定' 或 '推测'。
example: I presume you know the way since you've been here before.
我假定你知道路，因为你以前来过这里。

words.def_en: thinking logically to form ideas or reach conclusions
words.mnemonic: 由 reason 推理和 ing 动作后缀构成，指逻辑思考的过程，强调从前提导出结论的思维活动。
example: Her reasoning helped solve the problem by breaking it into smaller parts.
她的推理通过将问题分解成更小的部分帮助解决了问题。

kaoyan_ex.text: It is a flawed line of reasoning to argue against returning artifacts to their countries of origin.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“推理”；常接 to 不定式/介词 to；常见搭配 against；以 -ing 形式出现

words.def_en: a slow-cooked dish with meat and/or vegetables in liquid to cook food slowly in liquid in a closed dish to worry or think deeply about something
words.mnemonic: stew 来自古法语 estuver，原义蒸煮，现在指慢炖的菜肴，体现烹饪方法。
example: I'm making a hearty beef stew for dinner tonight.
今晚晚餐我要做一道丰盛的炖牛肉。

words.def_en: based on ideas and thinking, not on real tests or practice possible but not likely to happen or be true
words.mnemonic: theoretical 基于 theory 理论，后缀 ical 表示相关，指理论上的，科学研究中区分理论与实际应用。
example: The first year gives students a strong theoretical foundation for later study.
第一年为学生后续学习打下坚实的理论基础。

words.def_en: To think of or suggest ideas about what might be true or possible.
words.mnemonic: theorize 基于 theory 希腊语 theoria 本义是沉思观察 -ize 后缀表示使动 意为形成理论或推测 科学家常用这个词描述假说构建过程
example: Scientists often theorize about discoveries that could change our understanding of the world.
科学家们常常对可能改变我们世界观的发现进行理论推测。

kaoyan_ex.text: Copernicus theorized in 1543 that all of the planets that we knew of revolved not around the Earth, but the Sun, a system that…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“推测”；后接 that 从句；常见搭配 of；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: to make something worse to annoy someone
words.mnemonic: aggravate 前缀 ag- 加强语气，词根 grav 来自拉丁语 gravis 表示重，后缀 -ate 使动词化，意思是使情况变重或恶化，常用于描述问题加剧。
example: Smoking can aggravate breathing problems.
吸烟会加剧呼吸问题。

words.def_en: able to be understood in more than one way not clear or certain
words.mnemonic: ambiguous 来自拉丁语 ambiguus，ambi- 表示两者，agere 驱动，意思是模棱两可的或含糊不清的。
example: The ambiguous instructions confused everyone.
含糊不清的指示让所有人都感到困惑。

words.def_en: to hold something tightly with your hand to hold someone or something tightly with your arms to fasten something with a clasp a device that fastens something, like a bag or jewelry a tight hold with your hand or arms
words.mnemonic: clasp 可能来自古英语 clæpsan 表示抓住，描述扣子或紧握的动作，常用于珠宝或固定装置的设计。
example: She used a clasp to secure the necklace around her neck.
她用扣环把项链固定在脖子上。

words.def_en: to think of an idea or plan to imagine something to become pregnant with a baby
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 concipere，con- 一起 和 capere 拿或抓住，原意是怀孕或构思，引申为形成想法或计划。
example: It's hard to conceive a better solution than this one.
很难想出比这个更好的解决方案。

words.def_en: a small bed for a baby that rocks gently the place where something important started a small platform that moves up and down a building for cleaning windows the part of a phone where the handset rests to hold something gently in your arms or hands
words.mnemonic: cradle 源自古英语 cradol，指婴儿摇篮，引申为某事物的起源地
example: The baby slept soundly in the cradle.
婴儿在摇篮里睡得很香。

words.def_en: having two parts or aspects
words.mnemonic: dual 源自拉丁语 duo 表示二，因此它的意思是双重的，常用于描述 dual-core processor 等双核技术。
example: The device has dual cameras for better photos.
该设备配备双摄像头，可拍摄更好的照片。

words.def_en: to make a situation or problem more severe
words.mnemonic: exacerbate 来自拉丁语 exacerbare 使更尖锐，描述使问题或矛盾恶化的行为。
example: The heavy rain exacerbated the flooding issue in the city.
大雨加剧了城市的洪涝问题。

kaoyan_ex.text: …the angry inhabitants; between the British, ever keen to exacerbate the emperor’s difficulties, and the marshals sent from Paris to try to keep them…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“加剧”

words.def_en: a hand closed tightly with fingers bent into the palm
words.mnemonic: fist 是一个简单词，直接描述握紧的手形成拳头的形状。
example: He made a fist to show his strength.
他握紧拳头以显示自己的力量。

words.def_en: relating to a type of philosophy that explores the basic nature of reality
words.mnemonic: 前缀 meta-（超越）加上 physical（物理的），源于希腊哲学，指研究超越物质世界的抽象领域。
example: The discussion of life after death is a metaphysical topic that has intrigued philosophers for centuries.
关于死后生命的讨论是一个形而上学的主题，几个世纪以来一直吸引着哲学家们。

words.def_en: to make a hole in something with a sharp point to be suddenly seen or heard clearly to break through something that blocks the way
words.mnemonic: pierce 来自古法语 percer，指穿透或刺入的动作，常用于描述 piercing 如身体穿刺艺术。
example: The needle will pierce the fabric easily.
针会轻易刺穿布料。

words.def_en: an idea or statement that is the starting point for an argument or theory
words.mnemonic: premise 源自拉丁语 praemissa，prae- 指在前，mittere 意为发送，最初指放在前面的论点，现可表示逻辑前提或房产。
example: The main premise of the story is that love can overcome any obstacle.
故事的主要前提是爱可以克服任何障碍。

kaoyan_ex.text: The premise was that the common law of contract lacked sufficient safeguards for workers against arbitrary conduct by management.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“前提”；后接 that 从句；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: to move in a circle around a center point
words.mnemonic: revolve 包含前缀 re- 表示重复，和词根 volve 来自拉丁语 volvere，意为旋转或循环。
example: The planets revolve around the sun in our solar system.
在我们的太阳系中，行星围绕太阳运转。

kaoyan_ex.text: As a librarian whose day job revolves around special collections and digital assets, I share the night terrors of historians,…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“旋转”

words.def_en: A puzzle or question with a clever answer that you ask as a game. Something mysterious or hard to explain. To make many holes in something.
words.mnemonic: riddle 这里指谜语，来自古英语 rædels，意为需解开的难题，常与逻辑游戏关联。
example: Can you solve this riddle: I speak without a mouth and hear without ears. What am I?
你能解开这个谜语吗：我没有嘴巴却能说话，没有耳朵却能听见。我是什么？

words.def_en: strikingly strange or mysterious, causing a feeling of unease
words.mnemonic: uncanny 由前缀 un- 表示否定和 canny 组成，canny 源于苏格兰语意为精明，整体引申为怪异或超自然的体验。
example: The uncanny resemblance between the twins was unsettling.
这对双胞胎惊人的相似令人不安。

words.def_en: lacking written proof or records lacking official papers, especially for living and working in another country
words.mnemonic: 前缀 un- 表示否定，documented 是有文件的，因此 undocumented 指无证明文件的，特别用于描述无证移民。
example: The claim was dismissed as undocumented.
该说法因无文件证明而被驳回。

words.def_en: impossible to understand or know
words.mnemonic: 由前缀 un 不加上 knowable 可知道的构成，表示超出人类认知范围，无法被了解的事物。
example: The mysteries of the universe are considered unknowable by many scientists.
宇宙的奥秘被许多科学家认为是不可知的。

rows.def_en: to warn someone about danger or something that needs quick action to make someone notice or aware of something a state of watching carefully for danger and being ready to act a warning about danger or a problem a signal from a device to inform or remind you of something quick to notice things and think clearly aware of something, especially possible danger
rows.mnemonic: 源自意大利语 all'erta，意为在警戒中，因此 alert 表示警觉的或警告。安全设备如 smoke alert 系统能及时发出警报。
example: The system will alert you if there is a fire in the building.
如果大楼内发生火灾，系统会向你发出警报。

rows.def_en: to say something is true without showing proof
rows.mnemonic: allege 源于拉丁语 allegare 意思是声称或断言，常用于法律语境中表示未经证实的指控。
example: The company will allege that the employee stole money, but they have no evidence yet.
公司将指控该员工偷钱，但他们还没有证据。

rows.def_en: To talk about something without saying it directly. To hint at something without saying it clearly.
rows.mnemonic: allude 源自拉丁语 alludere，其中 ad- 表示向，ludere 意为玩，因此是间接提及或暗示某事而不直接说明。
example: He alluded to the problem without giving details.
他暗示了这个问题，但没有提供细节。

kaoyan_ex.text: “Nature gave us lips to conceal our teeth,” ran one popular Victorian saying, alluding to the fact that before the birth of…

rows.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“间接提及”；后接 that 从句；以 -ing 形式出现

rows.mnemonic: 作为拟声词模仿爆炸声；经济上表示繁荣或快速增长。
example: The city had a big boom after new factories opened.
新工厂开业后，这座城市经历了大繁荣。

kaoyan_ex.text: Some will say the audiobook boom revives it, though I suppose you can then worry about the decline of reading.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“繁荣期”

rows.def_en: A short fight between two groups. A strong argument between people with different ideas. A big difference between two opposing things. When two events happen at the same time. A loud noise when two metal objects hit. A game or match between two teams. When two colors or designs look bad together. To fight or compete with someone. To argue strongly with someone. To be very different from each other. To happen at the same time as something else. To look bad when put together. To hit together and make a loud noise.
rows.mnemonic: clash 可能源于拟声词，模仿金属碰撞的声音，现在描述冲突或意见不合，常见于文化或政治讨论。
example: A clash happened between police and protesters.
警察和抗议者之间发生了冲突。

rows.def_en: to admit something is true after first saying it was not to admit you lost a game or election to give something to someone, often when you do not want to
rows.mnemonic: Concede 来自拉丁语 concedere，con- 一起，cedere 让步，意思是承认失败或允许对方观点。
example: After arguing, I had to concede that his idea was better.
争论之后，我不得不承认他的想法更好。

kaoyan_ex.text: Of course, I need to concede that my collection of “Smiling Victorians” makes up only a tiny percentage of the vast catalogue…

rows.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“承认”；后接 that 从句；常见搭配 of

rows.def_en: to admit you did something wrong or illegal to admit something you feel bad about to tell God or a priest about bad things you did to be forgiven to listen when someone tells their sins
rows.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 confiteri，con- 表示完全，fateri 意为承认，整体指坦白或忏悔的行为。
example: He had to confess his mistake to the teacher.
他不得不向老师承认自己的错误。

rows.def_en: words that show you are happy for someone's good luck or success what you say to someone to show you are happy for them the act of telling someone you are happy for their success
rows.mnemonic: congratulation 来自拉丁语 congratulari，con- 表示共同，gratulari 意为庆贺，所以整体表达对他人成功的祝贺。
example: I sent my congratulations to my friend for winning the award.
我向我的朋友表示祝贺，因为他赢得了奖项。

rows.def_en: Designed for or involving informal talk, not formal. Relating to the act of talking in a normal way.
rows.mnemonic: 来自 converse 交谈，con- 前缀表示一起，verse 词根意为转向，形容健谈或会话式的
example: She picked up conversational phrases quickly during her stay abroad.
她在国外期间很快学会了日常会话用语。

rows.def_en: a long soft seat for many people a long bed-like seat, especially in a doctor's room to say or write something in a certain way
rows.mnemonic: couch 源自法语 coucher 躺卧，在中文中直接音译为沙发，常用于指代供休息的长椅。
example: The family sat together on the big couch to watch a movie.
一家人一起坐在大沙发上看电影。

rows.def_en: A public meeting or march where people show they are against or for something. Showing or explaining how to do something. Proof or evidence that shows something is true. Showing how you feel or what you think about something.
rows.mnemonic: 源自拉丁语 demonstrare，前缀 de-（完全）和 monstrare（展示），意思是公开展示，在抗议活动中常见如 street demonstration。
example: The large demonstration in the city center showed strong public support for the new policy.
市中心的大型示威活动显示了公众对新政策的强烈支持。

rows.def_en: to carefully make or prepare something with attention to details to express ideas clearly using carefully chosen words
rows.mnemonic: formulate 的词根 form 表示形式，后缀 -ulate 表示制作，意为系统阐述或制定计划，常用于科学或政策领域。
example: Scientists formulate new medicines to treat diseases effectively.
科学家们配制新药以有效治疗疾病。

kaoyan_ex.text: Next time you state your position, formulate an argument for what you claim and honestly ask yourself whether your argument is…

rows.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“精心制定”；常见搭配 for

rows.def_en: Too much worry or activity over small things Getting upset or complaining about unimportant things To spend time on small, unimportant things To worry too much about small things
rows.mnemonic: fuss 可能源于拟声词，模仿忙乱时的声响，现在表示小题大做或喧闹。
example: There was a big fuss about the small mistake.
那个小错误引起了一场大骚动。

rows.def_en: to make a deep sound when annoyed, upset, in pain, or with pleasure to complain in an annoying way to make a sound like a groan a deep sound made when groaning a complaint
rows.mnemonic: 来自古英语 granian，描述因痛苦、不满或压力发出的低沉声音。
example: Everyone groaned at his bad joke.
他讲了个冷笑话，大家都抱怨起来。

rows.def_en: a short official note sent between people in the same organization a written record of an agreement before the final documents are signed a detailed report or proposal on a specific topic for an organization or committee
rows.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 memorare，意思是需要记住的东西，指备忘录，常缩写为 memo，在办公环境中用于记录重要事项。
example: The manager sent a memorandum to all staff about the new office hours.
经理向所有员工发送了一份关于新办公时间的备忘录。

rows.def_en: to make a long, low sound because of pain, sadness, or pleasure to complain about something in an annoying way to make a long, low sound a long, low sound made because of pain, sadness, or pleasure a complaint about something a long, low sound, like the wind makes
rows.mnemonic: 源自古英语 mān，指因痛苦、悲伤或不满发出的低沉声音，常用于表达情感宣泄。
example: The hurt man let out a moan as the doctor checked his leg.
受伤的男子在医生检查他的腿时发出呻吟。

rows.def_en: Not speaking or making sound. Unable to speak. A button that turns off sound on devices. A device that makes musical instruments quieter. A person who cannot speak (old term). To turn off the sound. To make a musical instrument quieter. To make something less strong or clear.
rows.mnemonic: mute 来自拉丁语 mutus，意为沉默的或哑的，在音乐中用作弱音器，表示降低声音强度的装置。
example: The child sat mute in the corner, not saying a word.
那个孩子坐在角落里一言不发，一声不吭。

rows.def_en: to speak quietly in a low voice that is hard to hear, often when annoyed to complain quietly without saying it openly a quiet sound or words that are hard to hear
rows.mnemonic: 源自古英语 mutian，描述低声抱怨的行为，常用于表达不满或私语。
example: He would mutter complaints under his breath when he was upset.
他心烦时总会低声抱怨。

rows.def_en: to say that you are or have something, even if it is not true the main meaning or idea of something
rows.mnemonic: 词根来自拉丁语 portare 意思是携带，前缀 pur- 表示意图，purport 指声称或表达的主要意思。

雏鸟会羽翼丰满，然后就能飞走了。

该公司使用空运快速发送包裹。

rows.def_en: to feel with your hands to find something you cannot see to move by feeling with your hands when you cannot see well to touch someone sexually without their consent an unwanted sexual touch

他不得不在黑暗的房间里摸索着找电灯开关。

rows.def_en: to jump on one foot to jump with both feet together to go somewhere quickly to get on a vehicle to change quickly between things a short jump on one foot a short jump with both feet a short trip a climbing plant dried flowers used for beer a casual dance party

words.mnemonic: abolish 来自拉丁语 abolere，意思是废除或取消，在历史语境中常用于讨论废除奴隶制等社会变革。
example: Many people want to abolish this unfair tax.
许多人想要废除这项不公平的税收。

words.def_en: a metal made by mixing two or more metals together to mix metals together to make a new metal
words.mnemonic: 词根可追溯至拉丁语 alligare，意思是结合，指两种或多种金属混合形成的材料，体现融合的概念。
example: Steel is an alloy made from iron and carbon.
钢是由铁和碳制成的合金。

words.def_en: To break open suddenly from inside pressure. To move or come out suddenly with force. To be so full that something might break open. A sudden short period of activity or emotion. A break or hole from something bursting. A series of quick shots from a gun.
words.mnemonic: burst 是古英语单词，意思突然破裂，物理学中描述能量爆发如超新星爆炸。
example: The balloon will burst if you blow too much air into it.
如果你吹太多气进去，气球会爆裂。

words.def_en: A mixed drink made with alcohol and other ingredients like juice. A cold dish made of small pieces of mixed food. A mixture of different things that don't usually go together.
words.mnemonic: cocktail 词源模糊，可能源于混合饮料，涉及公鸡尾巴或其他元素，常与鸡尾酒会文化联系，象征社交和创意调配。
example: I ordered a refreshing cocktail at the beach bar.
我在海滩酒吧点了一杯清爽的鸡尾酒。

words.def_en: causing great damage or failure
words.mnemonic: 来自希腊语 disastros，拆解为 dis-（坏的）和 aster（星），源于占星学中凶星带来厄运的观念，引申为灾难性的后果。
example: The disastrous storm destroyed many homes and left people without power.
这场灾难性的风暴摧毁了许多房屋，导致人们断电。

words.def_en: very beautiful or carefully made very strong feeling very sensitive or refined
words.mnemonic: exquisite 来自拉丁语 exquisitus，前缀 ex- 意为出，词根 quaerere 意为寻求，原指精心寻求的，演变为精致或优美。
example: The exquisite jewelry was made with great care.
这件精美的珠宝制作得非常用心。

words.def_en: in a way that is very beautiful or detailed in a way that is very sensitive or noticeable in a very delicate or refined manner
words.mnemonic: exquisitely 是 exquisite 的副词形式，exquisite 源自拉丁语 exquirere，意为精心挑选的，表达极其精美或细致。
example: The vase was exquisitely painted with delicate flowers.
这个花瓶上精美地绘制了 delicate 的花朵。

words.def_en: to make someone happy or satisfied to fulfill a desire or need
words.mnemonic: 词根 grat 来自拉丁语 gratus 意为高兴的，后缀 -ify 表示使动，意思是使满足或取悦，如 gratify one's desires 指满足欲望。
example: It gratified him to see his team win the championship.
看到自己的团队赢得冠军，他感到欣慰。

words.def_en: a state of great damage, destruction, or confusion
words.mnemonic: 单词 havoc 源自中古英语，可能来自古法语的 havot，意指掠夺或破坏，它描述了事物陷入大规模混乱的状态。
example: The storm created havoc in the city, damaging buildings and flooding streets.
暴风雨在城市中造成了严重破坏，损坏了建筑物，淹没了街道。

words.def_en: to mix or combine things together to move around and talk to people at a social event
words.mnemonic: Mingle 源自中古英语 mengen，意指混合或社交互动，常出现在聚会场景中体现人际交往的融合。
example: At the party, people mingle and talk with each other.
在聚会上，人们互相交流交谈。

words.def_en: a small gun that you hold and fire with one hand
words.mnemonic: pistol 可能来自法语 pistole，指小型手持枪械。在历史中，这个词常用于描述武器设计，如早期手枪。
example: He carried a pistol for protection when walking alone at night.
他随身携带手枪，以便夜间独行时自卫。

words.def_en: A person who works at an airport to check passengers and their belongings for security purposes.
words.mnemonic: 由 screen 派生，指用于筛选信息或显示图像的设备或人，如电影筛选员或电子屏幕。
example: The screener at the airport carefully examined the passengers' luggage to ensure safety.
机场安检员仔细检查乘客的行李以确保安全。

kaoyan_ex.text: …in airline travel, so the TSA is now rushing to get new screeners on the line.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“安检员”；常见搭配 on

words.def_en: To shake a little because of cold, fear, or excitement. A quick shake of the body from cold, fear, or excitement. Body shaking from fear or fever.
words.mnemonic: shiver 可能源自古英语 cifer，描述身体因寒冷、恐惧或激动而轻微颤抖。
example: She started to shiver when she heard the scary noise.
听到可怕的声音时，她开始发抖。

words.def_en: advanced and complex in design or function worldly and cultured with good taste able to understand complex ideas easily
words.mnemonic: sophisticated 源于希腊语 sophos（智慧的），经过拉丁语演变，指高度复杂或世故的，如 sophisticated technology。
example: The new smartphone has a sophisticated camera system that takes amazing photos.
这款新智能手机拥有精密的摄像头系统，能拍出令人惊叹的照片。

kaoyan_ex.text: …one thing I’ve learnt is that while it is the enchantingly sophisticated technologies that get all the hype, it’s the cheap technologies that change…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“精密的”；后接 that 从句；以 -ed 形式出现

words.def_en: to write down or type words that someone said or that are in a document to write down the sounds of speech using a special system of symbols to change music so it can be played by a different instrument or sung by a different voice
words.mnemonic: 前缀 trans- 表示跨越，词根 scribe 意为写，指将内容从一种形式抄写到另一种，如音乐改编或 DNA 转录。
example: She had to transcribe her notes from the meeting into a formal report.
她不得不把会议笔记誊写成正式报告。

kaoyan_ex.text: At the same time, Dickens, who had a reporter’s eye for transcribing the life around him, especially anything comic or odd,…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“笔录”；以 -ing 形式出现

words.def_en: to break a law or rule to disturb someone's peace or privacy to damage a holy place to force someone to have sex
words.mnemonic: violate 来自拉丁语 violare 侵犯，词根与 vis 力量相关，意思是以武力破坏规则或权利。
example: They violate the speed limit by driving too fast.
他们超速行驶，违反了限速规定。

kaoyan_ex.text: …AI-directed weapons or use AI for surveillance that would violate international norms.

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“违反”

words.def_en: to become worse or make something worse
words.mnemonic: 从 worse 更坏派生，加后缀 en 表示使成，意为使情况恶化或变得更糟。
example: If you don't take medicine, your cold may worsen.
如果你不吃药，感冒可能会加重。

kaoyan_ex.text: “Short-termism,” or the desire for quick profits, has worsened in publicly traded companies, says the Bank of England’s top…

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“恶化”；常见搭配 in；以 -ed 形式出现

rows.def_en: connected with the way ideas or things are linked together in your mind in math, describing an operation that works the same way no matter how you group the numbers, like (a times b) times c equals a times (b times c)
rows.mnemonic: associative 来自 associate，词根 soci 表示同伴或联合，强调事物之间形成联想或连接的特性。
example: The game helps children make associative connections between words and pictures.
这个游戏帮助孩子们在单词和图片之间建立联想。

rows.def_en: A file sent with an email. Connecting one thing to another. A feeling of love or strong liking. Belief in an idea or value. A tool added to a machine for a special job. A short time working with a group or place.
rows.mnemonic: attach 源于古法语 attachier 意为固定，后缀 -ment 表示结果，指连接物或情感上的依恋。
example: Please send the document as an email attachment.
请将文档作为电子邮件附件发送。

kaoyan_ex.text: This mutual gaze is a major part of the attachment between mother and child.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“附件”

rows.def_en: able to govern itself able to act independently able to operate without human control
rows.mnemonic: 来自希腊语 autonomos，auto- 表示自己，nomos 表示法律，合起来指自我管理的，常用于描述自动驾驶汽车或独立系统。
example: The autonomous region makes its own laws.
自治区制定自己的法律。

kaoyan_ex.text: The coming use of autonomous vehicles, for example, poses thorny ethical questions.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“自治的”；常见搭配 for

rows.def_en: to tie someone or something tightly with rope or string to wrap cloth around something to unite people or groups closely together to force someone to do something by promise or duty to stick things together into one mass to fasten pages into a book cover to sew decorative or strengthening edges a difficult situation that is hard to escape
rows.mnemonic: bind 来自古英语 bindan，意为捆绑或约束，词根与印欧语系连接概念相关。
example: They used rope to bind his hands together.
他们用绳子把他的双手绑在一起。

rows.def_en: A word that connects words, phrases, or sentences, like 'and', 'but', 'or', or 'because'. A mix of events that leads to a specific outcome. When stars or planets appear close together in the sky from Earth.
rows.mnemonic: conjunction 来自拉丁语 coniunctio，词根 con-（一起）和 iungere（连接），表示结合或联合，如语法中连接词句的连词。
example: The conjunction 'and' joins two ideas together in a sentence.
连词“and”在句子中连接两个想法。

rows.def_en: A relationship in which a person, thing, or idea is linked or associated with something else. A means of joining or linking things together, such as a physical link or a transport link.
example: There is a strong connexion between regular exercise and improved mental health.
定期锻炼与改善心理健康之间有着密切的联系。

rows.def_en: to make something stronger or more secure to combine things into one
rows.mnemonic: consolidate 的词根 con- 表示一起，solid 来自 solidus 指坚固，合起来意为使组织或资源更稳固或合并。
example: The company consolidated its market position by acquiring smaller competitors.
该公司通过收购较小的竞争对手巩固了其市场地位。

kaoyan_ex.text: They infused some with stabilizing and consolidating chemicals.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“巩固”；以 -ing 形式出现

rows.def_en: to remove or separate something from something else to separate yourself from someone or something emotionally to send a group of people away from a larger group for a special task
rows.mnemonic: detach 源自法语 détacher，由 de-（表示远离）和 tach（源于 attach，意为附着）组合，意思是脱离连接或分开。
example: You can detach the keyboard from the tablet when you don't need it.
不需要时，你可以将键盘从平板电脑上拆下。

rows.def_en: separate and not connected to other things
rows.mnemonic: discrete 源自拉丁语 discretus，词根 dis- 表示分离，cret 来自 cernere 意为区分，整体指可分开的或独立的，常用于数学或逻辑中。
example: The data points are discrete and do not form a continuous line.
这些数据点是离散的，不形成连续线。

rows.def_en: To separate or release something that is connected or held together. To stop being involved in a conflict or argument.
rows.mnemonic: 前缀 dis- 表示分离 词根 engage 来自法语 engager 意为参与 disengage 指主动脱离或断开连接 常用于机械或人际关系
example: She carefully disengaged the clasp on her necklace.
她小心地解开了项链上的搭扣。

rows.def_en: the legal end of a marriage the separation of two things that were connected to legally end a marriage to separate one thing from another
rows.mnemonic: divorce 源于拉丁语 divortium，表示婚姻关系的正式解除或分离。
example: After the divorce, they both started new lives.
离婚后，他们都开始了新生活。

rows.def_en: A place in a port where ships are fixed or where things are loaded and unloaded. A group of docks and the buildings around them used for fixing ships and storing goods. A wall or platform by water where boats can be tied and people can get on and off. A raised area for loading trucks or trains. The place in a court where the person accused of a crime stands. A wild plant with big leaves that can help with nettle stings. A device that connects a laptop or phone to power or other devices. When a ship arrives and stays at a harbor, or to bring a ship there. When two spacecraft join together in space, or to join them. To take money from someone's pay. To connect a computer to a docking station. To cut an animal's tail short.
rows.mnemonic: dock 源于古英语 docce，指码头或船坞，也引申为扣减工资，在科技领域 docker 容器技术与此相关。
example: The ship was in the dock for repairs.
船在船坞里进行修理。

rows.def_en: A group of states that work together as one country but keep some local control. A group of clubs or groups that join together to work as one. The act of joining separate groups into one larger group.
rows.mnemonic: 单词 federation 源自拉丁语 foedus 意为条约或联盟，加上后缀 -ation 表示组织状态，指多个群体联合成的联邦体系。
example: The Russian Federation is a large country made up of many states.
俄罗斯联邦是一个由许多州组成的大国。

rows.def_en: a break in a bone or hard material the breaking of something, especially a bone to break or crack something to split into parts or divide a group
rows.mnemonic: 单词 fracture 来自拉丁语 fractura，意为打破，指骨骼或物体的断裂，在医学中常用于描述骨折情况。
example: The doctor found a fracture in his arm after the fall.
摔倒后，医生发现他的手臂骨折了。

rows.def_en: A place where two or more roads or railway lines come together. A place where two or more things connect or join together.
rows.mnemonic: junction 来自拉丁语 iunctio，iungere 表示连接，指道路或铁路的交汇点。
example: Be careful when driving through the junction where the main roads meet.
在主干道交汇处开车时要小心。

rows.def_en: to make clothes or fabric by looping yarn with needles to make a basic stitch in knitting to connect people or things closely to heal and join together, like broken bones clothing made by knitting
rows.mnemonic: knit 源于古英语 cnyttan，表示打结或编织的动作，常用于描述毛衣制作的过程，词根与 knot 相关，强调连接和构建。
example: She likes to knit warm sweaters for winter.
她喜欢织冬天穿的暖和的毛衣。

rows.def_en: in a way that relates to or involves relationships between people or things in terms of how things are connected or compared to each other in a manner characteristic of relational databases or systems
example: The two concepts are connected relationally rather than causally.
这两个概念是关联性的而非因果性的。

rows.def_en: a separate part of something a section of fruit like an orange or lemon a part of a circle cut by a line the smallest sound in a word to divide into parts
rows.mnemonic: segment 词根 seg- 源于拉丁语，意为切割，后缀 -ment 指结果或部分，表示被划分出来的片段，常用于数据分析或生物学。
example: The orange was cut into equal segments for everyone to share.
橙子被切成相等的瓣，供大家分享。

rows.def_en: to put flour or another fine substance through a sieve to look through something carefully to find what is useful or important to separate something from a group
rows.mnemonic: 词根源于古英语 siftan，与 sieve 相关，描述筛选或过滤的动作，常用于比喻仔细检查信息。
example: Sift the flour into the bowl.
把面粉筛进碗里。

kaoyan_ex.text: This was an attempt to recover the valuable nails, which could be reused after sifting the ashes.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“筛”；以 -ing 形式出现

rows.def_en: to come together as one group for a common purpose to bring people or things together into one whole
rows.mnemonic: unite 源自拉丁语 unire，词根 unus 表示一个，-ire 是动词后缀，整体意为联合或统一，强调团结概念，常用于社会运动。
example: The community will unite to clean up the park this weekend.
社区本周末将联合起来清理公园。

rows.def_en: working together as one looking complete and natural rules for plays to have one story, one day, one place one thing made of many parts the number one
rows.mnemonic: unity 的词源是拉丁语 unitas，源自 unus 意思是一。这个词强调团结或整体性，演变中常用于描述社会或艺术中的和谐。
example: The team showed great unity in achieving their goal.
团队在实现目标的过程中表现出了极大的团结。

rows.def_en: To stick pieces of metal together by heating and pressing them. To bring people or things together in a strong, unified way. A place where two pieces of metal have been welded together.
rows.mnemonic: weld 指通过高温融合金属的方法，源自古英语表示结合或连接。
example: In the workshop, we learned how to weld two pieces of metal.
在车间里，我们学习了如何焊接两块金属。

rows.def_en: A heavy object that holds a ship in place. Someone or something that makes you feel safe. A person who presents news on TV or radio. To drop an anchor to stop a boat from moving. To fix something firmly in place. To base something on something else. To present news on TV or radio.
rows.mnemonic: 来自希腊语 ankura，指船锚这种固定装置，象征稳定和安全，在新闻领域也引申为主持人的角色。
example: The ship dropped its anchor to stay in one spot.
船抛下锚以停留在原地。

rows.def_en: a strip of cloth used to cover and protect a wound to wrap a wound with a bandage
rows.mnemonic: band 带子和后缀 -age 表示物品，bandage 指用于包扎伤口的绷带，其词根源于法语 bande 带子。
example: She put a clean bandage on the cut to keep it safe.
她在伤口上贴了一块干净的绷带以保护它。

rows.def_en: a small broken piece from something larger an incomplete part of something to break into small pieces
rows.mnemonic: fragment 由 frag- 打破和 -ment 组成，指碎片或断裂的部分。
example: The glass broke into many small fragments on the floor.
玻璃杯掉在地上碎成了许多小碎片。

kaoyan_ex.text: …intensive chemical farming has reduced many species to tiny fragments of habitat and small nature reserves.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“碎片”；常见搭配 of

rows.def_en: A sticky material that holds things together. To stick things together using glue.
rows.mnemonic: glue 来自古法语 glu，源于拉丁语 gluten，意为粘合剂，用于粘贴物体或象征紧密连接。
example: Use glue to stick the paper pieces together.
用胶水把纸片粘在一起。

rows.def_en: a place where two or more roads cross the act of crossing or meeting
rows.mnemonic: 前缀 inter- 之间，sect 切割，后缀 -ion 表示位置，指道路或线条的交叉点，如城市交通的 intersection。
example: Be careful when driving through an intersection.
开车经过十字路口时要小心。

rows.def_en: to free a place or person from control by others to free someone from limits on their freedom or happiness
rows.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 liber（自由）加上后缀 -ate，意指使自由或解放，历史上常用于描述民族解放运动。
example: The army worked to liberate the city from enemy control.
军队努力将城市从敌人控制下解放出来。

kaoyan_ex.text: Liberate your imagination this year.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“解放”

rows.def_en: The concept of exchanging things like help or favors between two parties in a fair and equal way.
rows.mnemonic: 词根是拉丁语 reciprocus，re- 指回，pro- 指前，体现相互往来的概念，常用于描述互惠互利的关系。
example: The company values the principle of reciprocity, offering discounts to its loyal customers.
公司重视互惠原则，为忠实客户提供折扣。

rows.def_en: A wet area of land where plants grow in water. To give someone too much to handle. To cover with a lot of water.
rows.mnemonic: swamp 源于古英语，与低地德语 swamp 相关，指湿软的沼泽地，常描述被水浸透的低洼区域。
example: The swamp is home to many animals like frogs and birds.
沼泽是许多动物如青蛙和鸟类的家园。

words.def_en: connected with the way ideas or things are linked together in your mind in math, describing an operation that works the same way no matter how you group the numbers, like (a times b) times c equals a times (b times c)
words.mnemonic: associative 来自 associate，词根 soci 表示同伴或联合，强调事物之间形成联想或连接的特性。
example: The game helps children make associative connections between words and pictures.
这个游戏帮助孩子们在单词和图片之间建立联想。

words.def_en: A file sent with an email. Connecting one thing to another. A feeling of love or strong liking. Belief in an idea or value. A tool added to a machine for a special job. A short time working with a group or place.
words.mnemonic: attach 源于古法语 attachier 意为固定，后缀 -ment 表示结果，指连接物或情感上的依恋。
example: Please send the document as an email attachment.
请将文档作为电子邮件附件发送。

rows.mnemonic: 词根 dyn- 来自希腊语 dynamis 意为力量，后缀 -asty 相关，指一个家族凭借力量统治的王朝，如历史中的朝代。

尼赫鲁-甘地家族领导印度数十年。

rows.def_en: to suffer something hard or painful without giving up to last for a long time
rows.mnemonic: 源自拉丁语 indurare，in- 表示加强，durus 意为硬，所以 endure 指忍受或持久。

她不得不毫无怨言地忍受漫长的等待。

rows.def_en: A long and important period in history with its own special features. A very long period of time in geology.
rows.mnemonic: era 源于拉丁语 aera（时代），标志历史中的特定时期，如维多利亚时代。
example: The digital era changed how people communicate and access information.
数字时代改变了人们沟通和获取信息的方式。

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“时代”

rows.def_en: lasting forever; unchanging lasting too long; too frequent
rows.mnemonic: everlasting 由 ever 和 lasting 合成，ever 表示‘永远’，last 源自古英语 lǣstan 意为‘持续’，后缀 -ing 表示状态，形容永恒或持久的事物。
example: The love between them was an everlasting bond.
他们之间的爱是永恒的纽带。

rows.def_en: Being in a place or situation without protection from something harmful. When bad or dishonest facts about someone or something are made public. Being talked about or shown in media like TV or newspapers. Experiencing something new or different. A medical condition from being too cold without protection. How long light enters a camera to take a photo. One photo on a roll of film. Showing something that is usually hidden.
rows.mnemonic: exposure 由前缀 ex-（向外）和词根 pos-（放置）构成，后缀 -ure 名词化，指显露或接触的状态，如摄影中的曝光。
example: Too much exposure to the sun can cause sunburn.
过度暴露在阳光下会导致晒伤。

kaoyan_ex.text: But exposure times were much quicker by the 1880s, and the introduction of the Box Brownie and other portable cameras meant…

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“暴露”；常见搭配 by

rows.def_en: A person who studies and predicts future trends and developments, especially in science and technology.
rows.mnemonic: futurologist 拆解为 future 未来、-ology 学科和 -ist 家，指研究未来的专家；可选联系类似于科幻作家，预测科技和社会趋势。
example: The futurologist gave a fascinating talk about the potential advancements in artificial intelligence over the next decade.
未来学家就未来十年人工智能的潜在进展发表了一场引人入胜的演讲。

rows.def_en: The period of time when a person is a girl, or the state of being a girl.
rows.mnemonic: girlhood 由 girl（女孩）和后缀 -hood（表示状态或时期）组成，指少女时代或女性成长阶段。
example: She cherished her girlhood memories of playing in the park with her friends.
她珍视自己少女时代与朋友在公园玩耍的回忆。

rows.def_en: temporary; for a short time until something permanent is ready estimated before the final amount is known a temporary period between two events or situations a temporary arrangement or solution used until something permanent is established
rows.mnemonic: interim 源于拉丁语 inter 之间和 tempus 时间，意思是过渡期或临时的，常用于描述中间阶段。
example: She is the interim manager while they search for a permanent one.
在寻找正式经理期间，她是临时经理。

rows.def_en: A temporary solution or something used as a substitute because the real thing is not available.
rows.mnemonic: 拆解自 make 指制作和 shift 指临时移动或调整，描述在资源有限时凑合使用的临时解决方案。
example: The teacher used a makeshift ruler made out of a long piece of cardboard to show the students how to measure.
老师用一块长纸板做成的临时尺子，向学生展示如何测量。

kaoyan_ex.text: That’s likely because the rural poor are using the money as makeshift insurance policies against inclement weather, Ferraro says.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“临时的”；常见搭配 against

rows.def_en: The time when a meal is eaten.
rows.mnemonic: mealtime 是复合词，meal 源于古英语 mæl 意为时间或餐点，指固定的进餐时段，如早餐或晚餐时间。
example: During mealtime, the family gathered around the table to enjoy their dinner.
用餐时间，一家人围坐在桌旁享用晚餐。

rows.def_en: relating to the Middle Ages, from about 1000 to 1450 AD
rows.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 medium aevum，指欧洲中世纪时期，大约公元 500 到 1500 年，常与骑士文化和城堡建筑相关。
example: The medieval castle stood tall on the hill, reminding visitors of ancient times.
这座中世纪城堡矗立在山丘上，让游客想起古老的年代。

rows.def_en: When one thing partly covers another thing To place things so they partly cover each other When two events happen at the same time To share similar ideas or areas The shared part between two things The amount one thing covers another A time when two things happen together
rows.mnemonic: overlap 由 over（覆盖）和 lap（重叠部分）组合，表示事物部分重合，常用于描述时间或空间的交叠。
example: The roof tiles overlap to keep the rain out.
屋顶瓦片相互重叠以挡雨。

rows.def_en: in a way that lasts forever or cannot be changed
rows.mnemonic: permanently 是永久地的意思，源自 permanent，词根 per- 意为贯穿，manere 指停留，强调持久不变。
example: The accident permanently changed his life.
那场事故永久地改变了他的生活。

rows.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“永久地”；常见搭配 for

rows.def_en: never ending or changing happening too often and annoying lasting for a person's entire life
rows.mnemonic: perpetual 来自拉丁语 perpetuus，per 表示贯穿，petere 表示追求，意思是持续不断或永恒的，如 perpetual motion 指永动。
example: The perpetual motion of the ocean waves never stops.
海浪的永动从未停止。

rows.def_en: The condition of lasting forever or a very, very long time. In finance, an investment that gives you money for a very long time, often for the rest of your life.
rows.mnemonic: Perpetuity 来自拉丁语 perpetuus，per- 表示贯穿，petere 指追求，意为永恒或无限期持续的状态。
example: The ancient ruins have stood in perpetuity, bearing witness to the passage of time.
这些古代遗迹永世长存，见证着时间的流逝。

rows.def_en: to quickly pull out something like a hair or feather to remove feathers from a bird before cooking it to play a stringed instrument by pulling the strings to save or remove someone from a bad situation to take something by pulling it quickly to pick something like fruit or flowers from where it grows the courage to do something difficult
rows.mnemonic: pluck 源自古英语 pluccian，意为拔或采摘，后来引申为鼓起勇气的意思，与果断行动相关。
example: She plucked a gray hair from her head.
她从头上拔下了一根白发。

rows.def_en: Relating to a period or style of art, literature, or music that is characterized by a departure from traditional forms and techniques.
rows.mnemonic: postmodern 由前缀 post 表示之后和 modern 表示现代构成，指挑战传统现代主义的文化思潮，词缀分析突出了其时代背景的批判性。
example: The museum features a collection of postmodern art.
博物馆收藏了一系列后现代艺术。

rows.def_en: to move something to a later time
rows.mnemonic: postpone 来自拉丁语 postponere，post 表示之后，ponere 表示放置，合起来是放到以后，即推迟事件或任务。
example: We had to postpone the meeting because of bad weather.
由于天气恶劣，我们不得不推迟会议。

rows.def_en: occurring or existing after a war the period following a war
example: The country experienced rapid economic growth in the postwar period.
该国在战后时期经历了快速的经济增长。

rows.def_en: Change the time of a planned event to a different time. Change the due date for a payment or debt.
rows.mnemonic: reschedule 由 re 和 schedule 组成，re 表示重新，schedule 来自拉丁语 schedula，指时间表，整体指改变原定计划。
example: We had to reschedule the meeting because of the snowstorm.
由于暴风雪，我们不得不重新安排会议。

rows.def_en: to rub your skin with your nails when it itches to cut or hurt your skin a little with something sharp to mark or damage a surface by rubbing it with something hard to rub something hard to make or remove a mark to make a rough sound by rubbing something sharp to earn just enough money to live, but with difficulty to remove someone or something from an event before it starts a mark or small cut on skin or a surface from scratching a rough sound made by rubbing something sharp the act of rubbing your skin when it itches made quickly from whatever is available without any advantage or handicap in sports
rows.mnemonic: scratch 源于中古英语 scracchen，可能受古诺尔斯语影响，表示抓挠动作，在体育中用于从零开始的比赛。

他感到痒，就用指甲挠了挠胳膊。

rows.def_en: a narrow opening where you put something in a position or time for something in a schedule or list to put or fit something into a space
rows.mnemonic: slot 可能源于古英语，指狭缝或插槽，如机器中的 coin slot，含义简单直观，用于描述固定位置。
example: Put the coin in the slot to start the machine.
把硬币投入槽口来启动机器。

rows.def_en: to last through a period of time to cover a large area or many things to stretch across something from side to side the length of time something lasts a range or variety the part of a bridge between supports the distance from one side to the other relating to or covering the entire period from one point to another designed to bridge or connect two points
rows.mnemonic: 源自古英语 spannan，原意是拉紧，现在指时间或空间上的范围或跨度。

rows.mnemonic: stagger 源于古英语 stæger，意为摇晃或蹒跚，词根 stag- 可能关联不稳定动作，常用于描述醉酒或疲劳时的行走姿态。
example: After the accident, he walked with a stagger.
事故发生后，他走路摇摇晃晃。

rows.def_en: gradually and in a regular way without stopping or changing
rows.mnemonic: steadily 基于 steady（稳定的），后缀 -ly 表示方式，描述持续而平稳地进行，避免波动。

温度全天稳步上升。

rows.def_en: The time when the sun comes up in the morning. The colors in the sky when the sun comes up.
rows.mnemonic: sunrise 由 sun（太阳）和 rise（升起）简单组合，描述太阳升起的自然美景，象征新开始。
example: We woke up at sunrise to see the sun come up.
我们在日出时醒来，看着太阳升起。

rows.def_en: in a way that does not damage the environment and uses resources in a way that they can be replaced in a way that can last or continue for a long time without causing problems
rows.mnemonic: 副词 sustainably 来自 sustain 维持和后缀 -ably，强调以环保方式发展，不损害未来资源。
example: Farmers are planting trees to ensure their crops are grown sustainably.
农民们正在植树，以确保他们的作物可持续种植。

rows.def_en: related to the physical world, not spiritual things related to or limited by time near the temples on the side of the head
rows.mnemonic: temporal 来源于拉丁语 temporalis，根于 tempus 表示时间，因此指与时间有关的或暂时的，常用于描述短暂现象。
example: The temporal world changes, but spiritual beliefs often stay the same.
世俗世界在变化，但精神信仰往往保持不变。

rows.def_en: to make short, regular sounds like a clock to mark with a check (✓) a check mark (✓) a small bug that bites and drinks blood the sound a clock makes a very short time

example: The clock makes a tick sound every second.
时钟每秒发出滴答声。

rows.def_en: A line that shows how events are arranged in time, from the past on the left to the future on the right. A record of someone's posts and activities on social media, listed in the order they were made, with the newest at the top.
rows.mnemonic: timeline 是 time 和 line 的组合词，直译为时间线，用于展示事件的历史顺序，如在项目管理中。
example: The timeline of the project helps us see when each task should be completed.
项目的时间线帮助我们了解每项任务应在何时完成。

rows.def_en: A range of time within which something happens or is planned to happen.
rows.mnemonic: 由 time（时间，古英语 tima）和 scale（尺度，拉丁语 scala）组合，表示时间范围或测量单位
example: The project's completion is planned within a one-year timescale.
该项目计划在一年内完成。

rows.def_en: a cold sweet dish with layers of cake, fruit, jelly, custard, and cream a little bit something small or not important to treat something as unimportant or not serious to spend time in a light or frivolous way
rows.mnemonic: trifle 来自古法语 trufle，意为琐事或小事，在英语中还指一种分层甜点，体现从轻微事物到具体物品的演变。
example: For dessert, we enjoyed a delicious trifle with berries and cream.
至于甜点，我们享用了美味的浆果奶油蛋糕。

rows.def_en: The quality or state of not being able to be maintained at a certain rate or level.
example: The unsustainability of current fishing practices threatens marine ecosystems.
当前捕捞方式的不可持续性威胁着海洋生态系统。

rows.def_en: a fast spinning windstorm that causes damage a very busy and eventful time very fast and happening with little time to prepare
rows.mnemonic: whirlwind 组合了 whirl（旋转）和 wind（风），描述一种快速旋转的风暴，引申为迅猛或混乱的事件。
example: The park was damaged by a whirlwind last night.
昨晚公园被一阵旋风破坏了。

rows.def_en: helping or supporting the main group used when the main equipment fails a helping verb like 'be', 'do', or 'have' a helper who supports the main workers
rows.mnemonic: auxiliary 源自拉丁语 auxilium（帮助），词根 aux- 表示辅助，常用于描述备用或支持性的事物，如 auxiliary power。
example: The auxiliary team provides extra help during busy times.
辅助团队在繁忙时段提供额外帮助。

rows.def_en: to lose blood from the body to take blood from someone as an old medical treatment to make someone pay too much money to remove air or liquid from something to fix it to spread or mix into something else
rows.mnemonic: 来自古英语 blēdan，表示血液流出，词根 bleed 强调液体或颜色的渗出。印刷术语中，bleed 指图像延伸到纸张边缘的设计。
example: If you cut yourself, you may bleed.
如果你割伤自己，可能会流血。

rows.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“流血”；以 -ed 形式出现

rows.def_en: continuing without stopping, for a very long time
rows.mnemonic: 由 end 结束加后缀 -less 无和 -ly 副词化构成，表示无限持续，词缀组合强化时间或空间的无边界性。
example: The children played, endlessly chasing each other around the playground.
孩子们在操场上不停地追逐玩耍。

rows.def_en: something that has the same value, meaning, or purpose as another thing equal in value, meaning, or importance
rows.mnemonic: equivalent 词根为 equi-（相等）和 valere（价值），指在功能或意义上等同的事物，帮助理解比较关系。
example: This amount of sugar is the equivalent of ten teaspoons.
这个糖量相当于十茶匙。

rows.def_en: lasting forever with no end happening over and over without stopping
rows.mnemonic: eternal 来自拉丁语 aeternus，意为永久的，这个词源强调时间上的无限延续。
example: Their love is eternal and will never fade.
他们的爱是永恒的，永远不会消逝。

rows.def_en: to run away quickly because of fear or danger
rows.mnemonic: flee 源于古英语 fleon，意思是逃跑或躲避，词源简单直接，常用于描述紧急逃离场景。
example: When the fire alarm sounded, everyone had to flee the building immediately.
当火警响起时，每个人都必须立即逃离大楼。

rows.def_en: A long, flexible tube for moving water or other liquids. A word for tights, stockings, or socks, especially in shops. Tight-fitting trousers worn by men in the past. To wash or spray something with water using a hose.
rows.mnemonic: hose 词源是古英语，指用于输送液体的软管，常见于花园或消防设备。
example: Use the hose to water the plants in the garden.
用软管给花园里的植物浇水。

rows.def_en: the whole time that someone lives or something exists
rows.mnemonic: lifetime 拆解为 life 生命和 time 时间，指一生或终生，含义从时间跨度扩展到产品或事件的整个周期。
example: She saved money for her children's education over her entire lifetime.
她一生都在为孩子的教育存钱。

kaoyan_ex.text: To be fair , the FSA says it is not telling people to cut out roast foods entirely , but to reduce their lifetime intake.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“一生”

rows.def_en: ordinary and not interesting
rows.mnemonic: mundane 来自拉丁语 mundanus 世界的，指平凡或世俗事物，缺乏超凡脱俗的元素。
example: My daily routine feels mundane because it is the same every day.
我的日常生活感觉很单调，因为每天都是一样的。

rows.def_en: no longer used because something better exists
rows.mnemonic: obsolete 源自拉丁语 obsoletus，意为磨损的或废弃的，含义演变为过时的，常用于描述被新技术取代的事物。

软盘现在已经过时了，因为现代计算机使用USB驱动器和云存储。

rows.def_en: old and not useful anymore
rows.mnemonic: out- 前缀表示超出，dated 来自 date 日期，outdated 指因时间推移而过时的，如 outdated technology 指陈旧技术。
example: This computer is outdated and cannot run new programs.
这台电脑过时了，无法运行新程序。

rows.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“过时的”；以 -ed 形式出现

rows.def_en: Doing something very carefully and with a lot of attention to detail.
rows.mnemonic: painstakingly 由 pains 和 taking 组合而成，pains 指努力或辛劳，taking 表示承担，整体形容极其小心和费力的做事方式。
example: The artist painstakingly painted each leaf on the tree, making sure every detail was perfect.
艺术家一丝不苟地画了树上的每一片叶子，确保每个细节都完美。

rows.def_en: to say something you have learned from memory, like a poem or story, often to others to list or say many things one after another
rows.mnemonic: recite 词源来自拉丁语 recitare，其中 re- 表示再次，citare 意为召唤或引用，组合起来指逐字背诵或复述内容。
example: She will recite a poem at the school assembly.
她将在学校集会上朗诵一首诗。

rows.def_en: to practice a play, music, or performance before showing it to others to practice in your mind what you will say or do to repeat ideas or opinions that are already known
rows.mnemonic: rehearse 意思是排练或练习，源于古法语 rehercier，意为反复梳理，比喻像用耙子整理土地一样重复操作。

演员们需要排练他们的台词。

rows.def_en: something old that remains from the past a holy object from a religious person, kept after their death
rows.mnemonic: relic 源于拉丁语 reliquiae，指历史遗迹或宗教圣物，常与古代文明相关联。

这台旧打字机是我祖父时代的遗物。

保安例行检查每个进入大楼的人的身份证件。

rows.def_en: not related to religion or spiritual matters living in the ordinary world, not in a religious group
rows.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 saecularis ，saeculum 指时代或世纪，强调世俗的、非宗教的现世事务。
example: In our secular society, religious beliefs are a personal choice.
在我们这个世俗社会中，宗教信仰是个人的选择。

rows.def_en: To cause a sharp pain by piercing the skin. To feel or cause a sharp pain. To make someone feel upset or angry. To charge someone too much money. To borrow money from someone. The sharp part of an insect that causes pain. A painful wound from an insect or plant. A sharp physical or emotional pain. A police plan to catch criminals. A criminal plan to cheat people out of money.
rows.mnemonic: sting 源于古英语 stingan，本义是刺或叮咬，常描述昆虫攻击或情感上的刺痛感。
example: The bee sting on my arm hurt a lot.

words.def_en: Hair cut to hang over the forehead Decorative hanging threads on the edge of something A narrow strip along the edge of something The outer part of an area or group Activities or people not in the main group To border or edge something
words.mnemonic: fringe 来自古法语 frenge，意为边缘或装饰性流苏，可指事物的外围部分。
example: She brushed her fringe out of her eyes.
她把刘海从眼前拨开。

words.def_en: most hidden and personal part of someone's thoughts or feelings closest to the center or inside part of something
words.mnemonic: innermost 由 inner 加后缀 -most 构成，inner 意为内部，-most 表示最高级，整体指最深处或最私密的部分。
example: He shared his innermost secrets with his best friend.
他把自己内心最深处的秘密告诉了他最好的朋友。

words.def_en: a person who is part of a group or organization and knows secret information about it
words.mnemonic: insider 来自 inside（内部）和 er（表示人），指组织内部的知情人士。
example: An insider told us about the company's secret plans.
一位内部人士向我们透露了公司的秘密计划。

words.def_en: the inside part of something the land far from the coast a country's own matters inside something inland, away from the coast related to a country's own matters
words.mnemonic: interior 来自拉丁语 interior，意思是内部或里面，词根 inter- (在...之间) 强调空间位置。
example: The interior of the house is very beautiful.
房子的内部非常漂亮。

kaoyan_ex.text: …at government agencies like the Department of the Interior, that Yellowstone ought to be preserved.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“内部”；后接 that 从句

words.def_en: How far north or south a place is from the equator, measured in degrees An area of the world at a certain distance from the equator Freedom to make your own choices
words.mnemonic: 词源是拉丁语 latitudo 宽度，在地理中指纬度，也引申为行动的自由度。
example: The city's latitude is 40 degrees north of the equator.
该城市的纬度是北纬40度。

words.def_en: relating to the limbic system of the brain relating to a border or edge
example: The limbic system is involved in emotion, memory, and motivation.
边缘系统涉及情绪、记忆和动机。

words.def_en: the area around a place where something is located
words.mnemonic: locality 的词根 loc- 源于拉丁语 locus（地方），后缀 -ity 名词化，指特定地理位置或区域范围。
example: The locality around the school has many parks.
学校周边地区有很多公园。

words.def_en: Not given enough importance or opportunities to be part of society fully.
words.mnemonic: marginalized 由 margin 和 -ize 构成，margin 来自拉丁语 margo 指边缘，-ize 表示使动，整体指将群体推到社会边缘，体现排斥现象。
example: The community is working to help the marginalized youth find their place in society.
社区正在努力帮助边缘化青年在社会中找到自己的位置。

words.def_en: Items for sale in stores. Items that promote an event or group. To sell items using ads.
words.mnemonic: merchandise 来自古法语 marchandise，与 marchand 商人相关，后缀 -ise 表示商品，整体指用于销售的产品，也可作动词指推销，如 merchandise goods。
example: You can use this coupon to get any merchandise in our shop.
你可以用这张优惠券购买我们店里的任何商品。

words.def_en: Something that affects or involves the whole country.
words.mnemonic: nationally 是 nation 国家的副词形式，后缀 ally 表示方式，意思是在全国范围内。
example: The event was broadcasted nationally, reaching millions of viewers.
该活动在全国范围内播出，覆盖了数百万观众。

kaoyan_ex.text: The popularity of these novels consolidated Dickens as a nationally and internationally celebrated man of letters.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“全国范围地”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: To move your head up and down to show you agree or understand. To move your head down and up once to greet someone or signal them to do something. To point with your head to show where something is. To let your head drop forward when sleeping while sitting. A quick up and down movement of the head.
words.mnemonic: nod 源于古英语 hnoddian，意思是点头，这个简单动作常用于表示同意、致意或疲倦的信号。
example: When I asked if she understood, she gave a quick nod.
当我问她是否明白时，她迅速点了点头。

words.def_en: In the direction of the upper right on a map. At a location more towards the north-east compared to another.
example: The sun rises in the east, so my balcony faces north-east for morning shade.
太阳从东方升起，所以我的阳台朝东北，以便早晨有阴凉。

words.def_en: In the direction of the northwest, between north and west.
words.mnemonic: north-west 是方向词，north 指北，west 指西，组合后表示地理上的西北方位，常用于导航或描述位置。
example: The birds were flying north-west, towards the setting sun.
鸟儿们向西北方向飞去，朝着落日。

words.def_en: The curved path an object takes as it moves around another object in space. The area or range that someone or something can influence or control. To move in a curved path around a larger object in space.
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 orbita 车轮轨迹，原指圆形路径，天文上用于行星绕太阳的 orbit，如 Earth's orbit 地球轨道。
example: The moon's orbit around Earth takes about 27 days.
月球绕地球公转一周大约需要27天。

words.def_en: a field for playing sports how high or low a sound is the level or intensity of something a talk to sell or persuade a throw of the ball a black sticky substance for waterproofing a place to sell or perform outdoors a campsite for one tent or caravan the up and down movement of a ship or aircraft the slope of a roof to throw something forcefully to throw the ball to a batter to hit or make the ball hit the ground to hit the ball in a high curve to fall heavily forward to move up and down on water or in air to set something at a certain level to aim a product at a specific group to try to sell or persuade to produce sound at a certain level to set up a tent or camp
words.mnemonic: 词源复杂，可能源自古英语 pic，原指沥青或焦油，后来含义扩展到投掷动作、音高或运动场，在音乐中 pitch 常表示音符的高低。
example: The team practiced on the pitch every day.
球队每天都在球场上训练。

words.def_en: the outer edge of a round object the metal part of a wheel that holds the tire having an edge of a certain kind to put an edge around something
words.mnemonic: 源自古英语 rima 意为边缘，指物体如轮子或容器的外围部分，在工程中常用于描述轮圈或边框。
example: She sipped her coffee from the rim of the cup.
她从杯沿小口喝着咖啡。

words.def_en: used to show how big, strong, or much something is pure and nothing else very steep thin and see-through straight up or down to change direction suddenly, especially of a ship or vehicle to deviate from a course or topic
words.mnemonic: sheer 词源与古英语 scir 相关，本义纯粹或陡峭，在纺织业中指轻薄透明的面料，常用来形容悬崖或布料的无杂质特性。
example: The sheer number of people at the event was amazing.
活动现场的人数之多令人惊叹。

kaoyan_ex.text: There’s fun in testimonies of people enjoying the sheer newness.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“纯粹的”

words.def_en: In the direction between south and east. At a position more towards the south-east than another point.
words.mnemonic: 由 south 南和 east 东组合而成，表示罗盘上的东南方位，常用于地理导航。
example: The sun rises in the east, but our balcony faces south-east, so we get morning sun.
太阳从东方升起，但我们的阳台朝东南，所以早上能晒到太阳。

words.def_en: In the direction of the compass point halfway between south and west. At a location more towards the south-west than another point.
example: The sun sets in the south-west, casting a warm glow over the landscape.
太阳在西南方落下，给大地洒下温暖的光芒。

words.def_en: located in or coming from the southwest part of a country or region facing or moving towards the southwest relating to or characteristic of the southwest region of a country
example: The southwestern states of the US have a dry climate.
美国西南部各州气候干燥。

words.def_en: The range of colors seen when light is spread out, like in a rainbow. A range of waves, like light, sound, or radio waves. A wide range of different things or ideas.
words.mnemonic: spectrum 来自拉丁语，原意为幽灵或图像，词根 specere 指看，现在科学中特指光或电磁波的连续范围。
example: The rainbow shows the full spectrum of colors from red to violet.
彩虹展示了从红色到紫色的全色谱。

kaoyan_ex.text: This was also found in high-functioning men with some autistic spectrum symptoms, who may tend to avoid eye contact.

words.def_en: how fast something moves in a certain direction very fast speed

example: The ball's velocity increased as it rolled downhill.
球滚下山坡时速度增加了。

words.def_en: the area near or around a place
words.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 vicinitas，表示邻近区域或周围环境，常用于描述地理位置。

许多商店位于火车站附近。

kaoyan_ex.text: Each automatic door system analyses the light, sound, weight or movement in their vicinity as a signal to open.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“附近”；常见搭配 as

words.def_en: The area of land behind a house, often with grass or a garden. A paved area behind a house, usually surrounded by walls.
words.mnemonic: 直接由 back 和 yard 组成，指房屋后院的私人空间。作为家庭休闲场所，backyard 常与烧烤或园艺活动联系在一起。

我们经常在后院玩游戏。

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“后院”；常见搭配 by

石油是一种在全球交易的商品。

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“商品”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: A flying vehicle with spinning blades on top that can take off straight up, land vertically, and hover in one spot.
words.mnemonic: helicopter 源自希腊语 helix（螺旋）和 pteron（翼），指直升机这种旋翼飞行器，与航空技术发展紧密相关。

直升机飞越城市上空，协助执行救援任务。

words.def_en: inside your mind and not shown to others moving toward the inside or center toward the inside or center toward yourself and your own thoughts
words.mnemonic: in 向内 和 ward 方向后缀组合，指向内部或内心的
example: His calm face hid his inward fear.
他平静的面容掩盖了内心的恐惧。

words.def_en: A person without special knowledge in a subject A church member who is not a priest or clergy
words.mnemonic: layman 由 lay 和 man 组成，lay 源于古英语 leaw，指世俗或非专业，与宗教语境中的 laity 相关，man 表示人，合起来描述外行人士。

医生用外行能理解的术语解释了医疗程序。

words.def_en: closeness in space or time

学校靠近公园，方便孩子们课后玩耍。

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“接近”

医生给我做了全面检查，以确保我身体健康。

rows.def_en: to be very plentiful or numerous
rows.mnemonic: abound 的词源可追溯到拉丁语 abundare，其中 ab- 表示远离，und 意为流动，整体描述事物像水流般溢出，表示丰富或大量存在。

这个城市的学习机会比比皆是。

rows.def_en: not being present or available when expected not existing or not having something
rows.mnemonic: 由拉丁语 absentia 演变而来，前缀 ab- 表示远离，词根 esse 意为存在，所以 absence 描述缺席或缺乏的状态。日常中，absence 常出现在考勤记录中。

会议在我缺席的情况下继续进行，因为我生病了。

花园里长满了新鲜的蔬菜。

救生衣使他漂浮在水面上。

example: We have ample food for everyone at the party.
我们有充足的食物供聚会上的每个人享用。

rows.def_en: A container with a handle for carrying things like water or sand. The large scoop on a machine like a crane or digger. The amount that fits in one bucket. A very large amount of something. to carry or move something using a bucket to rain very heavily
rows.mnemonic: bucket 的词源可追溯到古英语 buc，指容器，可能源自法语 buquet。在计算领域，bucket 用于指代数据存储桶，比如在云服务中。

孩子在沙滩上把桶装满了沙子。

我切了一大块奶酪做三明治。

rows.def_en: to keep someone or something within certain limits to keep a person or animal in a closed space to have to stay in bed or a chair due to illness
rows.mnemonic: confine 源自拉丁语 confinare，con 表示一起，finis 意为边界，合起来指限制范围，常用于描述地理或行为约束。

请将你的评论限制在主要话题上。

他慷慨地捐钱帮助有需要的人。

rows.def_en: A row of bushes or small trees planted close together, often used as a border. A way to protect yourself from losing something, especially money. To avoid giving a direct answer. 我们在花园周围种了一排树篱，以标明地界。

这批艺术收藏品非常独特，因此流动性差，很少有买家愿意支付高价。

由于资产缺乏流动性，该公司面临严重的财务问题。

words.def_en: extremely large or powerful
words.mnemonic: titanic 源自希腊神话中的 Titan（泰坦巨人），后缀 -ic 表示相关，描述巨大无比的事物，历史上与 Titanic 邮轮事件联系紧密。
example: The Titanic was a titanic ship that tragically sank on its maiden voyage.
泰坦尼克号是一艘巨大的轮船，在首航中不幸沉没。

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“巨大的”

words.def_en: not clear in someone's mind not giving enough information or details showing a lack of clear thinking not having a clear shape
words.mnemonic: vague 源自法语 vague，拉丁语词根 vagus 意为徘徊不定，描述模糊不清的概念或记忆，避免明确细节。

他对那件事模糊的记忆使得很难描述。

example: It was too foggy to see the road clearly while driving.
雾太大了，开车时看不清路。

words.def_en: existing in name only, not real very small amount, much less than usual relating to a noun

他名义上担任主任一职，但实际上没有实权。

words.def_en: not known by many people hard to understand to hide or make unclear

那个偏僻的村庄深藏在群山之中。

kaoyan_ex.text: …anything comic or odd, submitted short sketches to obscure magazines.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“鲜为人知的”

words.def_en: a small nut that grows under the ground in a thin shell a very small amount of money
words.mnemonic: peanut 由 pea 豌豆和 nut 坚果组合而成，但实际指花生这种豆科植物，常联系到日常食品如 peanut butter 花生酱。
example: I like to eat a peanut as a snack.
我喜欢吃花生当零食。

words.def_en: related to a province or its local government from outside the capital, often seen as less cultured or modern narrow-minded or resistant to new ideas a person from outside the capital, often seen as less cultured
words.mnemonic: 源自 provincia 意思是省，-al 后缀表示相关，provincial 指省的或地方性的，有时隐含偏狭的含义。

words.def_en: very beautiful or impressive very good or excellent used to show you are happy or approve of something
words.mnemonic: splendid 由拉丁语 splendere（发光）演变而来，词根 splend- 表达光辉，后缀 -id 增强形容词性，形容极其辉煌的事物。
example: The sunset was a splendid sight with bright colors.
日落景色壮丽，色彩鲜艳。

words.def_en: extremely good or excellent
words.mnemonic: superb 的词源是拉丁语 superbus，super- 意为上或超越，后缀 -bus 表示状态，原义骄傲的，后来演变为卓越的。
example: The chef prepared a superb meal that everyone enjoyed.
厨师准备了一顿极好的饭菜，每个人都喜欢。

words.def_en: extremely large or impressive
words.mnemonic: 源自 whop 意为重击，-ing 后缀形成形容词，强调尺寸或数量的巨大，常用于口语如 a whopping success。
example: She won a whopping amount of money in the lottery.
她中了彩票，赢了一大笔钱。

rows.def_en: The language used in ancient Rome and spoken by people in many countries today. A person from a country where a language that comes from Latin is spoken, like Spain or Italy. A type of music from Latin America with a strong beat that people like to dance to. Related to the Latin language. Related to countries or people where languages that come from Latin are spoken. Related to Latin American music.
example: Many English words have Latin roots.
许多英语单词有拉丁词根。

kaoyan_ex.text: Such actions to seek knowledge and to understand what information we already knew were captured by the Latin phrase “sapere…

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“拉丁语”

rows.def_en: related to hearing or the ears
rows.mnemonic: aural 源于拉丁语 auris，意为耳朵，与听觉相关，常与 oral（口头的）对比，强调声音的接收而非发出。
example: The teacher gave an aural test to check how well students could understand spoken words.
老师进行了一次听力测试，以检查学生理解口语的能力。

rows.def_en: To push air out of your throat suddenly and loudly, often when you are sick. To push something out of your throat or lungs by coughing. To make a sudden, rough noise, like an engine that is not working well. The act or sound of pushing air out of your throat suddenly. An illness that makes you cough often.
rows.mnemonic: cough 源于古英语 cohhetan，描述一种身体反射动作，与喉咙或呼吸道的刺激相关。
example: When you have a cold, you may cough a lot.
感冒时，你可能会咳嗽很多。

rows.def_en: to give a funny or critical name to someone or something to change the speech in a movie or show to a different language to create music by mixing sounds from different recordings a type of West Indian music or poetry with a strong beat
rows.mnemonic: dub 源于古法语 adouber，最初指授予骑士称号，后来演变为给电影配音或添加音轨，现在常用于表示配音或赋予称号。
example: Fans dub him the king of pop because of his amazing music.
粉丝们称他为流行音乐之王，因为他的音乐令人惊叹。

rows.def_en: A sound that bounces back and repeats. To bounce back sound; to be filled with repeated sound. To repeat an idea or opinion because you agree. To repeat what someone said because it's surprising. A repeated sound that bounces back. Something that reminds you of something else. An opinion or feeling that matches another.

喊叫声的回声在山谷中回荡。

rows.def_en: Comments or suggestions about how good something is or how it can be improved A loud, high noise from electronic equipment when sound loops back into it

我从老师那里得到了关于我项目的有益反馈。

rows.def_en: one of the four books in the Bible about Jesus the life and teachings of Jesus in the Bible a set of ideas someone strongly believes in the complete truth a style of religious singing from African American culture

rows.def_en: cruel, severe, and unkind very difficult and unpleasant to live in too strong and bright; ugly or unpleasant to look at unpleasant to listen to too strong and rough, likely to damage something

她喜欢边工作边哼歌。
