words.mnemonic: pest 源自拉丁语 pestis 意为瘟疫或灾难，含义演变为有害的害虫或令人讨厌的人，在农业中常指破坏作物的生物。
example: Farmers use traps to catch pests that eat their crops.
农民使用陷阱捕捉吃庄稼的害虫。

words.def_en: A small round medicine you swallow whole. A pill women take to prevent pregnancy. A person who is annoying. To form small balls on fabric.
words.mnemonic: pill 源于拉丁语 pilula 指小球状物，描述口服药丸，如避孕 pill 或维生素补充剂。
example: Take this pill with water to feel better.
用水服下这片药，你会感觉好一些。

words.def_en: in a way that shows you are proud of something in a way that is big and impressive
words.mnemonic: proudly 来自 proud，意思是自豪的，加上后缀 -ly 形成副词，描述以骄傲或自信的方式行事。
example: She proudly showed her award to everyone.
她自豪地向每个人展示她的奖项。

words.def_en: to push away an attack or attacker to keep something away or prevent it from sticking to cause strong dislike or disgust to push away by magnetic or electric force
words.mnemonic: repel 来自拉丁语 repellere，re 表示回，pellere 表示推，整体意为推开或击退，常用于描述排斥或驱赶。
example: The army repelled the enemy forces.
军队击退了敌军。

words.def_en: blame or criticism for something done wrong words that express blame or criticism a feeling of shame or loss of honor something that causes shame or disgrace to blame or criticize someone for something they did wrong to feel guilty about something you think you should have done differently
words.mnemonic: reproach 来自古法语 reprochier，re- 意为 against，prochier 意为 come near，组合起来指责备或批评，带有情感色彩。
example: His voice was full of reproach when he spoke about the mistake.
他谈到这个错误时，声音里充满了责备。

words.def_en: done alone without others likes to be alone alone with nothing around only one punishment where a prisoner is kept alone a person who lives alone
words.mnemonic: solitary 来自 soli- 单独，后缀 -tary 表示状态，形容孤独的或独自的，也指监狱中的单独监禁。
example: He lived a solitary life in the mountains.
他在山里过着孤独的生活。

words.def_en: used to express relief or happiness that something good happened or something bad was avoided in a way that shows you are pleased or grateful
words.mnemonic: thankfully 源自 thank 表示感谢，加上 ful 后缀表达充满的状态，再以 ly 形成副词，整体传递感激或欣慰的情感，常用于描述一种幸运的解脱感。
example: The storm was strong, but thankfully our house was not damaged.
暴风雨很猛烈，但幸好我们的房子没有受损。

kaoyan_ex.text: Thankfully, there are signs that this is already happening, with Generation Z seeking to learn from their millennial…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“幸好”；后接 that 从句

words.def_en: not nice to look at not good or pleasant
words.mnemonic: unattractive 包含前缀 un-（不）和 attractive（吸引人的），表示缺乏魅力或不吸引人。
example: The old building was very unattractive and needed painting.
这座旧建筑非常不美观，需要粉刷。

words.def_en: The back part of your foot. The part of a sock that covers your heel. The raised back part of a shoe. Having a certain type of heel. Shoes with high heels. The raised part where your hand meets your wrist. A bad person who cannot be trusted. To fix the heel of a shoe. To lean to one side.
words.mnemonic: heel 意思是脚后跟，源自古英语。在鞋类中，high heel 高跟鞋是时尚元素。
example: She hurt her heel when she stepped on a rock.
她踩到一块石头时伤到了脚后跟。

words.def_en: by itself, with no others around raising children without a partner
words.mnemonic: lone 是 alone 的简化形式，表示孤单或孤立的状态，源于古英语 an 的演变。
example: A lone tree stood at the top of the hill.
一棵孤零零的树矗立在山顶。

words.def_en: A deadly disease spread by rats that causes fever, body swelling, and often death. Any fast-spreading disease that kills many people. A large number of animals or insects that cause damage. To cause ongoing pain or problems for someone or something. To annoy someone by constantly asking for things or attention.
words.mnemonic: 词源可追溯到拉丁语 plaga，意思是打击或伤口，后来演变为指代严重的传染病，如历史上有名的黑死病。
example: The plague killed many people in Europe long ago.
很久以前，瘟疫在欧洲夺走了许多人的生命。

words.def_en: rare and very expensive valuable and should not be wasted very loved and important used to show anger when someone thinks something is too important too formal and not natural used to emphasize that there is very little of something
words.mnemonic: precious 源于拉丁语 pretium 价值，加上后缀 -ous 构成形容词，形容事物极其珍贵或有情感价值。
example: The precious necklace was made of gold and diamonds.
这条珍贵的项链由黄金和钻石制成。

kaoyan_ex.text: To pressure zoos to spend less on their animals would lead to inhumane outcomes for the precious creatures in their care.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“珍贵的”；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: A cold-blooded animal with scaly skin that lays eggs, such as snakes, lizards, and turtles.
words.mnemonic: reptile 来自拉丁语 repere（爬行），指爬行动物如蛇或龟，强调其缓慢移动的特性。
example: A snake is a type of reptile that moves without legs.
蛇是一种没有腿的爬行动物。

words.def_en: Bad behavior or an event that shocks people and makes them angry Stories about bad things people have done Something very wrong that should not be accepted
words.mnemonic: scandal 来自希腊语 skandalon 原意绊脚石，后指丑闻或道德过失，媒体常报道 political scandal 涉及公众人物的不当行为。
example: The politician's scandal involved taking money illegally while in office.
这位政治家的丑闻涉及在任期间非法收受钱财。

words.def_en: to bend forward and down to stand or walk with bent shoulders bent shoulders from always leaning forward small porch with steps at a door
words.mnemonic: stoop 这个词来自古英语，描述身体向下弯曲的动作，常用于指弯腰或俯身，强调姿势的演变。
example: He had to stoop to enter the low door.
他不得不弯腰才能进入那扇低矮的门。

words.def_en: a small, flat computer with a touch screen a small, solid piece of medicine you swallow a small, solid piece of a substance a flat stone with writing on it, often on a wall a piece of soap sheets of paper fastened together
words.mnemonic: tablet 来源于拉丁语 tabula，意思是平板或板子，后来演变成指药片或平板电脑，因为形状扁平如板。
example: I use my tablet to watch videos and play games.
我用平板电脑看视频和玩游戏。

words.def_en: To make fun of someone in a playful or annoying way. To bother an animal by touching or pulling it. To make someone feel excited without following through. To show a little of something to make someone want more. To pull something apart gently into pieces. To comb hair against its growth to make it look fuller. A person who likes to joke or trick others. A playful trick or joke. A person who leads someone on without meaning to follow through.
words.mnemonic: 单词 tease 源自古英语 tæsan，本义是拉扯或梳理羊毛，后来演变为精神上的戏弄或挑逗，形象地描述了情感上的拉扯过程。
example: My friends often tease me about my silly laugh.
我的朋友经常取笑我傻笑的样子。

rows.def_en: loyalty and support for a person, group, or country
rows.mnemonic: allegiance 源于古法语 allegeance，al- 到和 liege 领主，表示效忠或忠诚，常用于政治或誓言。
example: The soldiers showed their allegiance to their country by fighting bravely.
士兵们通过英勇作战来表达对国家的忠诚。

rows.def_en: Your inner sense of right and wrong. A feeling of guilt for something you did or didn't do. Acting according to what you believe is right, even when it's hard.
rows.mnemonic: 拆解自拉丁语 conscientia，由 con-（共同）和 scientia（知识）构成，表示内心共享的道德知识或良知，常用于伦理讨论。
example: My conscience tells me not to lie.
我的良心告诉我不要说谎。

kaoyan_ex.text: …and issued a statement explaining that “we cannot in good conscience encourage you to pursue our profession”.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“良心”；常接 to 不定式/介词 to

rows.def_en: The quality of not changing or being steady. The quality of being loyal or committed.
rows.mnemonic: constancy 源于拉丁语 constantia，con- 表示一起，stare 表示站立，引申为坚定不移的品质或稳定性。
example: Her constancy in following the daily routine impressed everyone.
她坚持日常惯例的恒心给每个人留下了深刻印象。

rows.def_en: no light how dark something is evil or bad things
rows.mnemonic: darkness 由 dark 黑暗加上名词后缀 -ness 构成，表示缺乏光线的状态或比喻性的阴暗。
example: The darkness made it hard to see without a light.
黑暗使得没有光就很难看清东西。

kaoyan_ex.text: Nicholas Nickleb y , his next novel, combines the darkness of Oliver Twist with the sunlight of Pickwick.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“黑暗”；常见搭配 with

rows.def_en: not good or honest not following proper sexual behavior
rows.mnemonic: immoral 由前缀 im-（不）和 moral（道德的）构成，指违反道德准则的行为或态度，与 ethical 相对。
example: Lying to get what you want is immoral.
通过撒谎来获取想要的东西是不道德的。

rows.def_en: Being honest and having strong moral values Being whole and not broken into parts
rows.mnemonic: integrity 的词源是拉丁语 integer，意思是完整或未受损害，引申为道德上的正直和诚实，强调个人品质的整体性。
example: Her integrity was clear when she returned the lost wallet with all the money inside.
当她归还那个里面装满了钱的丢失钱包时，她的正直显而易见。

kaoyan_ex.text: This type of integrity requires well-enforced laws in government transparency, such as records of official meetings, rules on…

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“诚信”；常见搭配 in

rows.def_en: very high and impressive having high moral quality acting better than others
rows.mnemonic: 与 loft 高处相关，后缀 -y 赋予形容词性质，形容崇高的目标或有时略带傲慢的态度。
example: The lofty mountain peaks were covered in snow.
高耸的山峰被雪覆盖着。

rows.def_en: Someone who believes in and talks about strong ideas about what is right and wrong, often telling others how they should behave. A person who teaches or writes about what is right and wrong, focusing on moral principles.
rows.mnemonic: moralist 从 moral 道德派生，加上 -ist 表示人，指专注于道德说教或评判的个体。
example: The moralist argued that people should be more considerate of others' feelings.
道德家认为人们应该更多地体谅他人的感受。

kaoyan_ex.text: A moralist, satirist, and social reformer.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“道德家”

rows.def_en: Someone who believes that it is important to live in a very strict and simple way, especially saying no to physical pleasure. A person from a group of English Protestants from the 16th and 17th centuries who preferred simpler forms of worship. Related to the Puritans or their religious beliefs and practices. Having or showing very strict moral attitudes.
rows.mnemonic: Puritan 来自 purity 纯洁 指清教徒 他们倡导道德纯洁和宗教改革 在17世纪英国历史中扮演重要角色。
example: The town was known for its puritan attitudes towards parties and celebrations.
这个镇子以对派对和庆祝活动持清教徒式的态度而闻名。

definition: 处子（不分性别）, 处男, 处女
rows.def_en: A person who has never had sex. The Virgin Mary, mother of Jesus. A person new to an activity. Pure and untouched. Having no sexual experience.
rows.mnemonic: 源自拉丁语 virgo，意为处女，后来扩展指未开发或未使用的事物，如原始森林；此外，Virgin 是 Richard Branson 创立的知名品牌，如 Virgin Atlantic 航空公司。
example: She was a virgin before marriage.
她婚前是处女。

rows.def_en: Evil or very bad Playfully naughty or mischievous Very strong or dangerous Excellent or very good Evil people
rows.mnemonic: 词根源于古英语 wicca（巫术），演变为形容词后缀 -ed，原意邪恶，但在现代俚语中常表示极好或厉害，含义随语境变化。
example: The wicked king hurt many people.
邪恶的国王伤害了许多人。

rows.def_en: The time of day when it is getting dark but not completely dark yet.
rows.mnemonic: dusk 来自古英语 dox（昏暗的），描述日落后的黄昏时分，与 dawn 相对。
example: We took a walk at dusk when the sky was turning from light to dark.
我们在黄昏时分散步，那时天空正从明亮转为黑暗。

rows.def_en: a young unmarried woman an inning where no runs are scored first of its kind
rows.mnemonic: maiden 源自古英语 mægden，指未婚的年轻女子，也用于形容首次或原始状态。
example: The maiden waited for her knight to return from battle.
少女等待着她的骑士从战场归来。

rows.def_en: a person officially recognized by the Christian Church as very holy because of their life or death a very good, kind, or patient person
rows.mnemonic: saint 来自拉丁语 sanctus，意为神圣的，常用于宗教中指代圣人
example: Many people pray to a saint for help and guidance.
许多人向圣徒祈祷，寻求帮助和指引。

rows.def_en: doing things secretly or dishonestly to trick others showing you know a secret that others don't
rows.mnemonic: 单词 sly 源自古英语 sleag，意指狡猾或诡诈，常描述一种机智但可能欺骗性的行为特质，其含义从古老的狡诈演变到现代的机灵或偷偷摸摸。
example: He gave a sly look, knowing he had tricked them.
他露出狡黠的神情，知道自己骗过了他们。

rows.def_en: thinking you are better than others and acting rude because of it
rows.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 arrogantia，其中 ad- 表示向，rogare 意为要求，整体指傲慢自大，暗示过度索求尊重。
example: His arrogance made him ignore other people's ideas during the meeting.
他的傲慢使他在会议中无视他人的想法。

rows.def_en: thinking you are better than others and acting rude
rows.mnemonic: arrogant 源自拉丁语 arrogare，其中 ad- 表示向，rogare 意思是问，组合指傲慢地要求或自以为是。
example: The arrogant man ignored everyone's suggestions because he thought only his ideas were good.
那个傲慢的人无视所有人的建议，因为他认为只有自己的想法才是好的。

rows.def_en: courage when facing danger or difficulty
rows.mnemonic: bravery 是 brave 勇敢的加上 -ry 后缀，表示勇敢的品质或行为状态。
example: The firefighter showed great bravery when rescuing people from the burning building.
消防员在从燃烧的建筑物中救人时表现出了极大的勇气。

rows.def_en: careful to avoid danger or mistakes
rows.mnemonic: cautious 来自 caution 小心，后缀 -ous 形容词化，表示谨慎或小心的态度，常用于风险防范的场景。
example: Be cautious when crossing the busy street.
过繁忙的马路时要小心。

kaoyan_ex.text: Because employment protection laws make it costlier to fire an employee, employers are more cautious about hiring new staff.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“谨慎的”

rows.def_en: being happy and positive, even when things are hard
rows.mnemonic: cheerfulness 的基础词 cheer 意为高兴，后缀 -ful 和 -ness 使其名词化，描述一种持久的积极情绪状态。
example: Her cheerfulness helped everyone stay positive during the difficult time.

两份报告中的数字存在差异。

区分真实新闻和假新闻可能很难。

这两把钥匙完全相同，可以打开同一把锁。

报告中的信息与我们已知的事实不一致。

温度和加热时间成反比。

她在练习中的一贯性带来了稳步的提高。

words.def_en: opposite or different from something completely opposite in nature or direction doing the opposite of what is asked or expected the opposite thing or fact
words.mnemonic: 前缀 contra- 指反对，-ary 为形容词后缀，因此 contrary 表示相反或对立的态度。日常用语 on the contrary 用于反驳先前观点。

words.def_en: in the opposite way or direction

有些人通过阅读学习，而相反地，另一些人通过实践学习。

区分这两种相似的类型可能很困难。

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“区分”

words.def_en: a difference between things that should match or be the same
words.mnemonic: discrepancy 表示差异或不一致，源于拉丁语 discrepantia，dis- 分离，crepare 发出声音，比喻为不和谐或矛盾。
example: There is a discrepancy between the numbers in the two reports.
两份报告中的数字存在差异。

words.def_en: far away in space or time not similar or close related but not closely not friendly or warm not paying attention; thinking about something else
words.mnemonic: 来自 distance，distance 指距离，后缀 -ant 表示具有性质的，因此意思是遥远的，可以形容空间或情感上的疏远。
example: The distant mountains looked small from our window.
远山从我们的窗户看过去显得很小。

kaoyan_ex.text: The monetary value of the objects on display is a distant second place in importance.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“遥远的”；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: to tell the difference between two things to make someone or something different from others to see or hear something clearly to do something very well and become known for it
words.mnemonic: distinguish 源于拉丁语 distingere，dis- 表示分开，stinguere 意为标记，合起来指通过特征识别差异，帮助区分不同事物。
example: It can be hard to distinguish between real and fake news.
区分真实新闻和假新闻可能很难。

words.def_en: exactly the same in every way exactly the same thing or person
words.mnemonic: identical 拆解为拉丁语 idem 表示相同，加上后缀 ical 构成，指完全一致或没有差异。
example: The two keys are identical and can open the same lock.
这两把钥匙完全相同，可以打开同一把锁。

words.def_en: If something is inconsistent, it doesn't match or agree with something else. If someone's behavior is inconsistent, it doesn't follow a pattern or stay the same. If something is inconsistent, it changes too often and doesn't stay the same.
words.mnemonic: inconsistent 由前缀 in（不）和 consistent（一致）构成，指行为或说法前后矛盾，缺乏统一性。
example: The information in the report was inconsistent with the facts we already knew.
报告中的信息与我们已知的事实不一致。

words.def_en: opposite in amount or position to something else the exact opposite of something
words.mnemonic: inverse 由前缀 in- 不和 verse 转向组成，源自拉丁语 inversus，意为相反的或数学中的倒数关系。

温度和加热时间成反比。

words.def_en: To imitate someone's voice, movements, or behavior, often for amusement. To resemble or function like something else. A person or thing that is capable of imitating.

这位喜剧演员模仿了那位著名演员独特的嗓音。

words.def_en: A large number of things or ideas that are different from each other.

这幅画中色彩的多样性使其脱颖而出。

路上的两条平行线帮助驾驶员保持在车道内。

words.def_en: how much two things are alike but not the same a shared quality that makes things or people alike

这两幅画之间的相似之处表明它们出自同一位艺术家之手。

words.def_en: when two halves or sides of something are the same in size and shape when two things are very similar or equal
words.mnemonic: symmetry 来自希腊语 symmetria，syn- 表示一起，metron 表示测量，描述物体各部分平衡协调的美感。

蝴蝶的翅膀呈现出完美的对称性。

这位艺术家的作品以其独特性而闻名。

words.def_en: in different ways or by different means
words.mnemonic: variously 来自 various（多样的），加副词后缀 -ly，意思是以不同方式地，描述事物在多种形式或解释中存在。

人们对他话语的含义有各种不同的解读。

words.def_en: shows two teams or sides are against each other compares two different ideas or choices

比赛是A队对阵B队。

老师用了一个类比来解释细胞如何工作，把它们比作微型工厂。

words.def_en: based on personal choice or random chance, not reason or rules using power without limits or fairness

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“任意的”；常见搭配 by

碳是生命所必需的，因为它构成了所有有机化合物的基础。

公司首席执行官与合作伙伴公司的同行会面，讨论合并事宜。

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“对应的人”

请把桌子上的书拿来。

words.def_en: made up of things that are all the same or very similar

该混合物是均匀的，意味着所有部分都相同。

words.def_en: related to foreign countries across the sea to or in a foreign country across the sea

该公司正在寻找海外合作伙伴以扩展业务。

蜂蜜的黏性使它粘在勺子上。

rows.mnemonic: blur 可能源自中古英语 blurren，意为弄脏或混淆，词源与视觉模糊相关，常用于描述不清晰的图像或概念。
example: Without my glasses, everything becomes a blur.
不戴眼镜，一切都是一片模糊。

rows.def_en: A yellow metal made from copper and zinc, or things made from it. Metal wind instruments like trumpets, or the people who play them. A decorated brass object, often on a horse's harness. A brass plate in a church to remember someone who died. The top leaders in a company or group. Money.

门把手是黄铜做的，闪闪发亮。

example: We commemorate the heroes who fought for our freedom.
我们纪念为我们的自由而战的英雄们。

rows.def_en: a short written note used in an organization to share information

rows.def_en: A special church leader with duties in a cathedral. A widely accepted rule or standard used to judge something. A collection of works by an author that are considered genuine or important. A type of music where singers or instruments repeat a melody in turns.
rows.mnemonic: canon 源于希腊语 kanon（规则或标准），在宗教中指经典著作，在艺术中表示公认准则，同时与品牌 Canon 相机相关但含义不同。

由于长期服务，他被任命为大教堂的教士。

rows.def_en: A large and important church that is the main church of an area led by a bishop.

我们参观了市中心的美丽大教堂，欣赏其著名的彩色玻璃窗。

rows.def_en: A small building or room for Christian prayer and services, often in schools, prisons, or large homes. rows.mnemonic: chapel 词源是拉丁语 cappella 意为小披风，因历史关联演变为小型教堂。

学生们聚集在学校小教堂进行晨祷。

那位善良的牧师在婚礼上发表了优美的演讲。

rows.def_en: A very popular idea, activity, or way of life. A small group with extreme religious beliefs not part of a major religion. A system of religious beliefs and practices. Very popular with a specific group of people.

words.mnemonic: 来自希腊语 skeletos，指干枯的身体框架，引申为支撑结构的骨架
example: Scientists found a dinosaur skeleton in the rocks.
科学家在岩石中发现了一具恐龙骨架。

words.def_en: a person who watches an event, show, or game
words.mnemonic: spectator 源于拉丁语 spectare 观看，后缀 -or 表示人，意思是观众或旁观者，如体育赛事中的观赛者。
example: The excited spectator cheered loudly when his team scored a goal.
当他的球队进球时，兴奋的观众大声欢呼。

words.def_en: a man who plays sports, often as a job
words.mnemonic: sportsman 直接结合 sport 和 man，sport 指运动，man 是人，所以是运动员，强调公平竞赛精神。
example: The sportsman trains every day to stay at the top of his game.
这位运动员每天训练，以保持最佳状态。

words.def_en: A large place for sports events with seats for many people to watch.
words.mnemonic: stadium 词源是希腊语 stadion，原指古代赛跑场的长度单位，现在演变为大型体育场馆的代名词。
example: The new stadium can hold 50,000 fans for football games.
新体育场可容纳5万名球迷观看足球比赛。

words.def_en: A sports contest where players or teams compete in games, and losers are eliminated until one winner remains. A medieval competition where knights on horseback fought to display bravery and skill.
words.mnemonic: tournament 源自古法语，最初指中世纪骑士比赛，现在泛指各种体育或游戏锦标赛。
example: The tennis tournament had many players competing for the championship title.
这场网球锦标赛有许多选手争夺冠军头衔。

words.def_en: a game where two teams hit a ball over a net without letting it touch the ground on their side
words.mnemonic: volleyball 由 volley 和 ball 组成，volley 意为齐射，ball 是球，表示排球运动，其中球员连续击球。
example: We played volleyball at the beach yesterday and had a lot of fun.
我们昨天在海滩打排球，玩得很开心。

words.def_en: A large area with a flat center and seats around it where people watch sports or shows. A field or area where public activities happen, often with competition or conflict.
words.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 arena，原指沙子，因为古罗马竞技场铺沙吸收血液，arena 现在泛指竞赛或表演场所。
example: The concert at the arena was amazing.
在体育馆举行的音乐会太棒了。

words.def_en: a light, narrow boat moved with a paddle to travel by canoe
words.mnemonic: canoe 直接借自加勒比语，指独木舟，是一种源自原住民的轻便小船。
example: We used a canoe to paddle across the calm lake.
我们用独木舟划过平静的湖面。

words.def_en: a very popular activity or thing that many people like for a short time
words.mnemonic: 可能源自古挪威语 krasa（粉碎），含义演变为短暂狂热或时尚，如流行风潮。
example: The new dance craze quickly became popular among teenagers.
这种新舞蹈热潮很快在青少年中流行起来。

words.def_en: the process of starting and running your own business to make money, often while taking risks.
words.mnemonic: entrepreneurship 来自法语 entreprendre（承担），词根 entre-（之间）和 preneur（拿），描述开创和管理企业的精神，在现代经济中推动创新。
example: Learning about entrepreneurship can help people start their own businesses successfully.
学习创业知识可以帮助人们成功创办自己的企业。

kaoyan_ex.text: The Small Business & Entrepreneurship Council advocacy group said in a statement, “Small businesses and internet entrepreneurs…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“创业”；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: The most important ship out of a group of ships. The most important item or product offered by a company.
words.mnemonic: flagship 原指海军舰队中指挥官的船，现在象征一个组织中最优秀或代表性的部分。
example: The flagship led the other ships across the sea.
旗舰率领其他船只穿越大海。

words.def_en: A hand, head, or face movement that shows meaning. Something you do or say to show a feeling or plan. To move your hands, head, or face to express meaning.
words.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 gestura，词根 gerere（携带或表现）表示身体动作，用于非语言沟通，如手势在文化交流中的重要性。
example: She made a gesture to show she was tired.
她做了个手势表示自己累了。

words.def_en: a long, thin food made from flour and water, often used in soups and stir-fries your head or brain (informal)
words.mnemonic: noodle 源自德语 Nudel，意为面条，中文直接音译为面条，体现食物名称的文化传播。
example: I like to eat chicken noodle soup when I'm sick.
我生病时喜欢喝鸡汤面。

words.def_en: a long pole with a wide flat end used to move a boat through water
words.mnemonic: 源自古英语 ar，指划船用的桨，词源简单，直接关联到水上工具的使用。
example: He used the oar to row the small boat across the lake.
他用桨把小船划过了湖面。

words.def_en: A person who sells things A product that sells well
words.mnemonic: seller 来自 sell（源自古英语 sellan 意为出售）和 er（表示人的后缀），指卖家或销售商品的人。
example: The seller must provide a receipt to the buyer.
卖方必须向买方提供收据。

kaoyan_ex.text: Until now, many sellers that have a physical presence in only a single state or a few states have been able to avoid charging…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“卖家”；后接 that 从句；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: a person who owns or runs a shop
words.mnemonic: shopkeeper 组合 shop 商店和 keeper 看守者，keeper 源于古英语 cepan，描述店主角色。
example: The shopkeeper helped me find what I needed in the store.
店主帮我在店里找到了我需要的东西。

words.def_en: acting or happening naturally without planning
words.mnemonic: spontaneity 来自 spontaneous，词根 sponte 意为自愿，后缀 -ity 表示性质，因此指自然发生、无预先计划的状态，常与即兴艺术相关。
example: Her spontaneity made the party more fun and exciting.
她的即兴发挥让派对更加有趣和刺激。

words.def_en: strong excitement and eagerness for something you care about
words.mnemonic: zeal 来自希腊语 zēlos，原意热情或热忱，常形容对事业或信仰的强烈奉献精神。
example: She worked with great zeal to help the community.
她以极大的热情帮助社区。

rows.def_en: A gray powder that hardens when mixed with water, used in building to stick bricks or stones together. The hard material formed when cement dries. A substance that hardens to stick things together or fill holes. Something that unites people with shared interests. To join things together using cement or glue. To strengthen a relationship or agreement.
rows.mnemonic: cement 源于拉丁语 caementum 意为碎石或粘合剂，与 caedere 切相关，常用于建筑中的固定材料。
example: Mix cement with sand and water to make strong concrete.
将水泥与沙子和水混合，制成坚固的混凝土。

rows.def_en: A flat paper cover for sending letters. A flat plastic cover for holding papers.
rows.mnemonic: 来自法语 enveloppe，词根 en- 表示覆盖， veloppe 源于拉丁语 volvere 意为卷曲，合起来指包裹或覆盖物品的外层，如信件封套。
example: I put the letter in an envelope and mailed it.
我把信放进信封里寄了出去。

rows.def_en: A soft, light material with many small holes, used for seats and mattresses. Many small bubbles on the surface of a liquid. A substance that makes many small bubbles, used for cleaning, shaving, or fighting fires. To make or have many small bubbles.
rows.mnemonic: foam 直接源自古英语 fām，指液体形成的泡沫，如海浪或肥皂泡，体现了自然现象的演变。
example: The foam mattress is very comfortable to sleep on.
泡沫床垫睡起来非常舒服。

kaoyan_ex.text: Unfortunately, the polyurethane foam he used is inherently unstable.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“泡沫材料”

rows.def_en: a small useful tool or device
rows.mnemonic: gadget 起源不明，可能借自法语，指小工具或创新装置，如智能 gadget 在现代科技中无处不在。
example: This clever gadget helps open jars easily.
这个巧妙的小工具可以帮助轻松打开罐子。

rows.def_en: A group of machines, especially large ones The working parts inside a machine The system or way something is organized
rows.mnemonic: machinery 基于拉丁语 machina（机器），后缀 -ery 表示集合或系统，整体指机械装置或复杂机构。
example: The factory uses heavy machinery to make cars
这家工厂使用重型机械制造汽车。

rows.def_en: A set of parts in a machine that work together to do a job. A way or system to make something happen. Parts in a living thing that work together to perform a function.
rows.mnemonic: mechanism 词源可追溯至希腊语 mekhane，意为机器，指机械装置或运作原理，如 defense mechanism 防御机制，常用于科学和工程领域。
example: The clock's mechanism stopped working, so it no longer tells time.
时钟的机芯停止工作了，所以它不再显示时间。

kaoyan_ex.text: However, the mechanisms proposed were unwieldy and the Bill was voted down following the change in government later that year.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“机械装置”

rows.def_en: to close an envelope by sticking its edges together to close a container tightly so nothing can get in or out to make something final and cannot be changed to cover a surface with a protective layer to block a place so no one can pass an official mark on a document to show it is real something that makes an agreement final a material that closes a container tightly a wax or paper mark that must be broken to open something a tool used to make an official mark a sea animal that lives on coasts and eats fish
rows.mnemonic: seal 作为动词或名词，可能来自拉丁语 sigillum（印章），表示密封或盖章，也指动物海豹源于古英语 seolh。
example: Please seal the envelope after putting the letter inside.
请把信放进去后封好信封。

rows.def_en: Made by people, not natural Using word endings to show meaning in sentences A material made by people, not found in nature
rows.mnemonic: synthetic 来自希腊语 synthesis，syn- 前缀表示共同，thesis 意为放置，组合指人造或合成的，如合成纤维或化学材料。
example: This synthetic material feels like real leather but costs less.
这种合成材料摸起来像真皮，但价格更低。

rows.def_en: a machine used in homes for tasks like cooking, cleaning, or heating
rows.mnemonic: appliance 来自 apply 应用和 -ance 名词后缀，apply 源拉丁语 applicare 附着，因此指家用电器等应用工具。
example: Unplug the appliance when you are not using it to save energy.
不使用时拔掉电器插头以节省能源。

rows.def_en: made by people to look or act like something natural created by humans, not occurring naturally not genuine or real
rows.mnemonic: artificial 的词根 art 代表技艺，fic 表示制作，ial 是形容词后缀，整体指人造的或通过技艺制造的，常用于 artificial intelligence 即人工智能领域。
example: Artificial light helps us see when it's dark outside.
人造光帮助我们在外面天黑时看清东西。

kaoyan_ex.text: …celluloid animation stills from Disney films, the first artificial heart.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“人造的”

rows.def_en: A large, semi-aquatic rodent known for building dams, canals, and lodges. The soft, thick fur of the beaver, historically used for making hats. Slang term for a woman's pubic area. to work hard and persistently at something to move or act with energetic determination, often in a busy or industrious manner
rows.mnemonic: beaver 词源是古英语 beofor，指河狸动物，也常用于比喻勤奋工作的人如 eager beaver。
example: The industrious beaver was busily working on its dam.
勤劳的海狸正忙着筑坝。

rows.def_en: A wall built across a river to hold back water for storage or power. A man-made lake where water is stored. The mother of an animal, especially a horse. A small rubber sheet used by dentists to keep a tooth dry. A small rubber sheet used for protection during sex. To build a wall across a river to hold back water.
rows.mnemonic: dam 源于古英语 damm，指人工建造的水坝用于拦截水流，在工程中至关重要。
example: The dam holds back the river water to create a lake.
大坝拦住河水，形成一个人工湖。

rows.def_en: to be very angry but not show it to be crowded with people or animals to move around quickly and violently
rows.mnemonic: seethe 源于古英语 seothan，原意指液体沸腾，后来比喻愤怒时情绪激烈翻滚。
example: He seethed with anger but kept his voice calm.
他气得咬牙切齿，但保持声音平静。

To strengthen a relationship or agreement.

example: He seethed with anger but kept his voice calm.
他气得咬牙切齿，但保持声音平静。

rows.def_en: the formal rules and traditions used in ceremonies
rows.mnemonic: ceremonial 基于 ceremony 这个名词，ceremony 源于拉丁语 caerimonia 表示仪式，后缀 -al 表示属性，整体形容与正式礼节或庆典相关的事物。
example: The wedding followed all the ceremonial traditions of their culture.
婚礼遵循了他们文化中的所有仪式传统。

rows.def_en: what is usual or expected typical or accepted behavior in a group a required or agreed standard to set or adjust to a standard
rows.mnemonic: norm 的词源可追溯至拉丁语 norma 原指木匠的直角尺，后来演变为标准或规范的意思，帮助衡量行为准则。
example: Waking up early is the norm for farmers.
早起是农民的常态。

kaoyan_ex.text: …in which infants are carried in slings, is considered the norm.

rows.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“常规”

rows.def_en: making something normal or standard
rows.mnemonic: normal 源于拉丁语 norma 规则，-ization 后缀表示使成为标准的过程。
example: The normalization of data helps computers process information more efficiently.
数据的标准化有助于计算机更高效地处理信息。

rows.def_en: Used to describe a method in psychology where actions are made stronger or weaker by giving rewards or punishments. Describing a behavior that is learned because it gets a result, like a reward or a punishment.
rows.mnemonic: operant 源于 operate（操作），在心理学中指通过环境操作来改变行为的概念，如斯金纳的操作性条件反射。
example: The teacher used operant conditioning to encourage good behavior by giving out stickers as a reward.
老师使用操作性条件反射，通过发放贴纸作为奖励来鼓励良好行为。

rows.def_en: Permission to let someone act for you. A person who acts for someone else. A substitute for something being measured.
rows.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 procuratio 的缩写，表示代理或替代，常用于计算机中的 proxy server。
example: You can vote either in person or by proxy, which means someone else votes on your behalf.
你可以亲自投票或委托他人代理投票，即由他人代你投票。

rows.def_en: To make things of the same type have the same features or quality. To compare with a standard.
example: The company decided to standardise its procedures across all branches.
公司决定将其程序在所有分支机构标准化。

rows.def_en: to make things the same by following a set pattern or rule
rows.mnemonic: standardize 由 standard 加后缀 -ize 构成，standard 源自古法语 estandart 意为旗帜，-ize 表示使...化，整体指标准化过程，在工业质量控制中广泛应用。
example: The company decided to standardize all its products to ensure consistent quality.
公司决定标准化所有产品，以确保质量一致。

rows.def_en: without any limits or requirements
rows.mnemonic: unconditional 拆解为 un（不）和 conditional（有条件的），意为无限制的支持或爱，如父母对孩子的无私情感。
example: Her parents gave her unconditional love, no matter what happened.
无论发生什么，她的父母都给予她无条件的爱。

rows.def_en: following usual or accepted beliefs and ways following the traditional beliefs and practices of a religion closely related to the Orthodox Church
rows.mnemonic: orthodox 词源是希腊语 orthodoxos，ortho- 指正确或直的，-dox 来自 doxa 意为观点，合起来表示符合传统或正统教义的。
example: His orthodox views on education follow traditional methods.
他对教育的正统观点遵循传统方法。

rows.def_en: A set of actions done the same way each time, often for religious reasons. Something done regularly in the same way. Related to a ceremony or set of actions. Done in the same way each time, often without real feeling.

example: I ate a sweet peach for breakfast.
我早餐吃了一个甜桃子。

words.def_en: having a color that is a shade between purple and another color
words.mnemonic: purplish 由 purple（紫色，源出希腊语 porphura）加后缀 -ish（类似）构成，描述略带紫色的色调，用于颜色形容。

words.def_en: Someone who consumes a specific type of food or does so in a particular manner.
words.mnemonic: eater 简单由 eat 加后缀 -er 构成，表示吃的人或物，比如 big eater 指大胃王，这个词突出了动作的执行者。

他是一个注重健康饮食的人，喜欢沙拉胜过快餐。

kaoyan_ex.text: Elephants are very choosy eaters, but until recently little was known about how they selected their food.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“食者”

words.def_en: A short form of a word or phrase. The act of making something shorter.
words.mnemonic: abbreviation 源自拉丁语 abbreviare，词根 ab-（离开）和 breviare（缩短），指缩略形式如 etc. 或 Dr.。
example: The abbreviation 'Dr.' stands for 'Doctor'.
缩写“Dr.”代表“医生”。

words.def_en: a helper or assistant, especially to someone important like a politician
words.mnemonic: aide 表示助手或副官，直接源自法语，意为帮助，词根与 aid 同源，演变后特指提供支持的辅助人员。
example: The politician's aide helped organize the important meeting
这位政治家的助手协助组织了这次重要会议。

words.def_en: to find out for sure
words.mnemonic: 前缀 a- 表示使动，词根 certain 来自拉丁语 certus（确定的），组合意为通过调查或证据使某事变得明确无误。
example: We need to ascertain the exact time of arrival.
我们需要确定确切的到达时间。

words.def_en: a special vehicle that takes sick or hurt people to the hospital
words.mnemonic: ambulance 来自拉丁语 ambulare（行走），最初指移动医疗单位，现直接指救护车。
example: When someone is badly hurt, call an ambulance to take them to the hospital quickly.
当有人受重伤时，叫救护车尽快送他们去医院。

words.def_en: the act of staying away from something or not doing something
words.mnemonic: avoid 源自古法语 esvuidier，a- 表示离开，void 意为空的，后缀 -ance 表示状态，整体指避免或回避的行为。
example: Avoidance of sugary foods can help maintain good health.

kaoyan_ex.text: …eye contact triggered more activity associated with avoidance, according to the Finnish researcher Jari Hietanen and colleagues.

words.def_en: to feel a dull, ongoing pain to want something very much a dull, ongoing pain in the body
words.mnemonic: 源自古英语 æce，表示持续疼痛，词源独立发展，常与身体不适相关。
example: My head started to ache after staring at the screen all day.
盯着屏幕看了一整天后，我的头开始疼了。

words.def_en: A chemical that can burn things and has a sour taste. A strong illegal drug that makes people see and hear things that are not real. Containing acid or having acid-like properties. Having a sour or sharp taste. Critical and unkind in a sharp way.
words.mnemonic: acid 来自拉丁语 acidus，描述酸味或腐蚀性，在化学中特指酸类物质，演变中保留了其尖锐特性。
example: Lemon juice contains acid that gives it a sour taste.
柠檬汁含有酸，使其带有酸味。

words.def_en: in the middle of or during something, especially something exciting or scary surrounded by something
words.mnemonic: 源自古英语 on middan 意思是在中间，表示位于某事物之中
example: The company failed amid rumors of cheating.
该公司在作弊传闻中倒闭了。

words.def_en: doing something rather than doing nothing trying hard to make something happen having a direct effect or causing change
words.mnemonic: actively 是 active（积极的）的副词形式，表示以主动或积极的方式行动，鼓励参与社会活动。
example: The team is actively working on the project to finish it on time.
团队正在积极致力于该项目，以按时完成。

kaoyan_ex.text: “Many young people assume a great deal of personal responsibility for educating themselves and actively seeking out opposing…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“积极地”

words.def_en: able to change to fit new situations or needs
words.mnemonic: adaptive 由 adapt 加后缀 -ive 构成，adapt 源于拉丁语 adaptare，ad- 表示到，aptare 意为适合，-ive 表示特性，因此指适应的或自适应的，在科技中用于描述系统调整。
example: The adaptive software changes its difficulty based on how well you are doing.
自适应软件会根据你的表现调整难度。

words.def_en: a word that describes a person or thing
words.mnemonic: 这个词源于拉丁语 adjectivus，其中 ad 表示添加，jacere 意思是投掷，因此形容词是添加到名词上的修饰词，用于描述特征。
example: The word 'beautiful' is an adjective that describes how something looks.
单词'beautiful'是一个形容词，用来描述某物的外观。

words.def_en: relating to a relationship where a child is legally taken in by someone who is not their biological parent
words.mnemonic: Adoptive 基于 adopt，ad- 表示向，opt- 表示选择，描述收养关系，如 adoptive parents 指养父母。
example: She considered her adoptive parents as her true family.
她把养父母视为真正的家人。

words.def_en: to manage and run a company, organization, or country to make sure something is done fairly and correctly to give or provide something in a formal way to give medicine or drugs to someone to hit or kick someone or something
words.mnemonic: administer 源于拉丁语 administrare（服务或管理），词根 ad ministrare 意为协助，现指执行任务或给予治疗，如 administer a vaccine（接种疫苗）。

政府将实施新计划以帮助小企业。

words.def_en: friendly and pleasant to be around
words.mnemonic: amiable 形容人友好亲切，源自拉丁语 amicus 意为朋友，演变到描述温和的性格。
example: Her amiable nature made her popular with everyone at school.
她和蔼的性格使她在学校里深受大家欢迎。

words.def_en: the period when a person grows from a child into an adult
words.mnemonic: adolescence 源于拉丁语 adolescere 成长，前缀 ad- 向，词根 olesc 生长，后缀 -ence 表状态，指从儿童期到成年期的发育阶段。

青春期期间，随着儿童成长为成年人，会发生许多变化。

words.def_en: A device that sends or receives radio or TV signals. Taken from above, like from a plane or drone. In the air or above the ground.
words.mnemonic: aerial 词根是 air 空气，后缀 -ial 表示与...相关，指空中的或天线装置。

房子屋顶上装有天线，以便更好地接收电视信号。

words.def_en: not too expensive; easy to buy with the money you have
words.mnemonic: 由 afford（负担得起）加后缀 -able（能够）构成，意思是价格合理易于购买，经济语境常见。

这家店卖的衣服价格实惠、好看又耐穿。

由于高速公路上发生事故，交通延误不可避免。

words.mnemonic: dairy 源自古英语 dey 指挤奶女工，后演变为乳制品相关，如 milk 生产，现指奶制品商店或农场。

医生让我少吃红肉和乳制品。

words.def_en: A small magical creature with wings in stories. An insulting term for a gay man.
words.mnemonic: 来自古法语 faerie，指超自然生物，词源可能与命运女神相关，在童话中常见如格林故事。

仙女赐予了那个善良的孩子三个愿望。

words.def_en: A walkway between rows of seats or shelves.
words.mnemonic: aisle 源于古法语 aile，意为翅膀或侧翼，后指教堂或飞机的过道，词源与空间布局相关，容易联想到通道功能。

咖啡和茶在下一个过道。

服药可以帮助缓解疼痛，让你感觉好一些。

words.def_en: relevant or appropriate to a particular situation or person
words.mnemonic: applicable 源自拉丁语 applicare， ad 表示向， plicare 表示折叠，原意为附着，演变为可应用的或相关的，强调实用性和适配性。

此折扣适用于所有在月底前购买的顾客。

words.def_en: to give a share of something to someone or something
words.mnemonic: allot 表示分配或分派，词根与 lot 份相关，来自古法语 aloter 分配概念。

老师会给每个学生分配十分钟来展示他们的项目。

words.def_en: Relating to or characteristic of autism.
words.mnemonic: 来自 autism 自闭症 和后缀 -ic 形容词化，描述与自闭症谱系相关的特征，用于心理学或医学领域。

我们的儿子患有自闭症，有自己独特的表达方式。

words.def_en: not named or identified made by someone who hides their name plain and not special

example: The anonymous donor gave money without revealing their name.
匿名捐赠者捐了钱，没有透露姓名。

words.def_en: the sound of people clapping to show they like something
words.mnemonic: 源于拉丁语 applaudere，ad- 表示向，plaudere 意为鼓掌，合起来指鼓掌的行为。
example: The crowd showed their approval with loud applause.
人群用响亮的掌声表示赞许。

words.def_en: relating to the study of the movements and positions of celestial bodies and their supposed influence on human affairs
words.mnemonic: 前缀 astro 来自希腊语 astron 指星星，logical 源于 logos 表示逻辑或学科，描述占星术相关，常与星座预测联系。
example: Many people believe in the power of astrological signs to predict personality traits and future events.
许多人相信星座符号能够预测性格特征和未来事件。

words.def_en: on or to the land from water
words.mnemonic: ashore 拆解为前缀 a- 表示在...上 和词根 shore 岸，组合起来意思是在岸上或上岸。
example: After the long voyage, the sailors were happy to go ashore and walk on solid ground.
长途航行后，水手们很高兴能上岸走在坚实的土地上。

words.def_en: to push someone or something roughly to put something somewhere quickly and carelessly a strong, rough push
words.mnemonic: shove 来自古英语 scufan，词源强调用力推挤的动作，常用于物理或比喻性推动。
example: He shoved the door open with his shoulder.
他用肩膀撞开了门。

words.def_en: A device that burns fuel to heat a room. A large appliance for cooking food, with burners on top and an oven inside.
words.mnemonic: stove 源自古英语 stofa，最初指加热装置，现在专指厨房炉灶，是家庭生活的常见设备。
example: We use a wood stove to keep our cabin warm in winter.
冬天我们用柴火炉给小屋取暖。

words.def_en: to make something less intense or severe, especially a feeling or pain
words.mnemonic: assuage 来自拉丁语 assuaviare，其中 ad 表示加强，suavis 意为甜蜜，合起来表示缓解痛苦或使情绪平静，词根拆解有助于记忆其安抚的意味。
example: Her kind words helped to assuage his fears.
她亲切的话语帮助缓解了他的恐惧。

words.def_en: To stop sleeping or to cause someone else to stop sleeping. To cause a feeling or emotion to start being felt.
words.mnemonic: 由 awake 衍生，awake 意为醒来，awaken 表示唤醒或使意识到某事，常用于比喻意义。
example: The loud music at the party awakened her.
派对上响亮的音乐吵醒了她。

words.def_en: to stop sleeping or make someone stop sleeping to make someone remember or feel something again
words.mnemonic: waken 是 wake 的动词形式，源于古英语 wæcnan，表示从睡眠中唤醒或觉醒。
example: The loud noise will waken the baby from her nap.
巨大的噪音会把婴儿从午睡中吵醒。

words.def_en: facing or moving toward the back moving in a way that does not help you make progress not developed as much as others slow to learn toward the back in the opposite direction toward a worse state with the back where the front should be
words.mnemonic: backward 来自 back（后）和 -ward（方向后缀），表示向后的运动或发展落后的状态。
example: He walked backward without looking.
他头也不回地倒着走。

words.def_en: salted or smoked meat from a pig, cut into thin slices
words.mnemonic: bacon 来自古法语，指熏猪肉，中文直接音译为培根，常用于烹饪语境。
example: I cooked bacon for breakfast this morning.
今天早上我做了培根当早餐。

words.def_en: with little or no hair on the head without hair, marks, or covering on a surface plain and direct, without extra details
words.mnemonic: bald 可能源自古英语 beald，意指光秃的或没有覆盖物的，现在主要描述头部无发的状态。
example: He became bald at a young age.
他年纪轻轻就秃顶了。

kaoyan_ex.text: We can offer them a visit to Blackwater National Wildlife Refuge in Dorchester County where bald eagles fly over tidal marshes…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“秃头的”

words.def_en: to be careful and watch out for danger
words.mnemonic: beware 来自中古英语 be warian，其中 ware 意为警惕，整体表示警告或小心注意。
example: Beware of the dog in the yard, it might bite.
小心院子里的狗，它可能会咬人。

words.def_en: speech that is intended to impress but is actually empty and meaningless
words.mnemonic: bombast 最初指棉絮等填充物，后引申为空洞夸张的言辞，源自拉丁语 bombax，在修辞学中常用于批评浮夸的语言风格。
example: The politician's speech was full of bombast, making it hard to understand his actual plan.
这位政客的演讲充满了浮夸之词，让人难以理解他的实际计划。

words.def_en: happening later than expected or usual
words.mnemonic: belated 由 be（使）和 late（晚的）加上 ed 后缀形成，表示迟来的或延误的事物，如祝福。
example: Her belated birthday gift finally arrived after a month.
她迟到的生日礼物终于在一个月后到达了。

words.def_en: about someone's life story related to a person's life
words.mnemonic: biographical 来源于 biography 传记，bio- 根源于生命，graph 意思是书写，后缀 -ical 表示与生平故事相关的。
example: The book gives a biographical account of the famous scientist's life.
这本书对这位著名科学家的生平进行了传记式的叙述。

words.def_en: the sharp, flat part of a tool or machine used for cutting a flat part that spins in an engine or on a helicopter the wide, flat part of an oar that goes in the water a single, thin leaf of grass the flat metal part on the bottom of an ice skate
words.mnemonic: blade 源自古英语 blæd，原意叶子或刀片，现指锋利的物体如剃须刀片或风扇叶片。
example: Always keep the blade of your knife clean and sharp.
始终保持你的刀刃干净锋利。

words.def_en: A cleaning tool with a long handle and bristles for sweeping floors. A wild bush with small yellow flowers.
words.mnemonic: broom 来自古英语 brom，最初指扫帚草，后因用其制作清洁工具而演变为扫帚的意思，与日常家务紧密关联。
example: Use the broom to sweep the floor clean.
用扫帚把地板扫干净。

kaoyan_ex.text: It’s enough to make a person put down the smartphone and go out front with a yard broom.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“扫帚”

words.def_en: to appear as a large, unclear shape, often in a scary way to seem serious and about to happen soon a machine that makes cloth by weaving threads together
words.mnemonic: 作为名词时指织布机，源于古英语；作为动词则意为隐约出现或逼近，常带威胁感。
example: A dark shape loomed ahead of us in the fog.
一个黑色的形状在雾中隐约出现在我们前方。

words.kaoyan_note: 作vi.；意为“隐约出现”

words.def_en: the area of the face above the eyes and below the hairline the line of hair above each eye the top edge of a hill or slope
words.mnemonic: 来自古英语 bru，最初指眉毛或额头，后引申为任何事物的边缘或顶部，例如山坡的 brow 表示山脊。
example: She wiped sweat from her brow after working hard.
她辛苦工作后擦去额头上的汗水。

words.def_en: the long tube in your body where food goes after the stomach, especially the part where waste is stored before leaving the body the deepest or innermost part of something
words.mnemonic: bowel 来自拉丁语 botellus（小香肠），演变为指人体肠道内脏，常用于医学描述。
example: Eating more fiber can help keep your bowel movements regular.
摄入更多纤维有助于保持排便规律。

kaoyan_ex.text: Five years ago, at summer’s end, Andrew Fusek Peters was diagnosed with bowel cancer.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“肠”

words.def_en: a woman getting married or recently married
words.mnemonic: bride 一词来自古英语 bryd，指新娘，在婚礼文化中常与 groom（新郎）成对出现，体现了传统婚庆习俗。
example: The bride looked beautiful in her white dress.
新娘穿着白色连衣裙，看起来很漂亮。

words.def_en: A person who happens to be walking past a particular place.
words.mnemonic: passer-by 指偶然经过的路人，由 passer 经过者和 by 在旁边复合而成，描述短暂出现在某处的人。
example: The passer-by saw the dog running in the park.
路人看到那只狗在公园里跑。

words.def_en: A sea animal with a hard shell, eight legs, and two claws. Crabs walk sideways. The meat from a crab that people eat. An itchy condition caused by tiny insects in pubic hair.
words.mnemonic: crab 源于古英语 crabba，描述有钳的甲壳动物，在星座中代表巨蟹座，引申含义包括横行或抱怨的行为，体现了词义的演变。
example: We saw a crab crawling sideways on the beach.
我们看到一只螃蟹在海滩上横着爬行。

kaoyan_ex.text: Pennsylvania farmers, to use one telling example, aren’t thinking about next year’s blue crab harvest in Maryland when they…

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“螃蟹”；常见搭配 in

words.def_en: A tall machine with a long arm used to lift heavy things. A large bird with long legs and a long neck. To stretch your neck to see something better.
words.mnemonic: crane 古英语 cran 指鹤鸟，因长颈形似引申为起重机；作为动词意为伸长，常用于描述身体或机械动作。
example: The construction crew used a crane to lift the steel beams into place.
施工队用起重机将钢梁吊装到位。

words.def_en: how much a container or space can hold the ability to do or understand something a person's official role or job how much a factory or machine can make the size or power of an engine or machine
words.mnemonic: capacity 源于拉丁语 capacitas，词根 capax 意为容纳，指物体或人的承载能力或容量，引申为潜力或角色。
example: The stadium was filled to its full capacity with excited fans.
体育场座无虚席，挤满了兴奋的球迷。

kaoyan_ex.text: “For consciousness to evolve, a brain with a threshold level of complexity and capacity is required,” he added .

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“容量”

words.def_en: to cut shapes from wood, stone, or other hard materials to cut words or designs into a surface to cut cooked meat into slices to create a successful career through hard work
words.mnemonic: carve 意为雕刻，源于古英语 ceorfan，表示用刀具切割材料以形成形状。
example: He learned to carve animals from wood.
他学会了用木头雕刻动物。

kaoyan_ex.text: …line due to roads, train tracks, and other paths people carve through the woods.

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“雕刻”

words.def_en: An underground room used for storage An underground room for storing wine, or the wine kept there
words.mnemonic: cellar 的词根是拉丁语 cellarium，与 cell 小房间相关，指地下的储藏室或酒窖
example: We store our food in the cellar to keep it cool.
我们把食物存放在地窖里以保持凉爽。

words.def_en: lasting a long time and hard to cure having an illness for a long time lasting a long time and hard to fix very bad
words.mnemonic: 源于希腊语 khronikos，khronos 表示时间，后缀 -ic 构成形容词，意为与时间相关的，特指长期持续的；医学上 chronic 用于描述慢性疾病。
example: Chronic pain can affect daily life for many years.
慢性疼痛可能影响日常生活多年。

words.def_en: the bottom part of your face, below your mouth
words.mnemonic: chin 直接来自古英语 cin，指人类面部下方的突出部位，即下巴。
example: He rested his chin on his hand while thinking.
他思考时用手托着下巴。

words.def_en: A type of fine white clay used to make dishes. Dishes and cups made from this special clay.
words.mnemonic: china 指瓷器，源于中国（China）的出口贸易历史，其中 China 一词源自波斯语 Cin。这个词直接关联中国陶瓷文化，帮助记忆其作为物品的含义。
example: The beautiful china plate from China was very delicate.
来自中国的精美瓷器盘子非常易碎。

kaoyan_ex.text: Caravanserais were roadside inns that were built along the Silk Road in areas including China, North Africa and the Middle East.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“瓷器粘土”

words.def_en: a strong illegal drug that can make people feel very excited but is also very addictive a hard black fuel made from coal that is burned for heat
words.mnemonic: coke 可指焦炭，源自煤炭干馏；也常作为 Coca-Cola 的简称，这种饮料在全球广受欢迎。
example: He was caught with coke in his pocket during the police search.
警方搜查时发现他口袋里装有可卡因。

words.def_en: to hold or fasten things together tightly with a tool to hold something very tightly so it doesn't move to put a device on a car wheel to prevent driving a tool that holds things together tightly a device attached to a car wheel to prevent driving
words.mnemonic: 单词 clamp 源于古日耳曼语 klamp 表示夹紧工具，拆解为固定物体的装置，常用于机械或木工中固定部件
example: Clamp the wood to the table to keep it steady.
把木头夹在桌子上以保持稳定。

words.def_en: A clove is a dried flower bud from a tropical tree. It is used as a spice in cooking, especially in sweet dishes. It looks like a small nail. A clove is one of the small sections that make up a garlic bulb. To pierce or fasten something with a clove or a nail.
words.mnemonic: clove 有两种常见意思：蒜瓣源于古英语 clufu 表示分裂，因为蒜头自然分瓣；丁香则来自法语 clou 意思是钉子，因其形状类似小钉子，常用于烹饪和香料。
example: Clove is a common ingredient in gingerbread cookies.
丁香是姜饼曲奇中常见的配料。

words.def_en: when different things or people exist together at the same time
words.mnemonic: coexistence 前缀 co 表示共同，加上 existence 存在， existence 来自拉丁语 existere，意思是不同群体或事物和平共处
example: The peaceful coexistence of different cultures makes our community strong.
不同文化的和平共处使我们的社区变得强大。

words.def_en: related to thinking and understanding
words.mnemonic: cognitive 源自拉丁语 cognoscere 意思是知道，涉及认识过程，作为 AI 领域的关键词，它与 cognitive computing 相关，辅助理解思维机制。
example: Cognitive skills help us learn, remember, and solve problems.
认知技能帮助我们学习、记忆和解决问题。

kaoyan_ex.text: Their well-developed hippocampal structures may enable elephants, like rats and people, to construct cognitive maps.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“认知的”

words.def_en: Someone you trust and share your secrets and private thoughts with.
words.mnemonic: 词根 con- 表示共同 fid- 源自拉丁语 fidere 意思是信任 组合起来指互相信任的知己 常用于亲密朋友
example: I consider my sister my closest confidant because I can tell her anything.
我把姐姐视为最亲密的知己，因为我可以对她无话不谈。

words.def_en: done by people working together as a team
words.mnemonic: collaborative 派生自拉丁语 collaborare，com- 表示 '一起'，laborare 表示 '工作'，强调多人共同参与的协作性质。
example: The collaborative effort of the team led to a successful project completion.
团队的协作努力使项目成功完成。

kaoyan_ex.text: AI can be a collaborative tool in a wide range of creative endeavors.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“协作的”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: Working together with others to achieve a goal.
words.mnemonic: collaboratively 拆解为 co- 一起、labor 工作和 -atively 副词后缀，labor 来自拉丁语 laborare，强调团队合作的方式。
example: The team designed the project collaboratively, making sure everyone's ideas were considered.
团队协作设计了该项目，确保每个人的想法都得到考虑。

words.def_en: a high-ranking officer in the army, marines, or air force
words.mnemonic: 源于意大利语 colonello 指军队纵队，英语中发音受法语 coronel 影响演变为 kernel，现表示上校军衔
example: The colonel led his troops into battle with great courage.
上校以极大的勇气带领部队投入战斗。

words.def_en: to gather things together to make a list, book, or report to change computer code into a form the computer can understand
words.mnemonic: Compile 源自拉丁语 compilare，由 com- 一起和 pilare 掠夺组成，原意是收集，后来在计算机领域指编译代码。
example: We need to compile a list of all the items we have in stock.
我们需要整理一份库存所有物品的清单。

kaoyan_ex.text: In 2022, Swetnam and other scientists teamed up to compile a database of fire-scarred trees from across the continent.

words.kaoyan_note: 作v.；意为“汇编”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: a member of the same communist or socialist group a friend or fellow worker, especially in the military
words.mnemonic: 源自西班牙语 camarada，指同住一室的同伴，引申为同志或战友。在历史语境中，comrade 常用于革命或军事组织。
example: Let's work together for our cause, comrade.
同志，让我们为共同的事业而奋斗。

words.def_en: to move from different places and meet at one point to come together and meet at a point to become similar or the same
words.mnemonic: converge 前缀 con- 表示一起，词根 verge 来自拉丁语 vergere 意为倾向，整体指多条线或观点汇聚到一点，如数学中的收敛。
example: The rivers converge into one big stream.
这些河流汇成一条大河。

words.def_en: done on purpose
words.mnemonic: intentional 源自拉丁语 intentio，词根 tend-（伸展）表达目的性，后缀 -al 使其成为形容词，指有意识的行为。
example: The damage was intentional, not an accident.
损坏是故意的，不是意外。

kaoyan_ex.text: At the time of creation, no attempts were made at intentional preservation, yet analog materials have a chance of surviving…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“故意的”

words.def_en: done on purpose
words.mnemonic: intentionally 由 intention（意图）和后缀 -ally（表示方式）组成，指故意或有目的地行动，在行为分析中常见。
example: She intentionally left the door open to let the fresh air in.
她故意把门开着，让新鲜空气进来。

kaoyan_ex.text: These fires were carefully planned and intentionally ignited during periods when weather kept the blazes easy to control, and…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“故意地”

words.def_en: happening one after another without a break
words.mnemonic: 源自拉丁语 consecutus，其中 con- 表示一起，secutus 来自 sequi 意为跟随，合起来指事件或事物一个接一个连续发生，体现了顺序性。
example: The team won five consecutive games without losing any.
该队连续赢了五场比赛，一场未输。

words.def_en: as a result of something that happened before
words.mnemonic: consequently 来自 consequent（结果），基于拉丁语 consequi（跟随），表示因此或作为逻辑结论发生。
example: He forgot to set his alarm, and consequently he was late for work.
他忘了设闹钟，结果上班迟到了。

kaoyan_ex.text: Consequently—and paradoxically—laws introduced to protect the jobs of ordinary workers may be placing those jobs at risk.

words.kaoyan_note: 作adv.；意为“因此”

words.def_en: a person or company hired to do specific work for another company
words.mnemonic: contractor 基于 contract 合同，词源是拉丁语 contrahere 意为一起拉紧达成协议，因此指签约方如建筑承包商。
example: The company hired a contractor to build their new office.
公司雇佣了一位承包商来建造他们的新办公室。

words.def_en: a person who lacks courage and is easily frightened
words.mnemonic: coward 的词源是古法语 coart 本义为尾巴，引申为逃跑者，形象地描绘了懦弱行为如动物夹尾而逃。
example: He called me a coward because I was too scared to jump off the high diving board.
他叫我懦夫，因为我太害怕而不敢从高跳板上跳下去。

words.def_en: the last day or time when you can do something
words.mnemonic: deadline 据说起源于美国内战监狱，指一条越过即被枪击的线，现在广泛用于表示项目或任务的截止日期。
example: I have to finish my work before the deadline tomorrow.
我必须在明天截止日期前完成我的工作。

words.def_en: a period of ten years
words.mnemonic: 词根为希腊语 dekas，意为十，decade 指十年周期，如历史中的 roaring twenties 就是一个 decade
example: The last decade has seen many changes in technology.
过去十年见证了技术的许多变化。

kaoyan_ex.text: …chemist who, until retiring a few years ago, worked for decades at the Cultural Heritage Agency of the Netherlands (RCE).

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“十年”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: A false belief that you strongly believe is true The act of believing something that is not true
words.mnemonic: delusion 的词源是拉丁语 deludere，其中 de- 表示完全 ludere 表示欺骗，整体指一种顽固的错误信念或幻觉，常用于心理学讨论。
example: His delusion made him think he was a famous king from the past
他的妄想让他以为自己是从前的一位著名国王。

words.def_en: to use up or reduce something until very little remains
words.mnemonic: deplete 源自拉丁语 deplere，de- 表示减少，plere 意为填满，整体指资源耗尽。
example: The long drought will deplete the water supply in the reservoir.
长期的干旱将耗尽水库的供水。

words.def_en: to subtract an amount from a total
words.mnemonic: deduct 源于拉丁语 deducere，本义是引导出，现在常用于扣除款项或减除。
example: The teacher will deduct points for incorrect answers.
老师会因错误答案扣分。

words.def_en: A person who is accused of a crime in court or being sued by someone else.
words.mnemonic: defendant 源于 defend 辩护，后缀 -ant 表示人，指在法庭上辩护的被告。
example: The defendant pleaded not guilty to the charges in court.
被告在法庭上对指控表示不认罪。

words.def_en: to stop someone from doing something by making them think about the bad things that might happen
words.mnemonic: 来自拉丁语 deterrere，de-（远离）和 terrere（恐吓），本义是威慑或阻止，在安全策略中如 deter crime 指预防犯罪。
example: The high cost of parking may deter people from driving to the city center.
高昂的停车费可能会阻止人们开车到市中心。

words.def_en: how well something works in producing a desired effect
words.mnemonic: efficacy 来自拉丁语 efficacia，由 ex（出）和 facere（做）构成，意为产生预期效果的能力，在医学中常指药效。
example: Researchers are studying the efficacy of the new drug to ensure it is both safe and effective.
研究人员正在研究新药的疗效，以确保其既安全又有效。

kaoyan_ex.text: But demonstrating the efficacy of science will be crucial if we are to solve humanity’s greatest challenges.

words.kaoyan_note: 作n.；意为“功效”；常见搭配 of

words.def_en: When someone or something damages or destroys someone else's property or things.
words.mnemonic: Depredation 来自拉丁语 depraedari，其中 de- 前缀表示完全，praedari 意为掠夺，因此指大规模的破坏或抢劫行为，常用于生态或历史讨论。
example: The small town was struggling to recover from the depredation caused by the severe storm.
这个小镇正在努力从暴风雨造成的破坏中恢复过来。

words.def_en: to be a sign of something to mean something
words.mnemonic: de 表示向下或强调，note 源于标记，denote 在逻辑或数学中常用来指示符号的含义。
example: A red traffic light denotes that you must stop your vehicle.
红色交通灯表示你必须停车。

words.def_en: an image seen in a mirror or shiny surface
words.mnemonic: reflexion 是 reflection 的变体拼写，源自拉丁语 reflectere，其中 re- 表示回，flectere 意为弯曲，整体指光线或思想的反射过程，在英式英语中更常见。
example: She admired her own reflexion in the mirror.
她欣赏自己在镜子中的倒影。

words.def_en: the process of sharing resources or wealth in a new way
words.mnemonic: redistribution 由 re 和 distribution 组成，re 表示重新，整体指财富或资源的再分配，在经济政策中常见。
example: The government proposed a plan for the redistribution of wealth to reduce economic inequality.
政府提出了一项财富再分配计划，以减少经济不平等。

words.def_en: unhappiness or dissatisfaction with a situation
words.mnemonic: Discontent 由前缀 dis-（否定）和 content（满意）组成，表达不满情绪，词源反映了人类情感的演变。
example: The workers' discontent grew as their demands were ignored.
工人们的要求被忽视，他们的不满情绪日益增长。

words.def_en: the feeling of not liking or agreeing with something because you think it is wrong or bad
words.mnemonic: disapproval 由前缀 dis-（否定）和 approval（赞成）组成，表达不认可或反对的态度。
example: She showed her disapproval by frowning at the rude behavior.
她通过皱眉表示对粗鲁行为的不满。

words.def_en: to try to stop someone from doing something by making it hard or showing you don't like it to make someone feel less sure or excited about doing something
words.mnemonic: discourage 前缀 dis 表示否定，加上 courage，意思是打击信心或劝阻行动。
example: His parents tried to discourage him from becoming an actor because they thought it was too difficult.
他的父母试图劝阻他成为演员，因为他们认为这太难了。

words.def_en: to spread out or move away in different directions to spread something over a wide area
words.mnemonic: disperse 词根 dis 分开和 perse 撒播来自拉丁语 dispergere，意为使事物分散或传播开
example: The police asked the crowd to disperse after the event ended.
活动结束后，警方要求人群散去。

words.def_en: A woman who has a secret romantic and sexual relationship with a married man. A female teacher, especially in a private school. The female head of a household who employed servants. A woman who owns a pet animal. A woman who has great skill or control over something.
words.mnemonic: mistress 是 master 的女性对应词，源自古法语 maistresse，表示女主人或有权威的女性。
example: He kept his mistress in a separate apartment to hide the affair from his wife.
他把情妇安置在另一套公寓里，以向妻子隐瞒这段婚外情。

words.def_en: in a very extreme way that causes big and sudden changes
words.mnemonic: drastically 由 drastic（激烈的）加后缀 -ally 构成，drastic 来自希腊语 drastikos（有效的），因此意思是剧烈或彻底地改变。
example: The company had to drastically cut costs to survive the financial crisis.
公司不得不大幅削减成本以度过金融危机。

words.def_en: not awake or active now, but can wake up or become active later
words.mnemonic: dormant 来自法语，源于拉丁语 dormire 睡觉，意思是休眠的或不活动的，常用于描述火山或账户。
example: The bear remains dormant throughout the winter, sleeping in its den.
熊在整个冬天都处于休眠状态，在洞穴里睡觉。

kaoyan_ex.text: At issue is the TMT’s planned location on Mauna Kea, a dormant volcano worshiped by some Hawaiians as the piko, that connects…

words.kaoyan_note: 作adj.；意为“休眠的”；常见搭配 by

words.def_en: to remove something completely to remove writing or marks by rubbing to delete recorded information
words.mnemonic: erase 源于拉丁语 erasus，e 表示除去而 radere 意为刮擦，指清除痕迹，文具中 eraser 是常见的擦除工具。
example: You can erase your mistakes with a good eraser.
你可以用一块好橡皮擦掉你的错误。

words.def_en: A contract to use property or equipment for a set time by paying rent. To rent property or equipment to someone for a period of time.
words.mnemonic: lease 词源可追溯至古法语 lesser，意思是出租或租赁，现在用于表示租约协议，常见于房地产或设备租用。
example: The lease allows you to use the apartment for one year if you pay monthly rent.
租约允许你按月支付租金，使用该公寓一年。

words.def_en: When something doesn't work well or achieve the desired outcome.
words.mnemonic: ineffectiveness 由 in- 否定前缀和 effectiveness 构成，指缺乏效果的状态，词根来自拉丁语 effectus 表示结果。
example: The doctor was concerned about the ineffectiveness of the treatment.
医生担心治疗无效。

words.def_en: to get information or a reaction from someone
words.mnemonic: elicit 来自拉丁语 elicere，结合 e-（出）和 lacere（引诱），表示从他人引出信息或反应。

老师试图从安静的学生那里引出答案。
